4.0.m: Description of the Arrival of Vyāsa

4.1.s:
.. .. śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ..
.. śrīsarasvatyai namaḥ .. ..
oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya .. ..
kalyāṇāni dadātu vo gaṇapatiryasminnatuṣṭe sati kṣodīyasyapi karmaṇi prabhavituṃ brahmāpi jihmāyate ..
bheje yaccaraṇāravindamasakṛtsaubhāgyabhāgyodayaistenaiṣā jagati prasiddhimagamaddevendralakṣmī rapi .. 1 ..
4.1.d:
॥ ॥ श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
॥ श्रीसरस्वत्यै नमः ॥ ॥
ओं नमो भगवते वासुदेवाय ॥ ॥
कल्याणानि ददातु वो गणपतिर्यस्मिन्नतुष्टे सति क्षोदीयस्यपि कर्मणि प्रभवितुं ब्रह्मापि जिह्मायते ॥
भेजे यच्चरणारविन्दमसकृत्सौभाग्यभाग्योदयैस्तेनैषा जगति प्रसिद्धिमगमद्देवेन्द्रलक्ष्मी रपि ॥ 1 ॥
4.1.m: Om, homage to holy Gaṇeśa. / Homage to holy Sarasvatī. / Om, homage to the Blessed Lord Vāsudeva. / May the Lord of Ganas bestow blessings upon you, / without whose satisfaction even Brahmā becomes powerless to succeed even in the slightest undertaking; / because the fortune of the King of the Gods repeatedly resorted to his lotus feet / with the arising of her good fortune and merit, she became renowned throughout the world. 1.

4.1.s:
śaśvatpuṇyahiraṇyagarbharasanāsiṃhāsanādhyāsinī seyaṃ vāgadhidevatā vitaratu śreyāṃsi bhūyāṃsi vaḥ ..
yatpādāmalakomalāṃgulinakha jyotsnābhirudvellitaḥ śabdabrahmasudhāṃbudhirbudhamanasyucchraṃkhalaṃ khelati .. 2 ..
4.1.d:
शश्वत्पुण्यहिरण्यगर्भरसनासिंहासनाध्यासिनी सेयं वागधिदेवता वितरतु श्रेयांसि भूयांसि वः ॥
यत्पादामलकोमलांगुलिनख ज्योत्स्नाभिरुद्वेल्लितः शब्दब्रह्मसुधांबुधिर्बुधमनस्युच्छ्रंखलं खेलति ॥ 2 ॥
4.1.m: May that presiding deity of speech grant you abundant blessings, / who ever occupies the throne of the tongue of the holy Hiraṇyagarbha, / stirred by the moonbeams of the pure, tender nails on whose lotus feet, / the ocean of nectar of the Word-Brahman sports unrestrained in the minds of the wise. 2.

4.1.s:
namastasmai viśvodayavilayarakṣāprakṛtaye śivāya kleśaughacchidurapad padmapraṇataye ..
amandasvacchandaprathitapṛthulīlātanubhṛte trivedīvācāmapyapathanijatattvasthitikṛte .. 3 ..
4.1.d:
नमस्तस्मै विश्वोदयविलयरक्षाप्रकृतये शिवाय क्लेशौघच्छिदुरपद् पद्मप्रणतये ॥
अमन्दस्वच्छन्दप्रथितपृथुलीलातनुभृते त्रिवेदीवाचामप्यपथनिजतत्त्वस्थितिकृते ॥ 3 ॥
4.1.m: Homage to him, the origin of the emergence, dissolution, and protection of the universe, / to Śiva, homage to whose lotus feet cuts through the multitude of afflictions, / who bears an immense body of sport manifested by uninterrupted free will, / and whose own true nature abides beyond the reach even of the words of the three Vedas. 3.

4.1.s:
yasya gaṇḍatale bhāti vimalā ṣaṭpa dāvalī ..
akṣamāleva vimalā sa naḥ pāyādgaṇādhipaḥ .. 4 ..
4.1.d:
यस्य गण्डतले भाति विमला षट्प दावली ॥
अक्षमालेव विमला स नः पायाद्गणाधिपः ॥ 4 ॥
4.1.m: Upon whose temple shines a pure swarm of six-footed bees / like a spotless rosary—may that Lord of Gaṇas protect us. 4.

4.1.s:
oṃ namo vāsudevāya saśārṅgāya saketave ..
sagadāya sacakrāya saśaṃkhāya namo namaḥ .. 5 ..
4.1.d:
ओं नमो वासुदेवाय सशार्ङ्गाय सकेतवे ॥
सगदाय सचक्राय सशंखाय नमो नमः ॥ 5 ॥
4.1.m: Om, homage to Vāsudeva, who holds the Śārṅga bow and bears his banner; / to him who holds the mace, the discus, and the conch, homage, homage. 5.

4.1.s:
namaḥ śivāya somāya sagaṇāya sasūnave ..
savṛṣāya saśūlāya sakapālāya sendave .. 6 ..
4.1.d:
नमः शिवाय सोमाय सगणाय ससूनवे ॥
सवृषाय सशूलाय सकपालाय सेन्दवे ॥ 6 ॥
4.1.m: Homage to Śiva, accompanied by Umā, attended by his retinue, with his son, / accompanied by the bull, bearing the trident, with the skull, and bearing the crescent moon. 6.

4.1.s:
śivaṃ dhyātvā hariṃ stutvā praṇamya parame ṣṭhinam ..
citrabhānuṃ ca bhānuṃ ca natvā granthamudīrayet .. 7 ..
4.1.d:
शिवं ध्यात्वा हरिं स्तुत्वा प्रणम्य परमे ष्ठिनम् ॥
चित्रभानुं च भानुं च नत्वा ग्रन्थमुदीरयेत् ॥ 7 ॥
4.1.m: Having meditated upon Śiva, praised Hari, and bowed to Parameṣṭhin, / and having bowed to Citrabhānu and the sun, one should recite the text.

4.1.s:
chatrābhiṣiktaṃ dharmajñaṃ dharmaputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram ..
draṣṭumabhyāgatā hṛṣṭā vyāsādyāḥ parama rṣayaḥ .. 8 ..
4.1.d:
छत्राभिषिक्तं धर्मज्ञं धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम् ॥
द्रष्टुमभ्यागता हृष्टा व्यासाद्याः परम र्षयः ॥ 8 ॥
4.1.m: Delighted supreme sages headed by Vyāsa arrived to see Yudhiṣṭhira, / the son of Dharma, who knows dharma and was consecrated under the royal parasol.

4.1.s:
mārkaṇḍeyaḥ samāṇḍavyaḥ śāṇḍilyaḥ śākaṭāyanaḥ ..
gautamo gālavo gārgyaḥ śātātapaparāśarau .. 9 ..
4.1.d:
मार्कण्डेयः समाण्डव्यः शाण्डिल्यः शाकटायनः ॥
गौतमो गालवो गार्ग्यः शातातपपराशरौ ॥ 9 ॥
4.1.m: Mārkaṇḍeya, Māṇḍavya, Śāṇḍilya, Śākaṭāyana, / Gautama, Gālava, Gārgya, Śātātapa, and Parāśara;

4.1.s:
jāmadagnyo bharadvājo bhṛgu rbhāgurireva ca ..
uttaṃkaḥ śaṃkhalikhitau śaunakaḥ śākaṭāyaniḥ .. 4.1.10 ..
4.1.d:
जामदग्न्यो भरद्वाजो भृगु र्भागुरिरेव च ॥
उत्तंकः शंखलिखितौ शौनकः शाकटायनिः ॥ 4.1.10 ॥
4.1.m: Jāmadagnya, Bharadvāja, Bhṛgu, and Bhāguri, / Uttaṅka, Śaṅkha and Likhita, Śaunaka, and Śākaṭāyani;

4.1.s:
pulastyaḥ pulaho dālbhyo bṛhadaśvaḥ salomaśaḥ ..
nāradaḥ parvato jahurapāva suparāvasū .. 11 ..
4.1.d:
पुलस्त्यः पुलहो दाल्भ्यो बृहदश्वः सलोमशः ॥
नारदः पर्वतो जहुरपाव सुपरावसू ॥ 11 ॥
4.1.m: Pulastya, Pulaha, Dālbhya, Bṛhadaśva, together with Lomaśa, / Nārada, Parvata, Jahnu, and Apāvasu and Parāvasu.

4.1.s:
tānṛṣīnāgatāndṛṣṭvā vedavedāṅgapāragān ..
bhaktimānbhrātṛbhiḥ sārddhaṃ kṛṣṇadhaumyapuraḥsaraḥ .. 12 ..
4.1.d:
तानृषीनागतान्दृष्ट्वा वेदवेदाङ्गपारगान् ॥
भक्तिमान्भ्रातृभिः सार्द्धं कृष्णधौम्यपुरःसरः ॥ 12 ॥
4.1.m: Seeing those sages arrived who had crossed to the further shore of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, / the devout [king], together with his brothers, preceded by Kṛṣṇa and Dhaumya,

4.1.s:
yudhiṣṭhiraḥ saṃprahṛṣṭaḥ samutthāyābhivādya ca ..
arghyamācamanaṃ pādyamāsanāni svayaṃ dadau .. 13 ..
4.1.d:
युधिष्ठिरः संप्रहृष्टः समुत्थायाभिवाद्य च ॥
अर्घ्यमाचमनं पाद्यमासनानि स्वयं ददौ ॥ 13 ॥
4.1.m: Yudhiṣṭhira, overjoyed, stood up, greeted them, / and himself offered guest-water, water for sipping, foot-washing water, and seats.

4.1.s:
upaviṣṭeṣu teṣveva tapasviṣu yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ..
vinayāvanato bhūtvā vyāsaṃ vacanamabravīt .. 14 ..
4.1.d:
उपविष्टेषु तेष्वेव तपस्विषु युधिष्ठिरः ॥
विनयावनतो भूत्वा व्यासं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 14 ॥
4.1.m: When those ascetics were seated, Yudhiṣṭhira, / bowing low with humility, spoke these words to Vyāsa:

4.1.s:
bhagavaṃstvatprasādena prāptaṃ rājyaṃ mahanmayā ..
vikramya nihataḥ saṃkhye sānubandhaḥ suyodhanaḥ .. 15 ..
4.1.d:
भगवंस्त्वत्प्रसादेन प्राप्तं राज्यं महन्मया ॥
विक्रम्य निहतः संख्ये सानुबन्धः सुयोधनः ॥ 15 ॥
4.1.m: "O venerable one, by your grace this great kingdom was obtained by me; / advancing with valour in battle, Suyodhana was slain along with his followers.

4.1.s:
sarogasya yathā bhogaḥ prāpto'pi na sukhāvahaḥ ..
hatvā jñātīṃstathā rājyaṃ na sukhaṃ pratibhāti me .. 16 ..
4.1.d:
सरोगस्य यथा भोगः प्राप्तोऽपि न सुखावहः ॥
हत्वा ज्ञातींस्तथा राज्यं न सुखं प्रतिभाति मे ॥ 16 ॥
4.1.m: Just as enjoyment, even when obtained, brings no pleasure to a diseased man, / likewise, having slain my kinsmen, the kingdom appears to bring me no pleasure.

4.1.s:
yatsukhaṃ pāvanaṃ prītirvanamūlaphalāśinām ..
prāpya gāṃ ca hatārātiṃ na tadasti pitāmaha .. 17 ..
4.1.d:
यत्सुखं पावनं प्रीतिर्वनमूलफलाशिनाम् ॥
प्राप्य गां च हतारातिं न तदस्ति पितामह ॥ 17 ॥
4.1.m: The pure joy and delight of those who subsist on forest roots and fruits / does not belong to me, O grandfather, even after obtaining the earth with its enemies slain.

4.1.s:
yo no bandhurgururgoptā sadā śarma ca varma ca ..
sa mayā rājyalobhena bhīṣmaḥ pāpena ghātitaḥ .. 18 ..
4.1.d:
यो नो बन्धुर्गुरुर्गोप्ता सदा शर्म च वर्म च ॥
स मया राज्यलोभेन भीष्मः पापेन घातितः ॥ 18 ॥
4.1.m: He who was our kinsman, elder, protector, and ever our comfort and armour— / that Bhīṣma was caused to be slain by me, a sinner, out of greed for the kingdom.

4.1.s:
avivekamahaṃ dhāsye mano me pāpapaṅkilam ..
kṣālayitvā tava girā bahudarśitavāriṇā .. 19 ..
4.1.d:
अविवेकमहं धास्ये मनो मे पापपङ्किलम् ॥
क्षालयित्वा तव गिरा बहुदर्शितवारिणा ॥ 19 ॥
4.1.m: I shall place my mind, muddy with sin, having washed away / its lack of discernment with your speech, which is water revealing much.

4.1.s:
saṃśrutāni purāṇāni vedāssāṃgā mayā vibho ..
mamādya dharmasarvasvaṃ prajñādīpena darśaya .. 4.1.20 ..
4.1.d:
संश्रुतानि पुराणानि वेदास्सांगा मया विभो ॥
ममाद्य धर्मसर्वस्वं प्रज्ञादीपेन दर्शय ॥ 4.1.20 ॥
4.1.m: The Purāṇas and the Vedas with their auxiliary limbs have been heard by me, O lord; / show me today the essence of all dharma with the lamp of wisdom.

4.1.s:
ete sadharmagoptāro munayaḥ samupāgatāḥ ..
pibato netrabhramarairbhavato mukhapaṃkajam ..21..
4.1.d:
एते सधर्मगोप्तारो मुनयः समुपागताः ॥
पिबतो नेत्रभ्रमरैर्भवतो मुखपंकजम् ॥21॥
4.1.m: These sages, protectors of dharma, have assembled, / drinking in your lotus face with the bees of their eyes.

4.1.s:
arthaśāstrāṇi yāvaṃti dharmaśāstrāṇi yāni vai ..
śrutāni sarvaśāstrāṇi bhīṣmādbhāgīrathīsutāt .. 22 ..
4.1.d:
अर्थशास्त्राणि यावंति धर्मशास्त्राणि यानि वै ॥
श्रुतानि सर्वशास्त्राणि भीष्माद्भागीरथीसुतात् ॥ 22 ॥
4.1.m: All the treatises on statecraft and all the treatises on dharma— / all the treatises were heard from Bhīṣma, the son of the Bhāgīrathī.

4.1.s:
svargaṃ gate śāntanave bhavānkṛṣṇo'tha yādavaḥ ..
suhṛttvādbandhubhāvācca nānyaḥ śikṣayitā mama .. 23 ..
4.1.d:
स्वर्गं गते शान्तनवे भवान्कृष्णोऽथ यादवः ॥
सुहृत्त्वाद्बन्धुभावाच्च नान्यः शिक्षयिता मम ॥ 23 ॥
4.1.m: Now that Śāntanu’s son has gone to heaven, you and Kṛṣṇa the Yādava, / out of friendship and kinship, have no other to instruct me.

4.1.s:
satyaṃ satyavatīsūnurdharmarājāya vakṣyati ..
viśeṣadharmānakhilānmunīnāmaviśeṣataḥ .. 24 ..
4.1.d:
सत्यं सत्यवतीसूनुर्धर्मराजाय वक्ष्यति ॥
विशेषधर्मानखिलान्मुनीनामविशेषतः ॥ 24 ॥
4.1.m: Truly Satyavatī's son will declare to the King of Dharma / all the particular dharmas of the sages without distinction."

4.1.s:
vyāsa uvāca .. ..
yadākhyeyaṃ tadākhyātaṃ mayā bhīṣmeṇa te'nagha ..
mārkaṇḍeyena dhaumyena lomaśena maharṣiṇā .. 25 ..
4.1.d:
व्यास उवाच ॥ ॥
यदाख्येयं तदाख्यातं मया भीष्मेण तेऽनघ ॥
मार्कण्डेयेन धौम्येन लोमशेन महर्षिणा ॥ 25 ॥
4.1.m: Vyāsa said: / "What was to be told has already been told to you, O sinless one, by me, by Bhīṣma, / by Mārkaṇḍeya, by Dhaumya, and by the great sage Lomaśa.

4.1.s:
dharmajño hyasi medhāvī guṇavānprā jñasattamaḥ ..
na te'styaviditaṃ kiñciddharmādharmaviniścaye .. 26 ..
4.1.d:
धर्मज्ञो ह्यसि मेधावी गुणवान्प्रा ज्ञसत्तमः ॥
न तेऽस्त्यविदितं किञ्चिद्धर्माधर्मविनिश्चये ॥ 26 ॥
4.1.m: For you know dharma, are intelligent, virtuous, and the best of the wise; / there is nothing unknown to you in determining dharma and adharma.

4.1.s:
pārśvasthite hṛṣīkeśe keśave keśisūdane ..
kasyacitkathane jihvā tatra saṃpari vartate .. 27 ..
4.1.d:
पार्श्वस्थिते हृषीकेशे केशवे केशिसूदने ॥
कस्यचित्कथने जिह्वा तत्र संपरि वर्तते ॥ 27 ॥
4.1.m: When Hṛṣīkeśa, Keśava, the slayer of Keśin, stands at your side, / whose tongue would venture to speak then?

4.1.s:
kartā pālayitā hartā jagatāṃ yo jaganmayaḥ ..
pratyakṣadarśī sarvasya dharmānvakṣyatyasau tava .. 28 ..
4.1.d:
कर्ता पालयिता हर्ता जगतां यो जगन्मयः ॥
प्रत्यक्षदर्शी सर्वस्य धर्मान्वक्ष्यत्यसौ तव ॥ 28 ॥
4.1.m: He who is the creator, protector, and destroyer of the worlds, who consists of the world, / who directly sees everything, will declare your dharmas to you."

4.1.s:
samādiśyeti kartavyaṃ bhagavānbādarāyaṇaḥ ..
pūjitaḥ pāṇḍutanayairjagāma svatapovanam .. 29 ..
4.1.d:
समादिश्येति कर्तव्यं भगवान्बादरायणः ॥
पूजितः पाण्डुतनयैर्जगाम स्वतपोवनम् ॥ 29 ॥
4.1.m: Having thus instructed him in what should be done, the venerable Bādarāyaṇa, / worshipped by the sons of Pāṇḍu, departed to his own penance grove.

4.1.s:
svābhāṣya bhāratavidhātari saṃprayāte te kautukākuladhiyo munayaḥ praśāntāḥ ..
kiṃ pṛcchati kṣapitabhāratalokaśokaḥ kiṃ vakṣyatīha bhagavānyaduvaṃśavīraḥ .. 4.1.30 ..
4.1.d:
स्वाभाष्य भारतविधातरि संप्रयाते ते कौतुकाकुलधियो मुनयः प्रशान्ताः ॥
किं पृच्छति क्षपितभारतलोकशोकः किं वक्ष्यतीह भगवान्यदुवंशवीरः ॥ 4.1.30 ॥
4.1.m: When the creator of the Mahābhārata had taken his leave and departed, those tranquil sages, their minds stirred with curiosity, [wondered]: / 'What will he ask, who has dispelled the grief of the people of the Bharatas, and what will the venerable hero of the Yadu race declare here?'

4.1.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
puṇyā mahānavamyasti tithīnāṃ pravarā tithiḥ..
sānuṣṭheyā suraiḥ sarvaiḥ prajāpālairviśeṣataḥ..1..
4.1.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
पुण्या महानवम्यस्ति तिथीनां प्रवरा तिथिः॥
सानुष्ठेया सुरैः सर्वैः प्रजापालैर्विशेषतः॥1॥
4.1.m: The blessed Kṛṣṇa said: / "The meritorious Mahānavamī is the most excellent lunar day among lunar days; / it should be observed by all gods, especially by protectors of subjects.

4.1.s:
bhavānutthāpayetpārtha saṃvatsarasukhāya vai ..
bhūtapretapiśācānāṃ prītyarthaṃ cotsavāya vā .. 2 ..
4.1.d:
भवानुत्थापयेत्पार्थ संवत्सरसुखाय वै ॥
भूतप्रेतपिशाचानां प्रीत्यर्थं चोत्सवाय वा ॥ 2 ॥
4.1.m: You should observe it, O son of Pṛthā, for the happiness of the entire year, / or for the delight and festival of ghosts, pretas, and piśācas."

4.1.s:
.. yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
kasmātkālātpravṛtteyaṃ navamī mahaśabdayuk ..
kimādāvupānno'sti bhagavannavamīvidhiḥ .. 3 ..
4.1.d:
॥ युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
कस्मात्कालात्प्रवृत्तेयं नवमी महशब्दयुक् ॥
किमादावुपान्नोऽस्ति भगवन्नवमीविधिः ॥ 3 ॥
4.1.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / "From what time did this navamī, bearing the title 'Mahā,' begin? / In the beginning, O venerable one, how did the rite of the navamī originate?

4.1.s:
yaśodāgarbhasaṃbhūteruta yātrā pravartate ..
utāho pṛrvamevāsītkṛtatretāyugādiṣu ..4..
4.1.d:
यशोदागर्भसंभूतेरुत यात्रा प्रवर्तते ॥
उताहो पृर्वमेवासीत्कृतत्रेतायुगादिषु ॥4॥
4.1.m: Does this procession proceed from the birth from Yaśodā's womb, / or did it exist even earlier, in the Kṛta, Tretā, and other yugas?

4.1.s:
yadasyāṃ prāṇinaḥ kecinmanyaṃte ghātayaṃti ca ..
hatānāṃ prāṇināṃ teṣāṃ kā gatiḥ pāralaukikī .. 5 ..
4.1.d:
यदस्यां प्राणिनः केचिन्मन्यंते घातयंति च ॥
हतानां प्राणिनां तेषां का गतिः पारलौकिकी ॥ 5 ॥
4.1.m: Since on this [day] some people honour living beings and slaughter them, / what is the fate in the other world of those living beings who are slain?

4.1.s:
svayaṃ ghnatāṃ ghātayatāmanumodayatāṃ tathā ..
etanme saṃśayaṃ pūrvaṃ vaktumarhasi keśava .. 6 ..
4.1.d:
स्वयं घ्नतां घातयतामनुमोदयतां तथा ॥
एतन्मे संशयं पूर्वं वक्तुमर्हसि केशव ॥ 6 ॥
4.1.m: And of those who slay them themselves, who cause them to be slain, and who approve of it? / You ought first to explain this doubt of mine, O Keśava."

4.1.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
pārtha yā paramā śaktiranaṃtā lokaviśrutā ..
ādyā sarvagatā śuddhā bhāva gamyā manoharā .. 7 ..
4.1.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
पार्थ या परमा शक्तिरनंता लोकविश्रुता ॥
आद्या सर्वगता शुद्धा भाव गम्या मनोहरा ॥ 7 ॥
4.1.m: The blessed Kṛṣṇa said: / "O son of Pṛthā, that supreme power which is endless and renowned in the world, / primordial, all-pervading, pure, accessible through devotion, and captivating;

4.1.s:
ādyāṣṭamī kalākālī dvitīyā sarvamaṃgalā ..
māyā kātyāyanī durgā cāmuṃḍā śaṃkarapriyā .. 8 ..
4.1.d:
आद्याष्टमी कलाकाली द्वितीया सर्वमंगला ॥
माया कात्यायनी दुर्गा चामुंडा शंकरप्रिया ॥ 8 ॥
4.1.m: the first is Aṣṭamī, the [crescent-]digit is Kālī, the second is Sarvamaṅgalā, / Māyā, Kātyāyanī, Durgā, Cāmuṇḍā, beloved of Śaṅkara.

4.1.s:
dhyāyaṃti yāṃ yogaratāṃ sā devī parameśvarī ..
rūpabhedairnāmabhedairbhavānī pūjyate śivā..9..
4.1.d:
ध्यायंति यां योगरतां सा देवी परमेश्वरी ॥
रूपभेदैर्नामभेदैर्भवानी पूज्यते शिवा॥9॥
4.1.m: She whom those devoted to yoga meditate upon is the goddess Parameśvarī; / with diverse forms and diverse names, Bhavānī, Śivā, is worshipped.

4.1.s:
aṣṭamyāṃ tu navamyāṃ tu devadānavarākṣasaiḥ..
gaṃdharvairuragairyajñaiḥ pūjyate kinnarairnaraiḥ..10..
4.1.d:
अष्टम्यां तु नवम्यां तु देवदानवराक्षसैः॥
गंधर्वैरुरगैर्यज्ञैः पूज्यते किन्नरैर्नरैः॥10॥
4.1.m: On the aṣṭamī and on the navamī, she is worshipped by gods, dānavas, and rākṣasas, / by gandharvas, uragas, yakṣas, kinnaras, and mortals.

4.1.s:
anyeṣvapi yugeṣvādau sṛṣṭeḥ pūrvaṃ pradarśitā..
pūjyateyaṃ purā devī tebhyaḥ pūrvataraiḥ śubhaiḥ..11..
4.1.d:
अन्येष्वपि युगेष्वादौ सृष्टेः पूर्वं प्रदर्शिता॥
पूज्यतेयं पुरा देवी तेभ्यः पूर्वतरैः शुभैः॥11॥
4.1.m: In other yugas as well, revealed at the beginning before creation, / this goddess was worshipped of old by auspicious [beings] far earlier than them.

4.1.s:
āśvayukśuklapakṣe ca yāṣṭamī mūla saṃyutā ..
sā mahānavamī nāma trailokye'pi sudurlabhā .. 12 ..
4.1.d:
आश्वयुक्शुक्लपक्षे च याष्टमी मूल संयुता ॥
सा महानवमी नाम त्रैलोक्येऽपि सुदुर्लभा ॥ 12 ॥
4.1.m: And in the bright fortnight of Āśvayuja, that aṣṭamī which is conjoined with Mūla / is called Mahānavamī, very difficult to attain even in the three worlds.

4.1.s:
kanyāgate savitari śuklapakṣe'ṣṭamī tu yā ..
mūlanakṣatrasaṃyuktā sā mahānavamī smṛtā .. 13 ..
4.1.d:
कन्यागते सवितरि शुक्लपक्षेऽष्टमी तु या ॥
मूलनक्षत्रसंयुक्ता सा महानवमी स्मृता ॥ 13 ॥
4.1.m: When the sun has entered Virgo, that aṣṭamī in the bright fortnight / conjoined with the Mūla asterism is known as Mahānavamī.

4.1.s:
aṣṭamyāṃ ca navamyāṃ ca jaganmātaramambikām ..
pūjayitvā''śvine māsi viśoko jayati dviṣaḥ .. 14 ..
4.1.d:
अष्टम्यां च नवम्यां च जगन्मातरमम्बिकाम् ॥
पूजयित्वा'ऽश्विने मासि विशोको जयति द्विषः ॥ 14 ॥
4.1.m: Having worshipped Ambikā, the mother of the universe, on the aṣṭamī and on the navamī / in the month of Āśvina, one conquers enemies, free from sorrow.

4.1.s:
saṃtarjayaṃtī huṃkāraiḥ khaḍgādibhiraharniśam ..
navamyāṃ pūjitā devī dadāti navamaṃ phalam .. 15 ..
4.1.d:
संतर्जयंती हुंकारैः खड्गादिभिरहर्निशम् ॥
नवम्यां पूजिता देवी ददाति नवमं फलम् ॥ 15 ॥
4.1.m: Threatening day and night with huṃ-cries, with swords and other [weapons], / the goddess, when worshipped on the navamī, grants the ninth fruit.

4.1.s:
sā puṇyā sā pavitrā ca sā dharmasukhadāyinī ..
tasmātsadā pūjanīyā cāmuṃḍā muṃḍamālinī .. 16 ..
4.1.d:
सा पुण्या सा पवित्रा च सा धर्मसुखदायिनी ॥
तस्मात्सदा पूजनीया चामुंडा मुंडमालिनी ॥ 16 ॥
4.1.m: She is meritorious, she is pure, and she is the bestower of dharma and happiness; / therefore, Cāmuṇḍā, adorned with a garland of severed heads, should always be worshipped.

4.1.s:
tasyāṃ yadyupayujyaṃte prāṇino mahiṣādayaḥ ..
sarve te svargatiṃ yāṃti ghnatāṃ pāpaṃ na vidyate .. 17 ..
4.1.d:
तस्यां यद्युपयुज्यंते प्राणिनो महिषादयः ॥
सर्वे ते स्वर्गतिं यांति घ्नतां पापं न विद्यते ॥ 17 ॥
4.1.m: If on that [day] animals such as buffaloes are employed [in sacrifice], / they all go to heaven, and no sin attaches to those who slay them.

4.1.s:
na tathā balidānena puṣpadhūpavilepanaiḥ ..
yathā saṃtuṣyate loke mahiṣairviṃdhyavāsinī .. 18 ..
4.1.d:
न तथा बलिदानेन पुष्पधूपविलेपनैः ॥
यथा संतुष्यते लोके महिषैर्विंध्यवासिनी ॥ 18 ॥
4.1.m: Vindhyavāsinī is not as pleased in the world by animal sacrifice, / nor by flowers, incense, and unguents, as [she is] by buffaloes."

4.1.s:
uddiśya durgāṃ hanyaṃte vidhānādye'tra jaṃtavaḥ ..
svargaṃ te yāṃti kauṃteya ghātayaṃto'pi bhaktiḥ .. 19 ..
4.1.d:
उद्दिश्य दुर्गां हन्यंते विधानाद्येऽत्र जंतवः ॥
स्वर्गं ते यांति कौंतेय घातयंतोऽपि भक्तिः ॥ 19 ॥
4.1.m: Those creatures that are slain here according to the prescribed rules with reference to Durgā, / they go to heaven, O son of Kuntī, as do those who cause them to be slain through devotion.

4.1.s:
bhavānīprāṅgaṇe prāṇā yeṣāṃ yātā yudhiṣṭhira ..
teṣāṃ svarge dhruvaṃ vāso varāste'pyarasāṃ priyāḥ .. 20 ..
4.1.d:
भवानीप्राङ्गणे प्राणा येषां याता युधिष्ठिर ॥
तेषां स्वर्गे ध्रुवं वासो वरास्तेऽप्यरसां प्रियाः ॥ 20 ॥
4.1.m: Those whose lives depart in the courtyard of Bhavānī, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / their dwelling in heaven is certain; they are the best, beloved even of the apsarases.

4.1.s:
manvantareṣu sarveṣu kalpeṣu kurunadana ..
teṣu sarveṣu caivāsannavamīyaṃ purārcitā .. 21 ..
4.1.d:
मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु कल्पेषु कुरुनदन ॥
तेषु सर्वेषु चैवासन्नवमीयं पुरार्चिता ॥ 21 ॥
4.1.m: In all the Manvantaras and in all the Kalpas, O delight of the Kurus, / in all of them indeed, this navamī was worshipped in ancient times.

4.1.s:
prasiddhānādinidhanā varṣevarṣe yudhiṣṭhira ..
bhūyobhūyo'vatāraiśca bhavānīpūjya tesuraiḥ .. 22 ..
4.1.d:
प्रसिद्धानादिनिधना वर्षेवर्षे युधिष्ठिर ॥
भूयोभूयोऽवतारैश्च भवानीपूज्य तेसुरैः ॥ 22 ॥
4.1.m: Famous, without beginning or end, year after year, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / through repeated incarnations, Bhavānī is worshipped by the gods.

4.1.s:
avatīrṇā bhuvi sadā nityaṃ daityanibarhiṇī ..
svargapātālamartyeṣu karoti sthitipālanam .. 23 ..
4.1.d:
अवतीर्णा भुवि सदा नित्यं दैत्यनिबर्हिणी ॥
स्वर्गपातालमर्त्येषु करोति स्थितिपालनम् ॥ 23 ॥
4.1.m: She descends constantly upon the earth, ever destroying the Daityas; / she preserves world order in heaven, the netherworld, and the realm of mortals.

4.1.s:
punaścaiṣā mahādevī yaśodā garbhasaṃbhavā ..
kaṃsāsurasyottamāṅge pādaṃ dattvā gatāyuṣaḥ .. 24 ..
4.1.d:
पुनश्चैषा महादेवी यशोदा गर्भसंभवा ॥
कंसासुरस्योत्तमाङ्गे पादं दत्त्वा गतायुषः ॥ 24 ॥
4.1.m: And once again, this Great Goddess, born from the womb of Yaśodā, / placed her foot on the head of the demon Kaṃsa, whose life had run out.

4.1.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti lokeṣu yaśodānaṃdadāyinīm ..
viṃdhyācale sthāpayitvā punaḥ pūjā pravartitā .. 25 ..
4.1.d:
ततः प्रभृति लोकेषु यशोदानंददायिनीम् ॥
विंध्याचले स्थापयित्वा पुनः पूजा प्रवर्तिता ॥ 25 ॥
4.1.m: From that time forward, having established that giver of joy to Yaśodā / on the Vindhya mountain, her worship was propagated once more in the worlds.

4.1.s:
pūrvapravṛddho'pi punarbhaginyā mahimā kṛtaḥ ..
bhuvi sarvopakārāya sarvopadravaśāṃtaye .. 26 ..
4.1.d:
पूर्वप्रवृद्धोऽपि पुनर्भगिन्या महिमा कृतः ॥
भुवि सर्वोपकाराय सर्वोपद्रवशांतये ॥ 26 ॥
4.1.m: Though already vast of old, her greatness was displayed again by the sister, / on earth for the welfare of all and for the pacification of all afflictions.

4.1.s:
evaṃ viṃdhyopavāsinyā navarātropavāsinaḥ ..
ekarātreṇa naktena svaśaktyā'yācitena vā .. 27 ..
4.1.d:
एवं विंध्योपवासिन्या नवरात्रोपवासिनः ॥
एकरात्रेण नक्तेन स्वशक्त्याऽयाचितेन वा ॥ 27 ॥
4.1.m: Thus, for Vindhyavāsinī, those fasting during the Navarātra, / whether for a single night, with a nocturnal meal, according to their capacity, or eating only unsolicited food,

4.1.s:
yajanairyājanairdevāḥ sthānesthāne purepure ..
gṛhegṛhe bhaktipare rgrāmegrāme vanevane .. 28 ..
4.1.d:
यजनैर्याजनैर्देवाः स्थानेस्थाने पुरेपुरे ॥
गृहेगृहे भक्तिपरे र्ग्रामेग्रामे वनेवने ॥ 28 ॥
4.1.m: by worship and by officiating at worship, the deities in every place, in every city, / in every house, devoted, in every village, and in every forest,

4.1.s:
snātaiḥ pramuditairhṛṣṭairbrāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriyairnṛpaiḥ ..
vaiśyaiḥ śūdrairbhakticitrairmlecchairanyaiśca mānavaiḥ .. 29 ..
4.1.d:
स्नातैः प्रमुदितैर्हृष्टैर्ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्नृपैः ॥
वैश्यैः शूद्रैर्भक्तिचित्रैर्म्लेच्छैरन्यैश्च मानवैः ॥ 29 ॥
4.1.m: by brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, kings, who are bathed, gladdened, and delighted, / by vaiśyas, śūdras with variegated devotions, mlecchas, and other humans,

4.1.s:
strībhiśca kuruśārdūla tadvidhānamidaṃ śṛṇu ..
jayābhilāṣī nṛpatiḥ pratipatprabhṛtikramāt .. 30 ..
4.1.d:
स्त्रीभिश्च कुरुशार्दूल तद्विधानमिदं शृणु ॥
जयाभिलाषी नृपतिः प्रतिपत्प्रभृतिक्रमात् ॥ 30 ॥
4.1.m: and by women, O bull among Kurus—hear that procedure! / A king desiring victory, in order from the first day onwards,

4.1.s:
lohābhihārikaṃ karma kārayedyāvadaṣṭami ..
prāgudakpravaṇe deśe patākābhiralaṃkṛtam .. 31 ..
4.1.d:
लोहाभिहारिकं कर्म कारयेद्यावदष्टमि ॥
प्रागुदक्प्रवणे देशे पताकाभिरलंकृतम् ॥ 31 ॥
4.1.m: should perform the iron-lustration rite up to the aṣṭamī. / In an area sloping toward the east or north, decorated with flags,

4.1.s:
maṇḍapaṃ kārayeddivyaṃ navasaptakaraṃ varam ..
āgneyyāṃ kārayetkuṇḍaṃ hastamātraṃ suśobhanam .. 32 ..
4.1.d:
मण्डपं कारयेद्दिव्यं नवसप्तकरं वरम् ॥
आग्नेय्यां कारयेत्कुण्डं हस्तमात्रं सुशोभनम् ॥ 32 ॥
4.1.m: he should have a celestial, excellent pavilion erected, measuring nine by seven cubits. / In the south-east he should have a very beautiful sacrificial pit made, measuring a cubit,

4.1.s:
mekhalātrayasaṃ yuktaṃ yonyaśvatthadalābhayā ..
rājacihnāni sarvāṇi śastrāṇyastrāṇi yāni ca .. 33 ..
4.1.d:
मेखलात्रयसं युक्तं योन्यश्वत्थदलाभया ॥
राजचिह्नानि सर्वाणि शस्त्राण्यस्त्राणि यानि च ॥ 33 ॥
4.1.m: provided with three tiers, having a vulva-shaped channel resembling an aśvattha leaf. / All the insignia of royalty and whatever weapons and missiles there are,

4.1.s:
ānīya maṇḍape tāni sarvāṇyevādhivāsayet ..
tatastu brāhmaṇaḥ snātaḥ śuklāṃbaradharaḥ śuciḥ.. 34 ..
oṃkārapūrvakairmantraistalliṃgairjuhuyādghṛtam..
4.1.d:
आनीय मण्डपे तानि सर्वाण्येवाधिवासयेत् ॥
ततस्तु ब्राह्मणः स्नातः शुक्लांबरधरः शुचिः॥ 34 ॥
ओंकारपूर्वकैर्मन्त्रैस्तल्लिंगैर्जुहुयाद्घृतम्॥
4.1.m:
having brought them all to the pavilion, he should consecrate them. / Then a brāhmaṇa, bathed, wearing white garments, pure,
should offer clarified butter with mantras preceded by the syllable Oṃ and bearing their characteristic marks. (35cd)

4.1.s: lohanāmābhavatpūrvaṃ dānavastu mahābalaḥ .. 35 ..
4.1.d: लोहनामाभवत्पूर्वं दानवस्तु महाबलः ॥ 35 ॥
4.1.m: Formerly there was an exceedingly powerful dānava named Loha. (36ab)

4.1.s:
sa devaiḥ samare kruddhairbahudhā śakalīkṛtaḥ ..
tadaṃgasambhavaṃ lohaṃ yatsarvaṃdṛśyate kṣitau .. 36 ..
4.1.d:
स देवैः समरे क्रुद्धैर्बहुधा शकलीकृतः ॥
तदंगसम्भवं लोहं यत्सर्वंदृश्यते क्षितौ ॥ 36 ॥
4.1.m: he was hacked into many pieces by the enraged gods in battle; / whatever iron is seen on earth originated from his limbs.

4.1.s:
śastrāstramantrairhotavyaṃ pāyasaṃ ghṛtasaṃyutam ..
hutaśeṣaṃ turaṃgāṇāṃ gajānāmupahārayet .. 37 ..
4.1.d:
शस्त्रास्त्रमन्त्रैर्होतव्यं पायसं घृतसंयुतम् ॥
हुतशेषं तुरंगाणां गजानामुपहारयेत् ॥ 37 ॥
4.1.m: Milk-rice mixed with ghee is to be offered with the mantras for weapons and missiles; / the remainder of the oblation he should present to the horses and elephants.

4.1.s:
lohābhihārikaṃ karma tenaitadṛṣibhiḥ smṛtam ..
baddhapratiśaravyaṃ ca gajāśvasamalaṃkṛtam .. 38 ..
4.1.d:
लोहाभिहारिकं कर्म तेनैतदृषिभिः स्मृतम् ॥
बद्धप्रतिशरव्यं च गजाश्वसमलंकृतम् ॥ 38 ॥
4.1.m: For this reason the sages call this the iron-lustration rite. / Having set up an effigy-target, adorned with elephants and horses,

4.1.s:
bhrāmayennagare nityaṃ naṃdi ghoṣapurassaram..
pratyahaṃ nṛpatiḥ snātvā saṃpūjya pitṛdevatāḥ .. 39 ..
4.1.d:
भ्रामयेन्नगरे नित्यं नंदि घोषपुरस्सरम्॥
प्रत्यहं नृपतिः स्नात्वा संपूज्य पितृदेवताः ॥ 39 ॥
4.1.m: he should paraded through the city daily, accompanied by auspicious sounds. / Everyday the king, having bathed and worshipped the ancestors and gods,

4.1.s:
pūjayedrājacihnāni phalamālyānulepanaiḥ ..
hutaśeṣaṃ pradātavyamaupanāyanike dvije .. 40 ..
4.1.d:
पूजयेद्राजचिह्नानि फलमाल्यानुलेपनैः ॥
हुतशेषं प्रदातव्यमौपनायनिके द्विजे ॥ 40 ॥
4.1.m: should worship the insignia of royalty with fruits, garlands, and unguents. / The remainder of the oblation should be given to a brāhmaṇa who has received initiation.

4.1.s:
tasyābhiharaṇādrājño vijayaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ ..
pūjāmaṃtrānpravakṣyāmi purāṇoktānahaṃ tava .. 41 ..
4.1.d:
तस्याभिहरणाद्राज्ञो विजयः समुदाहृतः ॥
पूजामंत्रान्प्रवक्ष्यामि पुराणोक्तानहं तव ॥ 41 ॥
4.1.m: From performing that ritual, victory is declared for the king. / I shall tell you the worship mantras taught in the Purāṇas,

4.1.s:
yaiḥ pūjitāḥ prayacchanti kīrtimāyu ryaśobalama..
yathāṃbudaśchādayati śivāyemāṃ vasundharām .. 42 ..
4.1.d:
यैः पूजिताः प्रयच्छन्ति कीर्तिमायु र्यशोबलम॥
यथांबुदश्छादयति शिवायेमां वसुन्धराम् ॥ 42 ॥
4.1.m: worshipped with which they grant renown, long life, fame, and strength. / Just as a cloud covers this earth for its welfare,

4.1.s:
tathācchādaya rājānaṃ vijayārogyavṛddhaye .. ( iti chatramantraḥ) ..
gandharva kulajātastvaṃ mābhūyāḥ kuladūṣakaḥ .. 43 ..
4.1.d:
तथाच्छादय राजानं विजयारोग्यवृद्धये ॥ ( इति छत्रमन्त्रः) ॥
गन्धर्व कुलजातस्त्वं माभूयाः कुलदूषकः ॥ 43 ॥
4.1.m: so cover the king for the increase of victory and health. (Thus the mantra for the royal parasol.) / Born of the Gandharva race, do not become a disgrace to your family!

4.1.s:
brahmaṇaḥ satyavākyena somasya varuṇasya ca ..
prabhāvāñca hutāśasya varddhasva tvaṃ turaṃgama .. 44 ..
4.1.d:
ब्रह्मणः सत्यवाक्येन सोमस्य वरुणस्य च ॥
प्रभावाञ्च हुताशस्य वर्द्धस्व त्वं तुरंगम ॥ 44 ॥
4.1.m: By the truthful word of Brahmā, and of Soma, and of Varuṇa, / and by the power of the Fire-god, increase, O horse!

4.1.s:
tejasā caiva sūryasya munīnāṃ tapasā yathā ..
rudrasya brahmacaryeṇa pavanasya valena ca.. smṛ ..
smara tvaṃ rājaputro'si kaustubhaṃ ca maṇiṃ smara ..
yāṃ gatiṃ brahmahā gacchetpitṛhā mātṛhā tathā .. 46 ..
4.1.d:
तेजसा चैव सूर्यस्य मुनीनां तपसा यथा ॥
रुद्रस्य ब्रह्मचर्येण पवनस्य वलेन च॥ स्मृ ॥
स्मर त्वं राजपुत्रोऽसि कौस्तुभं च मणिं स्मर ॥
यां गतिं ब्रह्महा गच्छेत्पितृहा मातृहा तथा ॥ 46 ॥
4.1.m: Through the splendour of the Sun and the penance of the sages, / through Rudra's celibacy and the wind's strength, / remember that you are a prince, and remember the Kaustubha jewel! / The destination that a slayer of a brāhmaṇa, a father-slayer, and a mother-slayer would attain,

4.1.s:
bhūmyarthenṛtavādī ca kṣatriyaśca parāṅmukhaḥ ..
sūryācandramasau vāyuḥ pāvakaśca na yatra vai .. 47..
4.1.d:
भूम्यर्थेनृतवादी च क्षत्रियश्च पराङ्मुखः ॥
सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ वायुः पावकश्च न यत्र वै ॥ 47॥
4.1.m: and one who speaks falsehood for the sake of land, and a kṣatriya who turns his back [in battle], / where indeed the sun and moon, the wind, and the fire do not go,

4.1.s:
vrajecca tāṃ gatiṃ kṣipraṃ tacca pāpaṃ bhavetkila ..
vikṛtiṃ yadi gacchestvaṃ yuddhedhvani turaṃgama ..
ripūnvijitya samare saha bhartrā sukhī bhava .. 48 .... .. ( ityaśvamaṃtraḥ) .. ..
4.1.d:
व्रजेच्च तां गतिं क्षिप्रं तच्च पापं भवेत्किल ॥
विकृतिं यदि गच्छेस्त्वं युद्धेध्वनि तुरंगम ॥
रिपून्विजित्य समरे सह भर्त्रा सुखी भव ॥ 48 ॥॥ ॥ ( इत्यश्वमंत्रः) ॥ ॥
4.1.m: may you swiftly go to that destination, and indeed may that sin be yours, / if you falter in battle or on the march, O horse! / Having conquered enemies in battle together with your master, be happy! (Thus the horse mantra.)

4.1.s:
śakraketo mahāvīrya suparṇastvayyupasthitaḥ ..
patatrirāḍvainateyastathā nārāyaṇadhvajaḥ .. 49 ..
4.1.d:
शक्रकेतो महावीर्य सुपर्णस्त्वय्युपस्थितः ॥
पतत्रिराड्वैनतेयस्तथा नारायणध्वजः ॥ 49 ॥
4.1.m: O banner of Indra of great valour, the fair-winged bird is present on you, / the king of birds, son of Vinatā, who is also the banner of Nārāyaṇa,

4.1.s:
kāśyapeyo'mṛto jñeyo nāgārirviṣṇuvāhanaḥ ..
aprameyo durādharṣo devaśatruniṣūdanaḥ .. 50 ..
4.1.d:
काश्यपेयोऽमृतो ज्ञेयो नागारिर्विष्णुवाहनः ॥
अप्रमेयो दुराधर्षो देवशत्रुनिषूदनः ॥ 50 ॥
4.1.m: the son of Kaśyapa, immortal, enemy of serpents, mount of Viṣṇu, / immeasurable, invincible, slayer of the enemies of the gods,

4.1.s:
garutmānmārutagatistvayi sannihitaḥ sthitaḥ ..
śastravarmāyudhānyodhānrakṣāsmāṃśca ripūndaha .. 51 .. .. (iti dhvajamaṃtraḥ) .. ..
4.1.d:
गरुत्मान्मारुतगतिस्त्वयि सन्निहितः स्थितः ॥
शस्त्रवर्मायुधान्योधान्रक्षास्मांश्च रिपून्दह ॥ 51 ॥ ॥ (इति ध्वजमंत्रः) ॥ ॥
4.1.m: Garutmān, moving like the wind, resides fixed on you. / Protect the weapons, armour, arms, and warriors, protect us, and burn our enemies! (Thus the banner mantra.)

4.1.s:
kumudairāvaṇau padmaḥ puṣpadaṃto'tha vāmanaḥ ..
supratīkoñjano nīla ete'ṣṭau devayonayaḥ .... 52 ..
4.1.d:
कुमुदैरावणौ पद्मः पुष्पदंतोऽथ वामनः ॥
सुप्रतीकोञ्जनो नील एतेऽष्टौ देवयोनयः ॥॥ 52 ॥
4.1.m: Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, Vāmana, / Supratīka, Añjana, and Nīla—these eight are of divine origin.

4.1.s:
eteṣāṃ putrapautrāśca balānyaṣṭau samāśritāḥ ..
bhadro mandro mṛgaścaiva gajaḥ saṃkīrṇa eva ca ..
vanevane prasūtāste kariyoniṃ mahāgajāḥ..53..
4.1.d:
एतेषां पुत्रपौत्राश्च बलान्यष्टौ समाश्रिताः ॥
भद्रो मन्द्रो मृगश्चैव गजः संकीर्ण एव च ॥
वनेवने प्रसूतास्ते करियोनिं महागजाः॥53॥
4.1.m: Their sons and grandsons, supported by the eight forces, / bhadra, mandra, mṛga, and gaja, as well as the mixed types, / those great elephants were born in every forest in the elephant species.

4.1.s:
pātu tvāṃ vasavo rudrā ādityāḥ samarudgaṇāḥ ..
bhartāraṃ rakṣa nāgendra samayaṃ pratipālayan .. 54 ..
4.1.d:
पातु त्वां वसवो रुद्रा आदित्याः समरुद्गणाः ॥
भर्तारं रक्ष नागेन्द्र समयं प्रतिपालयन् ॥ 54 ॥
4.1.m: May the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas, together with the Marut hosts, protect you! / Protect your master, lord of elephants, observing your duty!

4.1.s:
avāpurhi jayaṃ yuddhe gamane svasti no vraja ..
śrīste somādbalaṃ viṣṇostejaḥ sūryājjavonilāt ..
sthairyaṃ merorjayaṃ rudrādyaśo devātpuraṃdarāt .. 55 ..
4.1.d:
अवापुर्हि जयं युद्धे गमने स्वस्ति नो व्रज ॥
श्रीस्ते सोमाद्बलं विष्णोस्तेजः सूर्याज्जवोनिलात् ॥
स्थैर्यं मेरोर्जयं रुद्राद्यशो देवात्पुरंदरात् ॥ 55 ॥
4.1.m: May they indeed achieve victory in battle; may we go in well-being on the march! / May your splendour come from Soma, strength from Viṣṇu, brilliance from the Sun, speed from the Wind, / firmness from Meru, victory from Rudra, and renown from god Puraṃdara!

4.1.s:
yuddhe rakṣaṃtu nāgāstvāṃ diśaśca saha daivataiḥ ..
aśvinau saha gaṃdharvaiḥ pāṃtu tvāṃ sarvataḥ sadā .. 56 .. ( iti hastimaṃtraḥ ..)
4.1.d:
युद्धे रक्षंतु नागास्त्वां दिशश्च सह दैवतैः ॥
अश्विनौ सह गंधर्वैः पांतु त्वां सर्वतः सदा ॥ 56 ॥ ( इति हस्तिमंत्रः ॥)
4.1.m: May the serpents and the directions along with the deities protect you in battle! / May the two Aśvins along with the Gandharvas protect you on all sides at all times! (Thus the elephant mantra.)

4.1.s:
hutabhugvasavo rudrā vāyuḥ somo maharṣayaḥ ..
nāgakinnaragandharvayakṣa bhūtagaṇāgrahāḥ .. 57 ..
4.1.d:
हुतभुग्वसवो रुद्रा वायुः सोमो महर्षयः ॥
नागकिन्नरगन्धर्वयक्ष भूतगणाग्रहाः ॥ 57 ॥
4.1.m: The fire-consumer, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Wind, Soma, the great sages, / the nāgas, kinnaras, gandharvas, yakṣas, bhūtas, and the planets,

4.1.s:
pramathāśca sahādityairbhūteśo mātṛbhiḥ saha ..
śakrasenāpatiḥ skando varuṇaścāśritāstvayi .. 58 ..
4.1.d:
प्रमथाश्च सहादित्यैर्भूतेशो मातृभिः सह ॥
शक्रसेनापतिः स्कन्दो वरुणश्चाश्रितास्त्वयि ॥ 58 ॥
4.1.m: and the Pramathas together with the Ādityas, the Lord of Bhūtas with the Mothers, / Indra’s commander Skanda, and Varuṇa—all have taken refuge in you.

4.1.s:
pradahaṃtu ripūnsarvānrājā vijayamṛcchatu ..
yāni prayuktānyaribhirdūṣaṇāni samaṃtataḥ .. 59 ..
4.1.d:
प्रदहंतु रिपून्सर्वान्राजा विजयमृच्छतु ॥
यानि प्रयुक्तान्यरिभिर्दूषणानि समंततः ॥ 59 ॥
4.1.m: Let them completely consume all enemies! May the king attain victory! / Whatever contaminations have been employed on every side by the foes,

4.1.s:
etāni paraśatrūṇāṃ hatāni tava tejasā ..
kālanemivadhe yuddhe yuddhe tripuraghātane .. 60 ..
4.1.d:
एतानि परशत्रूणां हतानि तव तेजसा ॥
कालनेमिवधे युद्धे युद्धे त्रिपुरघातने ॥ 60 ॥
4.1.m: these belonging to the external enemies have been destroyed by your brilliance! / In the battle for the slaying of Kālanemi, in the battle for the destruction of Tripura,

4.1.s:
hiraṇyakaśiporyuddhe yuddhe devāsure tathā ..
śobhitāsi tathaivādya śobhamānāstu bhūpateḥ .. 61 ..
4.1.d:
हिरण्यकशिपोर्युद्धे युद्धे देवासुरे तथा ॥
शोभितासि तथैवाद्य शोभमानास्तु भूपतेः ॥ 61 ॥
4.1.m: in the battle against Hiraṇyakaśipu, and in the battle between gods and asuras, / you shone; in that very way, shine today on behalf of the king!

4.1.s:
nīlāṃ śvetāmimāṃ dṛṣṭvā naśyaṃtvadya nṛpārayaḥ ..
vyādhibhirvividhairghoraiḥ śastraiśca yudhi nirjitāḥ .. 62 ..
4.1.d:
नीलां श्वेतामिमां दृष्ट्वा नश्यंत्वद्य नृपारयः ॥
व्याधिभिर्विविधैर्घोरैः शस्त्रैश्च युधि निर्जिताः ॥ 62 ॥
4.1.m: Beholding this [banner], dark blue and white, may the king’s enemies perish today, / vanquished in battle by dread diseases of various kinds and by weapons.

4.1.s: sadyaḥ svasthā bhavaṃti sma tvadvātenāpamārjitāḥ .. 63 ..
4.1.d: सद्यः स्वस्था भवंति स्म त्वद्वातेनापमार्जिताः ॥ 63 ॥
4.1.m: They became well at once, swept over by your breeze. 63.

4.1.s:
pūtanā revatī nāmnā kālarātrīti yā smṛtā ..
dahaṃtvāśu ripūnsarvānpatāke tvāmupāgatāḥ .. 64 .. (iti patākāmantraḥ ..)
4.1.d:
पूतना रेवती नाम्ना कालरात्रीति या स्मृता ॥
दहंत्वाशु रिपून्सर्वान्पताके त्वामुपागताः ॥ 64 ॥ (इति पताकामन्त्रः ॥)
4.1.m: O banner, may those who are remembered as Pūtanā, Revatī by name, and Kālarātrī, / having entered into you, swiftly burn all our foes. (Thus the mantra of the banner.)

4.1.s:
asiśca ripuhā khaḍgastīkṣṇakarmā durāsadaḥ ..
śrīgarbho vijayaścaiva dharmadhārastathaiva ca .. 69 ..
4.1.d:
असिश्च रिपुहा खड्गस्तीक्ष्णकर्मा दुरासदः ॥
श्रीगर्भो विजयश्चैव धर्मधारस्तथैव च ॥ 69 ॥
4.1.m: Asi, the foe-slayer, Khaḍga, fierce-working, unassailable, / Śrīgarbha, Vijaya, and likewise Dharmadhāra,

4.1.s:
ityaṣṭau tava nāmāni svayamuktāni vedhasā ..
nakṣatraṃ kṛttikā tubhyaṃ gururdevo maheśvaraḥ .. 66 ..
4.1.d:
इत्यष्टौ तव नामानि स्वयमुक्तानि वेधसा ॥
नक्षत्रं कृत्तिका तुभ्यं गुरुर्देवो महेश्वरः ॥ 66 ॥
4.1.m: these eight names of yours were proclaimed by the Creator himself. / Your constellation is Kṛttikā; your guru is the divine Maheśvara;

4.1.s:
hiraṇyaṃ ca śarīraṃte dhātā devojanārdanaḥ ..
pitā pitāmaho devastvaṃ māṃ pālaya sarvadā .. 67 .. (iti khaḍgamantraḥ ..)
4.1.d:
हिरण्यं च शरीरंते धाता देवोजनार्दनः ॥
पिता पितामहो देवस्त्वं मां पालय सर्वदा ॥ 67 ॥ (इति खड्गमन्त्रः ॥)
4.1.m: gold is your body, and the divine Janārdana is your creator; / your father is the divine Grandfather. Do you always protect me. (Thus the mantra of the sword.)

4.1.s:
śarmapradastvaṃ samare varma sarvāyaso hyasi ..
rakṣa māṃ rakṣaṇīyo'haṃ tava varmannamo'stu te .. 68 .. ( iti varmamantraḥ ..) ..
4.1.d:
शर्मप्रदस्त्वं समरे वर्म सर्वायसो ह्यसि ॥
रक्ष मां रक्षणीयोऽहं तव वर्मन्नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 68 ॥ ( इति वर्ममन्त्रः ॥) ॥
4.1.m: You grant protection in battle, for you are armour made entirely of iron. / Protect me, for I am to be protected by you; O armour, homage to you. (Thus the mantra of the armour.)

4.1.s:
dundubhe tvaṃ sapatnānāṃ .ghoṣāddhṛdayakampan ..
bhava bhūmipa sainyānāṃ tathā vijayavarddhanaḥ .. 69 ..
4.1.d:
दुन्दुभे त्वं सपत्नानां ।घोषाद्धृदयकम्पन् ॥
भव भूमिप सैन्यानां तथा विजयवर्द्धनः ॥ 69 ॥
4.1.m: O war drum, causing the hearts of adversaries to tremble with your roar, / become likewise the enhancer of victory for the armies of the king.

4.1.s:
yathā jīmūtaghoṣeṇa hṛṣyaṃti varavāraṇāḥ ..
tathāstu tava śabdena harṣo'smākaṃ mudāvahaḥ ..70..
4.1.d:
यथा जीमूतघोषेण हृष्यंति वरवारणाः ॥
तथास्तु तव शब्देन हर्षोऽस्माकं मुदावहः ॥70॥
4.1.m: Just as choice elephants rejoice at the roar of a raincloud, / so may your sound bring us joy that conveys delight.

4.1.s:
yathā jīmūtaśabdena strīṇāṃ trāso'bhijāyate ..
tathā ca tava śabdena trasyaṃtvasmaddviṣo raṇe..71..( iti duṃdubhimaṃtraḥ ..)
4.1.d:
यथा जीमूतशब्देन स्त्रीणां त्रासोऽभिजायते ॥
तथा च तव शब्देन त्रस्यंत्वस्मद्द्विषो रणे॥71॥( इति दुंदुभिमंत्रः ॥)
4.1.m: Just as terror arises in women at the sound of a raincloud, / so too may our enemies in battle tremble at your sound. (Thus the mantra of the war drum.)

4.1.s:
sarvāyudha mahāmātra sarvadevārisūdana ..
cāpa māṃ sarvadā rakṣa sākaṃ sāyakasattamaiḥ .. 72.. ( iti cāpamantraḥ..)
4.1.d:
सर्वायुध महामात्र सर्वदेवारिसूदन ॥
चाप मां सर्वदा रक्ष साकं सायकसत्तमैः ॥ 72॥ ( इति चापमन्त्रः॥)
4.1.m: O chief among all weapons, slayer of all the enemies of the gods, / O bow, protect me always together with the finest arrows. (Thus the mantra of the bow.)

4.1.s:
puṇyastvaṃ śaṅkha puṣpāṇāṃ maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam ..
viṣṇunā vidhṛto nityaṃ manaḥśāṃtiprado bhava .. 73 .. ( iti śaṅkhamantraḥ ..)
4.1.d:
पुण्यस्त्वं शङ्ख पुष्पाणां मङ्गलानां च मङ्गलम् ॥
विष्णुना विधृतो नित्यं मनःशांतिप्रदो भव ॥ 73 ॥ ( इति शङ्खमन्त्रः ॥)
4.1.m: You are holy, O conch, the flower of auspicious things and the most auspicious of all. / Held constantly by Viṣṇu, be the bestower of peace of mind. (Thus the mantra of the conch.)

4.1.s:
śaśāṃkakarasaṃkāśa hima ḍiṃḍīrapāṃḍura ..
protsārayāśu duritaṃ cāmarāmaravallabha .. 74 .. ( iti cāmaramaṃtraḥ ..)
4.1.d:
शशांककरसंकाश हिम डिंडीरपांडुर ॥
प्रोत्सारयाशु दुरितं चामरामरवल्लभ ॥ 74 ॥ ( इति चामरमंत्रः ॥)
4.1.m: Resembling the rays of the moon, white as snow and foam, / swiftly banish misfortune, O chowrie beloved of the immortals. (Thus the mantra of the chowrie.)

4.1.s:
sarvāyudhānāṃ prathamā nirmitā'si pinākinā ..
śūlāyudhādviniṣkṛṣya kṛtvā muṣṭiparigraham .. 75 ..
4.1.d:
सर्वायुधानां प्रथमा निर्मिताऽसि पिनाकिना ॥
शूलायुधाद्विनिष्कृष्य कृत्वा मुष्टिपरिग्रहम् ॥ 75 ॥
4.1.m: You were created first among all weapons by the wielder of Pināka, / who drew you out from the trident-weapon and formed you for the grasp of the fist.

4.1.s:
caṃḍikāyāḥ pradattāsi sarvaduṣṭanibarhiṇi ..
tathā vistāritā cāsi devānāṃ pratipāditā .. 76 ..
4.1.d:
चंडिकायाः प्रदत्तासि सर्वदुष्टनिबर्हिणि ॥
तथा विस्तारिता चासि देवानां प्रतिपादिता ॥ 76 ॥
4.1.m: You were given to Caṇḍikā, O destroyer of all the wicked; / then you were multiplied and presented to the gods.

4.1.s:
sarva sattvāṃgabhūtāsi
sarvāśubhanivāriṇi ..
churike rakṣa māṃ nityaṃ śāntiṃ yaccha namo'stu te .. 77 .. ( iticchūrikāmaṃtraḥ ..)
4.1.d:
सर्व सत्त्वांगभूतासि
सर्वाशुभनिवारिणि ॥
छुरिके रक्ष मां नित्यं शान्तिं यच्छ नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 77 ॥ ( इतिच्छूरिकामंत्रः ॥)
4.1.m: You have become a part of the bodies of all beings, / O dispeller of all inauspiciousness! / O dagger, protect me perpetually and grant peace! Homage to you! 77. (Thus the dagger mantra.)

4.1.s:
protsāraṇāya duṣṭānāṃ sādhusaṃgrahaṇāya ca ..
brahmaṇā nirmitaścāsi vyavahāraprasiddhaye ..78..
4.1.d:
प्रोत्सारणाय दुष्टानां साधुसंग्रहणाय च ॥
ब्रह्मणा निर्मितश्चासि व्यवहारप्रसिद्धये ॥78॥
4.1.m: For driving away the wicked and for protecting the virtuous, / and for the establishment of worldly order, you were created by Brahmā.

4.1.s:
yaśo dehi sukhaṃ dehi jagado bhava bhūpateḥ ..
tāḍayāśu ripūnsarvānhemadaṃḍa namostu te .. 70 .. ( iti kanakadaṇḍamantraḥ ..)
4.1.d:
यशो देहि सुखं देहि जगदो भव भूपतेः ॥
ताडयाशु रिपून्सर्वान्हेमदंड नमोस्तु ते ॥ 70 ॥ ( इति कनकदण्डमन्त्रः ॥)
4.1.m: Bestow fame, bestow happiness, be the protector of the world for the king; / strike down all foes swiftly, O golden sceptre, homage to you. (Thus the mantra of the golden sceptre.)

4.1.s:
vijayo jayado jetā ripughātī priyaṃkaraḥ ..
duḥkhahā dharmadaḥ śāṃtaḥ sarvāriṣṭavināśanaḥ ..80..
4.1.d:
विजयो जयदो जेता रिपुघाती प्रियंकरः ॥
दुःखहा धर्मदः शांतः सर्वारिष्टविनाशनः ॥80॥
4.1.m: Vijaya, the giver of victory, conqueror, foe-slayer, pleaser, / remover of sorrow, giver of righteousness, tranquil, destroyer of all misfortunes—

4.1.s:
ete'ṣṭausaṃnidhau yasmāttava siṃhā mahābalāḥ...
tena siṃhāsaneti tvaṃ viprairvedeṣu gīyase ..81..
4.1.d:
एतेऽष्टौसंनिधौ यस्मात्तव सिंहा महाबलाः॥।
तेन सिंहासनेति त्वं विप्रैर्वेदेषु गीयसे ॥81॥
4.1.m: because these eight exceedingly powerful lions stand in your presence, / therefore you are sung by the Brahmins in the Vedas as the lion-throne.

4.1.s:
tvayi sthitaḥ śivaḥ sākṣāttvayi śakraḥ sureśvaraḥ..
tvayi sthito harirdevastvadarthaṃ tapyate tapaḥ .. 82 ..
4.1.d:
त्वयि स्थितः शिवः साक्षात्त्वयि शक्रः सुरेश्वरः॥
त्वयि स्थितो हरिर्देवस्त्वदर्थं तप्यते तपः ॥ 82 ॥
4.1.m: In you dwells Śiva visibly; in you dwells Śakra, lord of the gods; / in you dwells the divine Hari; for your sake austerity is performed.

4.1.s:
namaste sarvato bhadra bhadrado bhava bhūpateḥ ..
trailokyajayasarvasva siṃhāsana namo'stu te .. 83 .. ( iti siṃhāsanamaṃtraḥ ..)
4.1.d:
नमस्ते सर्वतो भद्र भद्रदो भव भूपतेः ॥
त्रैलोक्यजयसर्वस्व सिंहासन नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 83 ॥ ( इति सिंहासनमंत्रः ॥)
4.1.m: Homage to you, auspicious on all sides; be the bestower of welfare upon the king; / O all-in-all of victory in the three worlds, O throne, homage to you. (Thus the mantra of the throne.)

4.1.s:
lohābhihārikaṃ karma kṛtvedaṃ maṃtrapūrvakam..
phalanaivedyakusumairdhūpadīpavilepanaiḥ ..84..
4.1.d:
लोहाभिहारिकं कर्म कृत्वेदं मंत्रपूर्वकम्॥
फलनैवेद्यकुसुमैर्धूपदीपविलेपनैः ॥84॥
4.1.m: Having performed this iron-lustration rite preceded by mantras, / with fruits, food-offerings, flowers, incenses, lamps, and ointments,

4.1.s: aṣṭamyāṃ dhāvanaṃ kṛtvā pūrvāhṇe snānamācaret.... 85 ..
4.1.d: अष्टम्यां धावनं कृत्वा पूर्वाह्णे स्नानमाचरेत्॥॥ 85 ॥
4.1.m: and having brushed [one's teeth] on the aṣṭamī, one should take a bath in the forenoon.

4.1.s:
( atha gadyam)
durgāṃ kāṃcanamūrtiṃ raupyāṃ vā paittalīṃ vārkṣī caitrīṃ tāmrīṃ vādhibhavataḥ kṛtvā
dāruvicitratoraṇavinyastāṃ śobhane sthāne purato vinyastadṛṣṭāṃ vicitragṛhamadhyagāṃ
snātāṃ kuṃkumacaṃdanagaṃdhaiścatuḥsamaiścīrapaṭṭaiścarcitagātrāṃ devīṃ kusumairabhyarcya
tāṃ bahubhiḥ puṣyamāṇakīrtistairdvijananairjanitaparitoṣairdivānvito nareṃdraḥ svayaṃ
prayacchetpurohitaiḥ sārdhaṃ bilvapatreṇārcanena maṃtreṇānena bhagavatyai ..
( iti gadyaṃ sampūrṇaṃ) ..
jayaṃtī maṃgalā kālī bhadrakālī kapālinī ..
durgā śivā kṣamā dhātrī svāhā svadhā namostu te .. 86 ..
4.1.d:
( अथ गद्यम्)
दुर्गां कांचनमूर्तिं रौप्यां वा पैत्तलीं वार्क्षी चैत्रीं ताम्रीं वाधिभवतः कृत्वा
दारुविचित्रतोरणविन्यस्तां शोभने स्थाने पुरतो विन्यस्तदृष्टां विचित्रगृहमध्यगां
स्नातां कुंकुमचंदनगंधैश्चतुःसमैश्चीरपट्टैश्चर्चितगात्रां देवीं कुसुमैरभ्यर्च्य
तां बहुभिः पुष्यमाणकीर्तिस्तैर्द्विजननैर्जनितपरितोषैर्दिवान्वितो नरेंद्रः स्वयं
प्रयच्छेत्पुरोहितैः सार्धं बिल्वपत्रेणार्चनेन मंत्रेणानेन भगवत्यै ॥
( इति गद्यं सम्पूर्णं) ॥
जयंती मंगला काली भद्रकाली कपालिनी ॥
दुर्गा शिवा क्षमा धात्री स्वाहा स्वधा नमोस्तु ते ॥ 86 ॥
4.1.m:
(Now the prose passage:)
Having fashioned an image of Durgā—either of gold, or of silver, or of brass, or of wood, or painted, or of copper, according to his means—
placed beneath a multi-coloured wooden archway in a beautiful place, with eyes directed forward, set within a splendid chamber,
bathed, her limbs smeared with saffron, sandalwood paste, catuḥsama, and strips of silken cloth, the king, his fame magnified by the many twice-born men who are thoroughly pleased, accompanied by [his people] by day, should himself, along with the royal priests, make an offering with a bilva leaf to the goddess with this mantra of worship:
(Thus ends the prose passage.)
Jayantī, Maṅgalā, Kālī, Bhadrakālī, Kapālinī, / Durgā, Śivā, Kṣamā, Dhātrī, Svāhā, Svadhā, homage to you.

4.1.s:
amṛtodbhavaḥ śrīvṛkṣo mahādevīpriyaḥ sadā ..
bilvapatraṃ prayacchāmi pavitraṃ te sureśvari .. 87 ..
4.1.d:
अमृतोद्भवः श्रीवृक्षो महादेवीप्रियः सदा ॥
बिल्वपत्रं प्रयच्छामि पवित्रं ते सुरेश्वरि ॥ 87 ॥
4.1.m: Born of nectar is the śrī-tree, ever dear to the Great Goddess. / I offer a holy bilva leaf to you, O queen of the gods.

4.1.s:
durgā saṃpūjanīyā ca taddināddroṇapuṣpayā ..
sā cābhīṣṭā sureśānyāstathā rūḍhavraṇāyutaḥ ...88...
4.1.d:
दुर्गा संपूजनीया च तद्दिनाद्द्रोणपुष्पया ॥
सा चाभीष्टा सुरेशान्यास्तथा रूढव्रणायुतः ॥.88॥।
4.1.m: And Durgā is to be worshipped from that day with droṇapuṣpa blossoms; / and that [flower] is beloved of the queen of the gods, [bringing healing to one] possessed of healed wounds.

4.1.s:
tataḥ khaḍgaṃ namaskṛtya śatrūṇāṃ mānamarddanam ..
icchetsvavijayaṃ rājyaṃ subhikṣaṃ cātmano nṛpa .. 89 ..
4.1.d:
ततः खड्गं नमस्कृत्य शत्रूणां मानमर्द्दनम् ॥
इच्छेत्स्वविजयं राज्यं सुभिक्षं चात्मनो नृप ॥ 89 ॥
4.1.m: Then, having bowed to the sword, the crusher of the pride of enemies, / one should desire for oneself victory, sovereignty, and abundance, O king.

4.1.s:
punaḥ punaḥ praṇamyātha dhyāyecca hṛdaye śivām..
mahiṣaghrīṃ bahubhujāṃ kumārīṃ siṃhavāhinīm .. 90 ..
4.1.d:
पुनः पुनः प्रणम्याथ ध्यायेच्च हृदये शिवाम्॥
महिषघ्रीं बहुभुजां कुमारीं सिंहवाहिनीम् ॥ 90 ॥
4.1.m: Having bowed again and again, one should then meditate in one's heart on Śivā: / the slayer of the buffalo, many-armed, the Maiden, riding a lion,

4.1.s:
dānavāṃstarjayaṃtīṃ ca khaḍgoddhatakarāṃ śubhām ..
ghaṃṭākṣasragdharāṃ durgāṃ raṇāraṃbhe vyavasthitām .. 91 ..
4.1.d:
दानवांस्तर्जयंतीं च खड्गोद्धतकरां शुभाम् ॥
घंटाक्षस्रग्धरां दुर्गां रणारंभे व्यवस्थिताम् ॥ 91 ॥
4.1.m: threatening the Dānavas, her hand raised with a sword, auspicious, / holding a bell and a rosary, Durgā, stationed at the outbreak of battle.

4.1.s: tato jayajayākāraiḥ stavaṃ kuryādimaṃ tataḥ .. 92 ..
4.1.d: ततो जयजयाकारैः स्तवं कुर्यादिमं ततः ॥ 92 ॥
4.1.m: Then, with cries of 'Victory, victory!', he should subsequently utter this hymn of praise:

4.1.s:
sarvamaṅgalamāṅgalye śive sarvārthasādhike ..
śaraṇye tryaṃbake gauri nārāyaṇi namo'stu te .. 93 ..
4.1.d:
सर्वमङ्गलमाङ्गल्ये शिवे सर्वार्थसाधिके ॥
शरण्ये त्र्यंबके गौरि नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 93 ॥
4.1.m: O most auspicious of all auspicious things, O Śivā, accomplisher of all aims, / refuge, three-eyed one, Gauri, Nārāyaṇī, homage to you.

4.1.s:
kuṃkumena samālabdhe candanena vilepite ..
bilvapatrakṛtāmāle durge'haṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ..94..
4.1.d:
कुंकुमेन समालब्धे चन्दनेन विलेपिते ॥
बिल्वपत्रकृतामाले दुर्गेऽहं शरणं गतः ॥94॥
4.1.m: O you who are smeared with saffron, anointed with sandalwood paste, / and adorned with a garland made of bilva leaves, O Durgā, I have come to you for refuge.

4.1.s:
kṛtvaivamarccāṃ kauravya aṣṭamyāṃ jāgaraṃ niśi ..
naṭanartanagītaiśca kārayettu mahotsavam ..95..
4.1.d:
कृत्वैवमर्च्चां कौरव्य अष्टम्यां जागरं निशि ॥
नटनर्तनगीतैश्च कारयेत्तु महोत्सवम् ॥95॥
4.1.m: Having performed this worship, O descendant of Kuru, one should keep a night-vigil on the aṣṭamī / and cause a great festival to be celebrated with actors, dances, and songs.

4.1.s:
evaṃ hṛṣṭairniśāṃ nītvā prabhāte cāruṇodaye ..
pātayenmahiṣānmeṣānagrato natakandharān ..96..
4.1.d:
एवं हृष्टैर्निशां नीत्वा प्रभाते चारुणोदये ॥
पातयेन्महिषान्मेषानग्रतो नतकन्धरान् ॥96॥
4.1.m: Having thus spent the night joyfully, at daybreak when the dawn is rising, / one should slaughter buffaloes and rams before [her], their necks bowed down,

4.1.s:
śataṃ cāpi śatārdhaṃ vā tadarddhaṃ vā yathecchayā ..
surāsavabhṛtaiḥ kuṃbhaistarpayetparameśvarīm .. 97 ..
4.1.d:
शतं चापि शतार्धं वा तदर्द्धं वा यथेच्छया ॥
सुरासवभृतैः कुंभैस्तर्पयेत्परमेश्वरीम् ॥ 97 ॥
4.1.m: a hundred, or fifty, or half of that, according to one's wish; / and with jars filled with spirituous liquor one should gratify Parameśvarī.

4.1.s:
kāpālikebhyastaddeyaṃ dāsīdāsajanaistathā ..
vibhajya sarvaṃ kauṃteya suhṛtsaṃbaṃdhibaṃdhuṣu ..98..
4.1.d:
कापालिकेभ्यस्तद्देयं दासीदासजनैस्तथा ॥
विभज्य सर्वं कौंतेय सुहृत्संबंधिबंधुषु ॥98॥
4.1.m: That should be given to the Kāpālikas, and likewise by the female and male servants, / having distributed it all, O son of Kuntī, among friends, relations, and kinsmen.

4.1.s:
tatoparāhṇasamaye navamyāṃ syaṃdane sthitām ..
bhavānīṃ bhrāmayedrāṣṭre svayaṃ rājā sasainyavān ..99..
4.1.d:
ततोपराह्णसमये नवम्यां स्यंदने स्थिताम् ॥
भवानीं भ्रामयेद्राष्ट्रे स्वयं राजा ससैन्यवान् ॥99॥
4.1.m: Then in the afternoon on the navamī, the king himself, accompanied by his army, / should conduct Bhavānī, mounted on a chariot, in procession through the realm,

4.1.s:
sahasraiḥ puruṣairvāpi rathayuktaiḥ suśikṣitaiḥ ..
śanaiḥ śanairadhikayā dīptyā prajvaladīpakaiḥ ..100..
4.1.d:
सहस्रैः पुरुषैर्वापि रथयुक्तैः सुशिक्षितैः ॥
शनैः शनैरधिकया दीप्त्या प्रज्वलदीपकैः ॥100॥
4.1.m: either with thousands of men, or with well-trained [horses] yoked to the chariot, / moving very slowly, with blazing lamps of intense brightness,

4.1.s:
ākṛṣṭakhaḍgairvīraiśca dhāturaktairgajaistathā ..
nadadbhiḥ śaṃkhapaṭahairnṛtyadbhirvārayauvataiḥ ..
alaṃkṛtābhirnārībhirbālakaiḥ suvibhūṣitaiḥ ..101..
4.1.d:
आकृष्टखड्गैर्वीरैश्च धातुरक्तैर्गजैस्तथा ॥
नदद्भिः शंखपटहैर्नृत्यद्भिर्वारयौवतैः ॥
अलंकृताभिर्नारीभिर्बालकैः सुविभूषितैः ॥101॥
4.1.m: and with heroes with drawn swords, with elephants reddened with mineral pigments, / with sounding conches and kettle-drums, with dancing courtesans, / with adorned women, and with well-decorated children.

4.1.s:
bhūtebhyastu baliṃ dadyānmaṃtreṇānena sāmiṣam ..
saraktaṃ sajalaṃ sānnaṃ gandhapuṣpākṣatairyutam ..1 02..
4.1.d:
भूतेभ्यस्तु बलिं दद्यान्मंत्रेणानेन सामिषम् ॥
सरक्तं सजलं सान्नं गन्धपुष्पाक्षतैर्युतम् ॥1 02॥
4.1.m: One should offer an offering with meat to the ghosts with this mantra, / accompanied by blood, accompanied by water, accompanied by cooked food, and supplied with fragrant perfumes, flowers, and unbroken grains:

4.1.s:
trīṃstrīnvārāṃstriśūlena digvidikṣu kṣipedbalim ..
baliṃ gṛhṇantvimaṃ devā ādityā vasavastathā .. 103 ..
4.1.d:
त्रींस्त्रीन्वारांस्त्रिशूलेन दिग्विदिक्षु क्षिपेद्बलिम् ॥
बलिं गृह्णन्त्विमं देवा आदित्या वसवस्तथा ॥ 103 ॥
4.1.m: Three times each, one should throw the offering in the cardinal and intermediate directions with a trident: / "May the gods, the Ādityas, and likewise the Vasus receive this offering,

4.1.s:
maruto'thāśvinau rudrāḥ suparṇāḥ pannagā grahāḥ ..
asurā yātudhānāśca mātaraśca piśācakāḥ .. 104
4.1.d:
मरुतोऽथाश्विनौ रुद्राः सुपर्णाः पन्नगा ग्रहाः ॥
असुरा यातुधानाश्च मातरश्च पिशाचकाः ॥ 104
4.1.m: as well as the Maruts, the two Aśvins, the Rudras, the birds, the serpents, the planets, / the asuras, the yātudhānas, the mothers, and the piśācas,

4.1.s:
śākinyo yakṣavetālā yoginyaḥ pūtanāḥ śivāḥ ..
jṛṃbhakāḥ siddhagandharvā vyālā vidyādharā dharāḥ.. 105..
4.1.d:
शाकिन्यो यक्षवेताला योगिन्यः पूतनाः शिवाः ॥
जृंभकाः सिद्धगन्धर्वा व्याला विद्याधरा धराः॥ 105॥
4.1.m: the śākinīs, the yakṣas, the vetālas, the yoginīs, the pūtanās, the śivās, / the jṛmbhakas, the siddhas, the gandharvas, the venomous serpents, the vidyādharas, the dharas,

4.1.s:
dikpālā lokapālāśca ye ca vighnavināyakāḥ ..
jagatāṃ śāṃtikartāro brahmādyāśca maharṣayaḥ ..106..
4.1.d:
दिक्पाला लोकपालाश्च ये च विघ्नविनायकाः ॥
जगतां शांतिकर्तारो ब्रह्माद्याश्च महर्षयः ॥106॥
4.1.m: the guardians of the directions, the world protectors, and whichever vināyakas cause obstacles, / the creators of peace for the worlds, and the great sages beginning with Brahmā!

4.1.s:
savighnaṃ mama pāpaṃ te śāmyaṃtu paripanthinaḥ..
saumyā bhavaṃtu tṛptāśca bhūtāḥ pretāḥ sukhāvahāḥ ..107..
ityevaṃ bhrāmayedrāṣṭre durgāṃ devīṃ rathe sthitām..
narayānena vā pārtha tato'vighnaṃ samāpayet ..1 08..
athotpanneṣu vighneṣu bhūtaśāṃtiṃ samācaret ..
yena vighnā na jāyaṃte yātrāsaṃpūrṇatāṃ vrajet..1 09..
evaṃ ye kurvate yātrāṃ rājāno'nye'pi mānavāḥ..
mahānavamyāṃ naṃdāyāṃ putrakā hṛṣṭamānasāḥ ..11 0..
te sarve pāpanirmuktā yāṃti bhāgavatīṃ purīm ..1 11..
4.1.d:
सविघ्नं मम पापं ते शाम्यंतु परिपन्थिनः॥
सौम्या भवंतु तृप्ताश्च भूताः प्रेताः सुखावहाः ॥107॥
इत्येवं भ्रामयेद्राष्ट्रे दुर्गां देवीं रथे स्थिताम्॥
नरयानेन वा पार्थ ततोऽविघ्नं समापयेत् ॥1 08॥
अथोत्पन्नेषु विघ्नेषु भूतशांतिं समाचरेत् ॥
येन विघ्ना न जायंते यात्रासंपूर्णतां व्रजेत्॥1 09॥
एवं ये कुर्वते यात्रां राजानोऽन्येऽपि मानवाः॥
महानवम्यां नंदायां पुत्रका हृष्टमानसाः ॥11 0॥
ते सर्वे पापनिर्मुक्ता यांति भागवतीं पुरीम् ॥1 11॥
4.1.m:
May those adversaries along with obstacles and my sin be pacified; / may the ghosts and pretas be gentle, satisfied, and bringers of happiness!"
In this manner one should lead goddess Durgā in procession through the realm, seated upon a chariot / or upon a palanquin, O son of Pṛthā, and then complete [the rite] without obstacles.
Now, should obstacles arise, one should perform a pacification of spirits, / by which obstacles do not arise and the procession reaches completion.
Those who conduct the procession in this manner, whether kings or other men, / with joyful minds, O son, on the Nandā tithi of Mahānavamī,
all of them, freed from sin, go to the city of the Lord.

4.1.s:
na teṣāṃ śāvakonāgnirna caurā na vināyakāḥ ..
vighnaṃ kurvanti rājendra yeṣāṃ tuṣṭā maheśvarī .. 112 ..
4.1.d:
न तेषां शावकोनाग्निर्न चौरा न विनायकाः ॥
विघ्नं कुर्वन्ति राजेन्द्र येषां तुष्टा महेश्वरी ॥ 112 ॥
4.1.m: Neither child-devouring [spirits] nor fire, neither thieves nor vināyakas / cause an obstacle for those with whom the Great Goddess is pleased, O lord of kings.

4.1.s:
nīrujaḥ sukhino bhogabhoktāro bhayavarjitāḥ..
bhavaṃti bhaktāḥ puruṣāḥ bhagavatyāḥ kimucyate .. 113 ..
4.1.d:
नीरुजः सुखिनो भोगभोक्तारो भयवर्जिताः॥
भवंति भक्ताः पुरुषाः भगवत्याः किमुच्यते ॥ 113 ॥
4.1.m: Healthy, happy, enjoyers of pleasures, and free from fear / do the devoted men of the Goddess become; what more can be said?

4.1.s:
ityeṣa te samākhyāto durgādevyā mahotsavaḥ ..
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva sarvāśubhavināśanaḥ .. 114 ..
4.1.d:
इत्येष ते समाख्यातो दुर्गादेव्या महोत्सवः ॥
पठतां शृण्वतां चैव सर्वाशुभविनाशनः ॥ 114 ॥
4.1.m: Thus has this great festival of goddess Durgā been fully related to you; / for those who recite and hear it, it destroys all misfortune.

4.1.s:
śūlāgrabhinnamahiṣāsurapṛṣṭhaviṣṭāmṛtakhātakhaḍgarucirāṃgadabāhudaṇḍām ..
abhyarcya paṃcavadanānugatāṃ navamyāṃ durgāṃ sudurgagahanāni taraṃti martyāḥ .. 115 ..
4.1.d:
शूलाग्रभिन्नमहिषासुरपृष्ठविष्टामृतखातखड्गरुचिरांगदबाहुदण्डाम् ॥
अभ्यर्च्य पंचवदनानुगतां नवम्यां दुर्गां सुदुर्गगहनानि तरंति मर्त्याः ॥ 115 ॥
4.1.m: Mortals who worship Durgā on the ninth tithi, standing upon the back of Mahiṣāsura pierced by the point of her trident, her armlet-adorned staff-like arm splendid with a sword drawn from its sheath, attended by a lion, cross over the impenetrable difficulties of life.

4.1.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇa uttaraparvaṇi śrīkṛṣṇayudhiṣṭhirasaṃvāde mahānavamīvratavarṇanaṃ
nāmāṣṭatriṃśaduttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ..138..
brahmāṇḍotpattivarṇanam
4.1.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराण उत्तरपर्वणि श्रीकृष्णयुधिष्ठिरसंवादे महानवमीव्रतवर्णनं
नामाष्टत्रिंशदुत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः॥138॥
ब्रह्माण्डोत्पत्तिवर्णनम्
4.1.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-eighth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Mahānavamī Vrata', in the dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Yudhiṣṭhira, in the Uttaraparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa. 138
Description of the Origin of the Cosmic Egg

4.2.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
kasya pratiṣṭhā nirdiṣṭā ko hetuḥ kiṃ parāyaṇam ..
kasminnaitallayaṃ yāti kasmādu tpadyate jagat .. 1 ..
4.2.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
कस्य प्रतिष्ठा निर्दिष्टा को हेतुः किं परायणम् ॥
कस्मिन्नैतल्लयं याति कस्मादु त्पद्यते जगत् ॥ 1 ॥
4.2.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / On what is the foundation declared to rest? What is the cause? What is the final refuge? / Into what does all this dissolve, and from what does the universe arise?

4.2.s:
kati dvīpāḥ samudrāśca kiyaṃto hi kulācalāḥ ..
kiyatpramāṇamavanerbhuvanāni kiyaṃti ca .. 2 ..
4.2.d:
कति द्वीपाः समुद्राश्च कियंतो हि कुलाचलाः ॥
कियत्प्रमाणमवनेर्भुवनानि कियंति च ॥ 2 ॥
4.2.m: How many are the continents and oceans, and how many are the principal mountain ranges? / What is the measure of the earth, and how many are the worlds?

4.2.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
paurāṇaścaiva viṣayo yatpṛṣṭo'haṃ tvayānagha ..
śruto'nubhūtaśca mayā saṃsāre saratā ciram .. 3 ..
4.2.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
पौराणश्चैव विषयो यत्पृष्टोऽहं त्वयानघ ॥
श्रुतोऽनुभूतश्च मया संसारे सरता चिरम् ॥ 3 ॥
4.2.m: The Blessed Kṛṣṇa said: / The matter of the Purāṇas about which I am asked by you, O sinless one, / has been heard and experienced by me while wandering for a long time in saṃsāra.

4.2.s:
ajāya viśvarūpāya nirguṇāya guṇātmane ..
namastasmai bhagavate vāsudevāya vedhase .. 4 ..
4.2.d:
अजाय विश्वरूपाय निर्गुणाय गुणात्मने ॥
नमस्तस्मै भगवते वासुदेवाय वेधसे ॥ 4 ॥
4.2.m: Obeisance to that unborn, all-formed Lord, free from qualities, the self of the qualities, / to Vāsudeva, the creator.

4.2.s:
atra te varṇayiṣyāmi śṛṇu pārtha purātanam ..
yājñavalkyena muninā bhaviṣyaṃ bhāsvatāṃpatiḥ ..
pṛṣṭo yaduttaraṃ prādādṛṣibhyastanmayā śrutam .. 5 ..
4.2.d:
अत्र ते वर्णयिष्यामि शृणु पार्थ पुरातनम् ॥
याज्ञवल्क्येन मुनिना भविष्यं भास्वतांपतिः ॥
पृष्टो यदुत्तरं प्रादादृषिभ्यस्तन्मया श्रुतम् ॥ 5 ॥
4.2.m: Here I shall relate to you the ancient lore, listen, O son of Pṛthā: / when the lord of luminaries was asked by the sage Yājñavalkya about the future, / the reply he gave to the sages—that was heard by me.

4.2.s:
dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ sarvāśubhavināśanam ..
bhaviṣyottarametatte kathayāmi yudhiṣṭhira .. 6 ..
4.2.d:
धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं सर्वाशुभविनाशनम् ॥
भविष्योत्तरमेतत्ते कथयामि युधिष्ठिर ॥ 6 ॥
4.2.m: Auspicious, bringing renown, bestowing long life, destroying all misfortune— / this Bhaviṣyottara I narrate to you, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

4.2.s:
ekātmakaṃ tridaivatyaṃ catuḥpaṃcasulakṣaṇam ..
guṇakālādibhedena sadasatsaṃpradarśitam .. 7 ..
4.2.d:
एकात्मकं त्रिदैवत्यं चतुःपंचसुलक्षणम् ॥
गुणकालादिभेदेन सदसत्संप्रदर्शितम् ॥ 7 ॥
4.2.m: Unified in essence, having three deities, endowed with four and five excellent characteristics, / through divisions of qualities, time, and so forth, the real and the unreal are revealed.

4.2.s:
eka eva jagadyoniḥ pratiyoniṣu saṃsthitaḥ ..
ekadhā bahudhā caiva dṛśyate jalacandravat .. 8 ..
4.2.d:
एक एव जगद्योनिः प्रतियोनिषु संस्थितः ॥
एकधा बहुधा चैव दृश्यते जलचन्द्रवत् ॥ 8 ॥
4.2.m: The single source of the universe resides within each womb; / it is seen as one and as many, like the moon in water.

4.2.s:
brahmā viṣṇurvṛṣāṃkaśca trayo devāḥ satāṃ matāḥ ..
nāmabhedaiḥ kriyābhedairbhidyaṃte nātmanā svayam.. 9 ..
4.2.d:
ब्रह्मा विष्णुर्वृषांकश्च त्रयो देवाः सतां मताः ॥
नामभेदैः क्रियाभेदैर्भिद्यंते नात्मना स्वयम्॥ 9 ॥
4.2.m: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and he whose emblem is the bull are considered the three gods by the virtuous; / they are differentiated by distinctions of name and action, not in their own essence.

4.2.s:
prakriyā cānuṣaṃgaśca upoddhātastathaiva ca ..
upasaṃhāra ityetaccatuṣpādaṃ prakīrtitam .. 4.2.10 ..
4.2.d:
प्रक्रिया चानुषंगश्च उपोद्धातस्तथैव च ॥
उपसंहार इत्येतच्चतुष्पादं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 4.2.10 ॥
4.2.m: The primary creation, the connection, the introduction, and likewise / the conclusion: thus is it proclaimed to have four quarters.

4.2.s:
tarkaśca pratisargaśca vaṃśo manvantarāṇi ca ..
vaṃśānucaritaṃ caiva purāṇaṃ paṃcalakṣaṇam .. 11 ..
4.2.d:
तर्कश्च प्रतिसर्गश्च वंशो मन्वन्तराणि च ॥
वंशानुचरितं चैव पुराणं पंचलक्षणम् ॥ 11 ॥
4.2.m: Original creation, secondary creation, genealogy, the manvantaras, / and the deeds of royal dynasties: [such is] the Purāṇa with its five characteristics.

4.2.s:
eṣa vaktavyaviṣayaḥ sumahānpratibhāti me ..
tathāpyuddeśato vacmi sargaṃ prati tavānagha .. 12 ..
4.2.d:
एष वक्तव्यविषयः सुमहान्प्रतिभाति मे ॥
तथाप्युद्देशतो वच्मि सर्गं प्रति तवानघ ॥ 12 ॥
4.2.m: This subject to be spoken of appears very vast to me; / nonetheless, O sinless one, I shall speak briefly to you concerning creation.

4.2.s:
mahadādiviśeṣāntaṃ savairūpyaṃ salakṣaṇam ..
pañcapramāṇaṃ ṣaṭkakṣaṃ puruṣādhiṣṭhitaṃ jagat.. 13..
4.2.d:
महदादिविशेषान्तं सवैरूप्यं सलक्षणम् ॥
पञ्चप्रमाणं षट्कक्षं पुरुषाधिष्ठितं जगत्॥ 13॥
4.2.m: Beginning with the intellect and ending with the gross elements, possessing diverse forms and distinct characteristics, / having five standards of measurement and six divisions, the universe is presided over by the Puruṣa.

4.2.s:
avyaktājjāyate buddhirmahāniti ca sā smṛtā..
ahaṃkārastu mahatastriguṇaḥ sa ca paṭhyate .. 14 ..
4.2.d:
अव्यक्ताज्जायते बुद्धिर्महानिति च सा स्मृता॥
अहंकारस्तु महतस्त्रिगुणः स च पठ्यते ॥ 14 ॥
4.2.m: From the unmanifest the intellect is born, and it is traditionally known as the Great One; / from the Great One arises the ego, and it is recited as possessing the three qualities.

4.2.s:
tanmātrāṇi ca pañcāhurahaṅkārācca sāttvikāt ..
jātāni tebhyo bhūtāni bhūtebhyaḥ sacarācaram .. 15 ..
4.2.d:
तन्मात्राणि च पञ्चाहुरहङ्काराच्च सात्त्विकात् ॥
जातानि तेभ्यो भूतानि भूतेभ्यः सचराचरम् ॥ 15 ॥
4.2.m: And they say the five subtle elements arise from the sāttvika ego; / from them the gross elements are born, and from the gross elements the animate and inanimate world.

4.2.s:
jalamūrtimaye viṣṇau naṣṭe sthāvarajaṃgame ..
bhūtātmakamabhūdaṇḍaṃ mahattadudakeśayam .. 16 ..
4.2.d:
जलमूर्तिमये विष्णौ नष्टे स्थावरजंगमे ॥
भूतात्मकमभूदण्डं महत्तदुदकेशयम् ॥ 16 ॥
4.2.m: When all that is mobile and immobile had perished in Viṣṇu whose form is water, / a great cosmic egg composed of the elements arose, resting upon the water.

4.2.s:
sṛṣṭyāṃ śaktyā ca nirbhinnaṃ tadaṇḍamabhavaddvidhā ..
bhūkapālamathaikaṃ taddvi tīyamabhavannabhaḥ .. 17 ..
4.2.d:
सृष्ट्यां शक्त्या च निर्भिन्नं तदण्डमभवद्द्विधा ॥
भूकपालमथैकं तद्द्वि तीयमभवन्नभः ॥ 17 ॥
4.2.m: Split into two by power at the time of creation, that egg became two parts: / one skull of the egg became the earth, and the second became the sky.

4.2.s:
ulbaṃ tasyābhavanmerurjarāyuḥ parvatāḥ smṛtāḥ ..
nadyo dhamanyaḥ sañjātāḥ kledaḥ sarvatragaṃ payaḥ .. 18 ..
4.2.d:
उल्बं तस्याभवन्मेरुर्जरायुः पर्वताः स्मृताः ॥
नद्यो धमन्यः सञ्जाताः क्लेदः सर्वत्रगं पयः ॥ 18 ॥
4.2.m: Its amnion became Meru, the chorion is known as the mountains, / the rivers became the blood vessels, and the moisture became the water flowing everywhere.

4.2.s:
yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi ṣoḍaśādhaḥ pratiṣṭhita ..
utsedhe caturāśītirdvātriṃśadūrdhvavistṛtaḥ..
bhūmipaṃkajavistīrṇā karṇikā merurucyate .. 19 ..
4.2.d:
योजनानां सहस्राणि षोडशाधः प्रतिष्ठित ॥
उत्सेधे चतुराशीतिर्द्वात्रिंशदूर्ध्वविस्तृतः॥
भूमिपंकजविस्तीर्णा कर्णिका मेरुरुच्यते ॥ 19 ॥
4.2.m: Resting sixteen thousand yojanas below, / eighty-four [thousand] in height, extended thirty-two [thousand] above, / the pericarp spread out in the lotus of the earth is called Meru.

4.2.s:
ādityaścādidevatvāttatrābhūttriguṇātmakaḥ ..
prātaḥ prajāpatirasau madhyāhne viṣṇuriṣyate ..
rudro'parāhṇasamaye sa evaikastridhāmataḥ .. 4.2.20 ..
4.2.d:
आदित्यश्चादिदेवत्वात्तत्राभूत्त्रिगुणात्मकः ॥
प्रातः प्रजापतिरसौ मध्याह्ने विष्णुरिष्यते ॥
रुद्रोऽपराह्णसमये स एवैकस्त्रिधामतः ॥ 4.2.20 ॥
4.2.m: And the sun, because of being the primal deity, became possessed of the three qualities there: / in the morning he is considered Prajāpati, at midday Viṣṇu, / and at the time of afternoon he is Rudra; that same one is regarded as threefold.

4.2.s:
prātaḥ prajāpaterjātā munayo nava mānavāḥ ..
marīciratryaṃgirasau pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ ..
bhṛgurvaśiṣṭha ityaṣṭau nārado navamaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 21 ..
4.2.d:
प्रातः प्रजापतेर्जाता मुनयो नव मानवाः ॥
मरीचिरत्र्यंगिरसौ पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः ॥
भृगुर्वशिष्ठ इत्यष्टौ नारदो नवमः स्मृतः ॥ 21 ॥
4.2.m: In the morning from Prajāpati were born nine mind-born sages: / Marīci, Atri and Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, / Bhṛgu and Vasiṣṭha—these are the eight, and Nārada is recorded as the ninth.

4.2.s:
nava brahmāṇa ityeṣa purāṇe niścayaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
aṃguṣṭhāddakṣiṇāddakṣaḥ saṃjajñe kamalodbhavāt .. 22 ..
4.2.d:
नव ब्रह्माण इत्येष पुराणे निश्चयः स्मृतः ॥
अंगुष्ठाद्दक्षिणाद्दक्षः संजज्ञे कमलोद्भवात् ॥ 22 ॥
4.2.m: The nine Brahmās—this is the settled conclusion recorded in the Purāṇa. / From the right thumb of the lotus-born [creator] Dakṣa was born;

4.2.s:
vāmā prasūtirudagādaṃguṣṭhāttau ca daṃpatī ..
tābhyāṃ jātāstu tanayā haryaśvāste vināśitāḥ ..
sṛṣṭiṃ prati samudyuktā nāradena mahātmanā ..23..
4.2.d:
वामा प्रसूतिरुदगादंगुष्ठात्तौ च दंपती ॥
ताभ्यां जातास्तु तनया हर्यश्वास्ते विनाशिताः ॥
सृष्टिं प्रति समुद्युक्ता नारदेन महात्मना ॥23॥
4.2.m: from the left thumb Prasūti arose, and those two became husband and wife. / The sons born of those two, the Haryaśvas, / when they were preparing for creation, were ruined by the great-souled Nārada.

4.2.s:
dakṣaḥ kṣīṇānsutānvīkṣya janayāmāsa kanyakāḥ ..
pañcāśaddaśa vikhyātāḥ satyāyā nāmabhiḥ smṛtāḥ .. 24 ..
4.2.d:
दक्षः क्षीणान्सुतान्वीक्ष्य जनयामास कन्यकाः ॥
पञ्चाशद्दश विख्याताः सत्याया नामभिः स्मृताः ॥ 24 ॥
4.2.m: Seeing his sons lost, Dakṣa begot daughters; / sixty famous [daughters] are recorded by the names of the true [one].

4.2.s:
dadau sa daśa dharmāya kaśyapāya trayodaśa ..
kālasya nayane yuktāḥ saptarviśatimiṃdave .. 25 ..
4.2.d:
ददौ स दश धर्माय कश्यपाय त्रयोदश ॥
कालस्य नयने युक्ताः सप्तर्विशतिमिंदवे ॥ 25 ॥
4.2.m: He gave ten to Dharma, thirteen to Kaśyapa, / and twenty-seven, employed in the guiding of time, to the Moon;

4.2.s:
dve prādādbāhuputrāya dve kṛśāśvāya caiva hi ..
rūpayauvanaśālinyaścatasro'riṣṭanemine .. 26 ..
4.2.d:
द्वे प्रादाद्बाहुपुत्राय द्वे कृशाश्वाय चैव हि ॥
रूपयौवनशालिन्यश्चतस्रोऽरिष्टनेमिने ॥ 26 ॥
4.2.m: he gave two to Bahuputra, and indeed two to Kṛśāśva, / and four, endowed with beauty and youth, to Ariṣṭanemi;

4.2.s:
ekāṃ bhṛgorbhavāyaikāṃ prādāttebhyaścarācaraḥ ..
abhavatpuruṣavyāghra bhūtagrāmaścaturvidhaḥ .. 27 ..
4.2.d:
एकां भृगोर्भवायैकां प्रादात्तेभ्यश्चराचरः ॥
अभवत्पुरुषव्याघ्र भूतग्रामश्चतुर्विधः ॥ 27 ॥
4.2.m: he gave one to Bhṛgu and one to Bhava; from them the animate and inanimate, / the fourfold aggregate of living beings, came into being, O tiger among men.

4.2.s:
vairājamatha vaikuṇṭhaṃ kelāsamiti nāmataḥ ..
meroḥ śṛṃgatrayaṃ mūrdhni brahmaviṣṇuśivālayam .. 28 ..
4.2.d:
वैराजमथ वैकुण्ठं केलासमिति नामतः ॥
मेरोः शृंगत्रयं मूर्ध्नि ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवालयम् ॥ 28 ॥
4.2.m:
The three peaks upon the summit of Meru, known by name
as Vairāja, Vaikuṇṭha, and Kailāsa, are the abodes of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.

4.2.s:
prācīdikkramayogena teṣāṃ pārśve puraḥ smṛtāḥ ..
indrādilokapālānāṃ divyaiḥ svarllakṣaṇairyutāḥ .. 29 ..
4.2.d:
प्राचीदिक्क्रमयोगेन तेषां पार्श्वे पुरः स्मृताः ॥
इन्द्रादिलोकपालानां दिव्यैः स्वर्ल्लक्षणैर्युताः ॥ 29 ॥
4.2.m:
Beside them, in order from the eastern direction, are recorded the cities
of the world protectors, Indra and the rest, endowed with heavenly characteristics.

4.2.s:
himavānhemakūṭaśca niṣadho merureva ca ..
nīlaḥ śvetastathā śṛṃgī jambūdvīpe kulācalāḥ ..
jambūdvīpapramāṇena sahasraguṇitaṃ śatam .. 4.2.30 ..
4.2.d:
हिमवान्हेमकूटश्च निषधो मेरुरेव च ॥
नीलः श्वेतस्तथा शृंगी जम्बूद्वीपे कुलाचलाः ॥
जम्बूद्वीपप्रमाणेन सहस्रगुणितं शतम् ॥ 4.2.30 ॥
4.2.m:
Himavān, Hemakūṭa, Niṣadha, and Meru,
Nīla, Śveta, and Śṛṅgin are the clan mountains in Jambūdvīpa.
The extent of Jambūdvīpa is a hundred multiplied by a thousand [yojanas].

4.2.s:
bhidyate navadhā so'pi varṣabhedena bhārata ..
jambūśākakuśakrauñcaśālmagomeda puṣkarāḥ ..
dvīpāḥ sapta samākhyātāḥ samudre saptabhirvṛtāḥ .. 31 ..
4.2.d:
भिद्यते नवधा सोऽपि वर्षभेदेन भारत ॥
जम्बूशाककुशक्रौञ्चशाल्मगोमेद पुष्कराः ॥
द्वीपाः सप्त समाख्याताः समुद्रे सप्तभिर्वृताः ॥ 31 ॥
4.2.m:
It is divided ninefold, O Bhārata, by the division of realms.
Jambū, Śāka, Kuśa, Krauñca, Śālmalī, Gomeda, and Puṣkara—
these are declared to be the seven continents, encircled by seven oceans:

4.2.s:
kṣārakṣīrekṣusurayā dadhnā caiva ghṛtena ca ..
svādūdakena ca bhṛtairdviguṇairdviguṇaista thā ..32..
4.2.d:
क्षारक्षीरेक्षुसुरया दध्ना चैव घृतेन च ॥
स्वादूदकेन च भृतैर्द्विगुणैर्द्विगुणैस्त था ॥32॥
4.2.m:
filled with salt water, milk, sugarcane juice, liquor, curds, clarified butter,
and sweet water, each [ocean and continent] twice the size of the preceding.

4.2.s:
bhūrloko'tha bhuvarlokaḥ svarmaharjjana ityapi ..
tapaḥ satyaśca kathitāḥ pārtha sapta surālayāḥ .. 33 ..
4.2.d:
भूर्लोकोऽथ भुवर्लोकः स्वर्महर्ज्जन इत्यपि ॥
तपः सत्यश्च कथिताः पार्थ सप्त सुरालयाः ॥ 33 ॥
4.2.m:
Bhūrloka, Bhuvarloka, Svar, Mahar, and Janas,
Tapas, and Satya—these seven abodes of the gods are declared, O son of Pṛthā.

4.2.s:
mahātalo bhūmitalaḥ sutalo vitala stataḥ ..
rasātalaśca vijñeyaḥ saptamaśca talātalaḥ ..34..
4.2.d:
महातलो भूमितलः सुतलो वितल स्ततः ॥
रसातलश्च विज्ञेयः सप्तमश्च तलातलः ॥34॥
4.2.m:
Mahātala, Bhūmitala, Sutala, then Vitala,
Rasātala is to be known, and Talātala as the seventh.

4.2.s:
hiraṇyākṣaprabhṛtayo dānavendrā mahoragāḥ..
vasaṃtyeteṣu kaunteya siddhāśca ṛṣayaśca ye ..35..
4.2.d:
हिरण्याक्षप्रभृतयो दानवेन्द्रा महोरगाः॥
वसंत्येतेषु कौन्तेय सिद्धाश्च ऋषयश्च ये ॥35॥
4.2.m:
In these dwell the lords of Dānavas beginning with Hiraṇyākṣa, great serpents,
and those who are siddhas and ṛṣis, O son of Kuntī.

4.2.s:
svāyaṃbhuvo manuḥ pūrvaṃ tataḥ svārociṣo'bhavat ..
uttamastāmasaścaiva raivataścākṣuṣeti ṣaṭ ..36..
4.2.d:
स्वायंभुवो मनुः पूर्वं ततः स्वारोचिषोऽभवत् ॥
उत्तमस्तामसश्चैव रैवतश्चाक्षुषेति षट् ॥36॥
4.2.m:
First was Svāyambhuva Manu; after him came Svārociṣa,
Uttama, Tāmasa, Raivata, and Cākṣuṣa—these six.

4.2.s:
vaivasvato'yamadhunā vartate manuruttamaḥ ..
yasya putraiḥ prapautraiśca vibhakteyaṃ vasundharā .. 37 ..
4.2.d:
वैवस्वतोऽयमधुना वर्तते मनुरुत्तमः ॥
यस्य पुत्रैः प्रपौत्रैश्च विभक्तेयं वसुन्धरा ॥ 37 ॥
4.2.m:
Presently reigns this excellent Manu Vaivasvata,
by whose sons and grandsons this earth has been divided.

4.2.s:
ādityā vasavo rudrā ekādaśa tathāśvinau ..
uṣastrayaḥ samākhyātā deva vaivasvateṃ'tare .. 38 ..
4.2.d:
आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा एकादश तथाश्विनौ ॥
उषस्त्रयः समाख्याता देव वैवस्वतेंऽतरे ॥ 38 ॥
4.2.m:
The Ādityas, the Vasus, the eleven Rudras, and the two Aśvins,
these three [classes of gods] are declared, O king, in the Vaivasvata period.

4.2.s:
vipracittihiraṇyākhyau daityadānavasattamau ..
tayorvaṃśe tu bahavo daityadānavasattamāḥ .. 39 ..
4.2.d:
विप्रचित्तिहिरण्याख्यौ दैत्यदानवसत्तमौ ॥
तयोर्वंशे तु बहवो दैत्यदानवसत्तमाः ॥ 39 ॥
4.2.m:
Vipracitti and Hiraṇya are the two foremost among Daityas and Dānavas;
in their lineages are many foremost Daityas and Dānavas.

4.2.s:
pañcāśadguṇitakoṭiyojanānāṃ mahattayā ..
saptadvīpasamudrāyāḥ pramāṇamavaneḥ smṛtam .. 4.2.40 ..
4.2.d:
पञ्चाशद्गुणितकोटियोजनानां महत्तया ॥
सप्तद्वीपसमुद्रायाः प्रमाणमवनेः स्मृतम् ॥ 4.2.40 ॥
4.2.m:
By a magnitude of fifty multiplied by a crore of yojanas
is recorded the extent of the earth containing the seven continents and oceans.

4.2.s:
piṇḍena ca sahasrāṇi saptatirjalamadhyataḥ ..
gaurivaiṣā sumahatī bhrājate na ca līyate .. 41 ..
4.2.d:
पिण्डेन च सहस्राणि सप्ततिर्जलमध्यतः ॥
गौरिवैषा सुमहती भ्राजते न च लीयते ॥ 41 ॥
4.2.m:
And in mass, seventy thousand [yojanas] amidst the waters;
like a cow, this very vast [earth] shines forth and does not dissolve.

4.2.s:
lokā lokaḥ parataraḥ parvato'gramahocchrayaḥ ..
dvaitamarthaṃ sa niyato yo'sau ravirucāmapi .. 42 ..
4.2.d:
लोका लोकः परतरः पर्वतोऽग्रमहोच्छ्रयः ॥
द्वैतमर्थं स नियतो योऽसौ रविरुचामपि ॥ 42 ॥
4.2.m:
Beyond lies the mountain Lokāloka, of supreme height;
it is fixed as the boundary for the light of the sun itself.

4.2.s:
naimittikaḥ prākṛtikastathaivātyantiko layaḥ ...
nityaścaturtho vijñeyaḥ kālo nityāpahārakaḥ .. 43 ..
4.2.d:
नैमित्तिकः प्राकृतिकस्तथैवात्यन्तिको लयः ॥।
नित्यश्चतुर्थो विज्ञेयः कालो नित्यापहारकः ॥ 43 ॥
4.2.m:
Occasional dissolution, elemental dissolution, and likewise absolute dissolution;
a fourth is to be known as continuous, for Time is the continuous snatcher away.

4.2.s:
utpadyate svayaṃ yasmāttattasminneva līyate ..
rakṣati ca pare puṃsi bhūtānāmeva niścayaḥ .. .. 44 ..
4.2.d:
उत्पद्यते स्वयं यस्मात्तत्तस्मिन्नेव लीयते ॥
रक्षति च परे पुंसि भूतानामेव निश्चयः ॥ ॥ 44 ॥
4.2.m:
That from which [a thing] arises of itself dissolves into that very thing;
and it is preserved in the Supreme Person—such is the certainty regarding created beings.

4.2.s:
yathartāvṛtuliṅgāni nānārūpāṇi paryaye ..
dṛśyaṃte tāni tānyeva tathā bhāvā yugādiṣu .. 45 ..
4.2.d:
यथर्तावृतुलिङ्गानि नानारूपाणि पर्यये ॥
दृश्यंते तानि तान्येव तथा भावा युगादिषु ॥ 45 ॥
4.2.m:
Just as in season, the various signs of the seasons
are seen again and again in their turn, so are conditions at the beginning of the yugas.

4.2.s:
pratilīneṣu bhūteṣu vibuddhaḥ sakalaṃ jagat ..
vedaśabdebhya evādau nirmame sa maheśvaraḥ .. 46 ..
4.2.d:
प्रतिलीनेषु भूतेषु विबुद्धः सकलं जगत् ॥
वेदशब्देभ्य एवादौ निर्ममे स महेश्वरः ॥ 46 ॥
4.2.m:
When created beings have dissolved, that Great Lord, awoken,
fashioned the entire universe in the beginning from the words of the Veda alone.

4.2.s:
hiṃsrāhiṃsre mṛdukrūre dharmādharmāvṛtānṛte ..
te taṃ vinā prapadyaṃte punasteṣveva karma su .. 47 ..
4.2.d:
हिंस्राहिंस्रे मृदुक्रूरे धर्माधर्मावृतानृते ॥
ते तं विना प्रपद्यंते पुनस्तेष्वेव कर्म सु ॥ 47 ॥
4.2.m:
Violence and non-violence, gentle and cruel, righteousness and unrighteousness, truth and falsehood:
without Him, they return again to those very deeds.

4.2.s:
bhūrdaśaguṇena payasā saṃvṛtā tacca tejasā ..
tejo'nilena nabhasā tadguṇenānilo vṛtaḥ .. 48 ..
4.2.d:
भूर्दशगुणेन पयसा संवृता तच्च तेजसा ॥
तेजोऽनिलेन नभसा तद्गुणेनानिलो वृतः ॥ 48 ॥
4.2.m:
The earth is surrounded by ten times [as much] water, and that by fire;
fire by wind, and wind is surrounded by an equal measure of space;

4.2.s:
bhūtādinā tathākāśaṃ bhūtādirmahatāvṛtaḥ..
mahānparivṛtastena puruṣeṇāvināśinā ..49..
4.2.d:
भूतादिना तथाकाशं भूतादिर्महतावृतः॥
महान्परिवृतस्तेन पुरुषेणाविनाशिना ॥49॥
4.2.m:
space likewise by the origin of elements, and the origin of elements is surrounded by the intellect;
the intellect is surrounded by that imperishable Person.

4.2.s:
evaṃ vidhānāmaṇḍānāṃ sahasrāṇi śatāni ca ..
utpannāni vinaṣṭāni bhāvitāni mahātmanā .. 4.2.50 ..
4.2.d:
एवं विधानामण्डानां सहस्राणि शतानि च ॥
उत्पन्नानि विनष्टानि भावितानि महात्मना ॥ 4.2.50 ॥
4.2.m:
Hundreds and thousands of such cosmic eggs
have been generated, destroyed, and manifested by the Great Self.

4.2.s:
vaikuṇṭhakoṣṭhagatametadaśeṣatāyāṃ khyātaṃ jagatsuranaroragasiddhanaddham ..
paśyaṃti śuddhamunayo bahiraṃtare ca māyā carācaraguroraparaiva kācit .. 51 ..
māyādarśanavarṇanam
4.2.d:
वैकुण्ठकोष्ठगतमेतदशेषतायां ख्यातं जगत्सुरनरोरगसिद्धनद्धम् ॥
पश्यंति शुद्धमुनयो बहिरंतरे च माया चराचरगुरोरपरैव काचित् ॥ 51 ॥
मायादर्शनवर्णनम्
4.2.m:
Remaining within the chamber of Vaikuṇṭha, this entire renowned universe,
bound with gods, men, serpents, and siddhas, pure sages perceive outside and inside;
yet the Māyā of the Guru of the moving and unmoving is something quite different.
Description of the Vision of Māyā

4.3.s:
.. yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ..
kīdṛśī kṛṣṇa sā māyā viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ ..
yayā vyāmohitaṃ yacca jagadetaccarācaram .. 1 ..
4.3.d:
॥ युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥
कीदृशी कृष्ण सा माया विष्णोरमिततेजसः ॥
यया व्यामोहितं यच्च जगदेतच्चराचरम् ॥ 1 ॥
4.3.m:
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
Of what sort, O Kṛṣṇa, is that Māyā of Viṣṇu of immeasurable splendour,
by which this world, moving and unmoving, is deluded?

4.3.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
yena dvīpe purā viṣṇurāste cakragadādharaḥ ..
vāsudevaḥ sagaruḍaḥ sacakraśca śriyā saha .. 2 ..
4.3.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
येन द्वीपे पुरा विष्णुरास्ते चक्रगदाधरः ॥
वासुदेवः सगरुडः सचक्रश्च श्रिया सह ॥ 2 ॥
4.3.m:
The venerable Kṛṣṇa said:
Formerly, on the island where Viṣṇu resides, bearing discus and mace,
as Vāsudeva with Garuḍa, with discus, and together with Śrī,

4.3.s:
nīlotpaladalaśyāmaḥ kuṃḍalābhyāṃ vibhūṣitaḥ ..
bhrājate mukuṭoddyotakeyūravanamālayā .. 3 ..
4.3.d:
नीलोत्पलदलश्यामः कुंडलाभ्यां विभूषितः ॥
भ्राजते मुकुटोद्द्योतकेयूरवनमालया ॥ 3 ॥
4.3.m:
dark as the petal of a blue lotus, adorned with two earrings,
he shines with the radiance of a diadem, armlets, and a forest garland.

4.3.s:
tasya draṣṭumathābhyāgānnārado munisattamaḥ ..
praṇamya stutibhirddevaṃ prāhedaṃ vismayānvitaḥ .. 4 ..
4.3.d:
तस्य द्रष्टुमथाभ्यागान्नारदो मुनिसत्तमः ॥
प्रणम्य स्तुतिभिर्द्देवं प्राहेदं विस्मयान्वितः ॥ 4 ॥
4.3.m:
Then Nārada, the best of sages, came to see him;
having bowed to the god with praises, filled with wonder, he said this:

4.3.s:
saṃśayaṃ paripṛcchāmi bhagavanvaktumarhasi ..
kā māyā kīdṛśī māyā kiṃrūpā ca kutastathā .. 5 ..
4.3.d:
संशयं परिपृच्छामि भगवन्वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
का माया कीदृशी माया किंरूपा च कुतस्तथा ॥ 5 ॥
4.3.m:
I ask about a doubt, O Blessed One; you ought to speak:
What is Māyā? Of what sort is Māyā? What form has it, and whence does it come?

4.3.s:
tasyā darśaya me rūpaṃ māyāyāḥ puruṣottama ..
yā ca mohayate sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram .. 6 ..
4.3.d:
तस्या दर्शय मे रूपं मायायाः पुरुषोत्तम ॥
या च मोहयते सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥ 6 ॥
4.3.m:
Show me the form of that Māyā, O Supreme Person,
which deludes the entire three worlds, moving and unmoving,

4.3.s:
ābrahmastaṃbaparyaṃtaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam ..
vaikuṃṭhaṃ vāsudevaṃ ca prasādaṃ kartumarhasi .. 7 ..
4.3.d:
आब्रह्मस्तंबपर्यंतं सदेवासुरमानुषम् ॥
वैकुंठं वासुदेवं च प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि ॥ 7 ॥
4.3.m:
from Brahmā down to a clump of grass, together with gods, asuras, and humans;
O Vaikuṇṭha, O Vāsudeva, be pleased to grant this favour!

4.3.s:
evamuktastu muninā devadevo janārdanaḥ ..
prahasyovāca devarṣe na kāryaṃ māyayā tvayā .. 8 ..
4.3.d:
एवमुक्तस्तु मुनिना देवदेवो जनार्दनः ॥
प्रहस्योवाच देवर्षे न कार्यं मायया त्वया ॥ 8 ॥
4.3.m:
Thus addressed by the sage, Janārdana, the god of gods,
laughed and said: 'O divine sage, you have no need of Māyā.'

4.3.s:
bhūyo'pi mohayāmāsa somagrāheṇa nāradam ..
nāradopi mahārāja provācedaṃ punaḥ punaḥ .. 9 ..
4.3.d:
भूयोऽपि मोहयामास सोमग्राहेण नारदम् ॥
नारदोपि महाराज प्रोवाचेदं पुनः पुनः ॥ 9 ॥
4.3.m:
He further deluded Nārada with the grasping of soma;
and Nārada, O great king, spoke this again and again:

4.3.s:
māyāṃ darśaya me deva nānyadasti prayojanam ..
athāsau viṣṇurutthāya śvetadvīpaṃ punaryayau .. 4.3.10 ..
4.3.d:
मायां दर्शय मे देव नान्यदस्ति प्रयोजनम् ॥
अथासौ विष्णुरुत्थाय श्वेतद्वीपं पुनर्ययौ ॥ 4.3.10 ॥
4.3.m:
'Show me Māyā, O Lord; there is no other purpose.'
Then that Viṣṇu, having arisen, went again to Śvetadvīpa,

4.3.s:
aḍulyagreṇa saṃgṛhya nāradaṃ muni puṅgavam ..
tato mārgagataścakre ātmānaṃ dvijarūpiṇam .. 11 ..
4.3.d:
अडुल्यग्रेण संगृह्य नारदं मुनि पुङ्गवम् ॥
ततो मार्गगतश्चक्रे आत्मानं द्विजरूपिणम् ॥ 11 ॥
4.3.m:
taking Nārada, the foremost among sages, by the tip of his finger.
Then, having set out on the road, he made himself take the form of a twice-born;

4.3.s:
ṛgvedasadṛśaḥ sākṣādviṣṇurbrahmavadāsthitaḥ ..
