vṛddhadvijottamavapuḥ saṃśayo nālpako bhavat .. 12 ..
4.3.d:
ऋग्वेदसदृशः साक्षाद्विष्णुर्ब्रह्मवदास्थितः ॥
वृद्धद्विजोत्तमवपुः संशयो नाल्पको भवत् ॥ 12 ॥
4.3.m:
resembling the Ṛgveda in visible form, Viṣṇu stood like Brahmā,
in the body of an aged, foremost twice-born; no small doubt arose.

4.3.s:
śikhī kamaṃḍaludhṛto mṛgacarmopavītakaḥ ..
yajñaśarmeti saṃjñāṃ ca cakre'sāvātmanaḥ prabhuḥ .. 13 ..
4.3.d:
शिखी कमंडलुधृतो मृगचर्मोपवीतकः ॥
यज्ञशर्मेति संज्ञां च चक्रेऽसावात्मनः प्रभुः ॥ 13 ॥
4.3.m:
Possessing a tuft of hair, carrying a water pot, wearing an antelope skin and sacred thread,
the Lord gave himself the name Yajñaśarman;

4.3.s:
kṛtvāpi kuśataṃtvagrapavitrakṛta lakṣaṇam..
āyayau sa mahīpṛṣṭhe jambūdvīpaṃ cacāra ha .. 14 ..
4.3.d:
कृत्वापि कुशतंत्वग्रपवित्रकृत लक्षणम्॥
आययौ स महीपृष्ठे जम्बूद्वीपं चचार ह ॥ 14 ॥
4.3.m:
and having made the mark of a purifying ring of kuśa grass tips,
he came upon the surface of the earth and roamed Jambūdvīpa.

4.3.s:
vaidiśaṃ nāma nagaraṃ vetravatyāstaṭe śubham ..
tasminsadodyamaparo dhanadhānyasa mṛddhimān .. 15 ..
4.3.d:
वैदिशं नाम नगरं वेत्रवत्यास्तटे शुभम् ॥
तस्मिन्सदोद्यमपरो धनधान्यस मृद्धिमान् ॥ 15 ॥
4.3.m:
There is an auspicious city named Vaidiśa on the bank of the Vetravatī;
in it, always intent on exertion, rich in wealth and grain,

4.3.s:
gomahiṣyajasaṃpūrṇaṃ pāśupālyena saṃsthitaḥ ..
halakarmavṛṣāsakto vaiśyajātiraniṃditaḥ .. 16 ..
4.3.d:
गोमहिष्यजसंपूर्णं पाशुपाल्येन संस्थितः ॥
हलकर्मवृषासक्तो वैश्यजातिरनिंदितः ॥ 16 ॥
4.3.m:
abounding in cows, buffaloes, and goats, living by animal husbandry,
attached to the work of the plough and oxen, blameless of the vaiśya caste,

4.3.s:
gṛhakarmaṇi tanniṣṭhaḥ sīrabhadra iti smṛtaḥ ..
tasyāṃtike hariḥ sākṣānnāradena sahāgataḥ .. 17 ..
4.3.d:
गृहकर्मणि तन्निष्ठः सीरभद्र इति स्मृतः ॥
तस्यांतिके हरिः साक्षान्नारदेन सहागतः ॥ 17 ॥
4.3.m:
devoted to domestic duties, known as Sīrabhadra [dwelt there].
Hari came into his presence in visible form together with Nārada.

4.3.s:
tenāpyāsanasanmānaiḥ samarthena kṛtādarau ..
proktaṃ kenātha kiṃ tubhyaṃ sādhyamannaṃ na sādhyate .. 18 ..
4.3.d:
तेनाप्यासनसन्मानैः समर्थेन कृतादरौ ॥
प्रोक्तं केनाथ किं तुभ्यं साध्यमन्नं न साध्यते ॥ 18 ॥
4.3.m:
And honoured by him who was capable [of hospitality] with seats and respects,
it was said: 'By whom and what should be accomplished for you? Is cooked food not to be prepared?'

4.3.s:
na vāsmadīyaṃ yuṣmākaṃ rocatennaṃ tato hariḥ ..
prahasya pradadau tasmai varaṃ dvijavaro mahat .. 19 ..
4.3.d:
न वास्मदीयं युष्माकं रोचतेन्नं ततो हरिः ॥
प्रहस्य प्रददौ तस्मै वरं द्विजवरो महत् ॥ 19 ॥
4.3.m: "Or does our food not please you?" Then Hari, / laughing, granted him, best of the twice-born, a great boon.

4.3.s:
unnāmya vaktraṃ covāca devasaṃstutayā girā ..
saṃtu te bahavaḥ putrāḥ kṣetravyāpārabuddhayaḥ .. 4.3.20 ..
4.3.d:
उन्नाम्य वक्त्रं चोवाच देवसंस्तुतया गिरा ॥
संतु ते बहवः पुत्राः क्षेत्रव्यापारबुद्धयः ॥ 4.3.20 ॥
4.3.m: Lifting his face, he spoke with a voice praised by the gods: / "May you have many sons whose minds are intent on working the fields,

4.3.s:
paśupāśagṛhāsaktāḥ śatārddhabalavāhanāḥ ..
teṣāṃ putrāśca pautrāśca kṛṣi vṛddhipravarddhakāḥ .. 21 ..
4.3.d:
पशुपाशगृहासक्ताः शतार्द्धबलवाहनाः ॥
तेषां पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च कृषि वृद्धिप्रवर्द्धकाः ॥ 21 ॥
4.3.m: devoted to their house, herds, and tethers, possessing fifty forces and mounts; / and may their sons and grandsons continually foster the increase of agriculture.

4.3.s:
tvañca vṛttiśatairnnityaṃ varddhasva svajanāvṛtaḥ ..
ityuktvā sa jagannātho vāsudevaḥ sanāradaḥ .. 22 ..
4.3.d:
त्वञ्च वृत्तिशतैर्न्नित्यं वर्द्धस्व स्वजनावृतः ॥
इत्युक्त्वा स जगन्नाथो वासुदेवः सनारदः ॥ 22 ॥
4.3.m: And may you ever prosper through a hundred livelihoods, surrounded by your kinsmen." / Having spoken thus, that lord of the universe, Vāsudeva, accompanied by Nārada,

4.3.s:
kṣetre gosvāmināmānaṃ dvijaṃ dadṛśatuśca tau..
daridraṃ halakarmārttaṃ methyādyopaskarārditam .. 23 ..
4.3.d:
क्षेत्रे गोस्वामिनामानं द्विजं ददृशतुश्च तौ॥
दरिद्रं हलकर्मार्त्तं मेथ्याद्योपस्करार्दितम् ॥ 23 ॥
4.3.m: in a field, the two of them saw a twice-born man named Gosvāmin, / poor, afflicted by ploughing, distressed by farming implements such as the threshing post,

4.3.s:
bhāgīrathyāstaṭe ramye veṇikāgrāmasannidhau ..
tṛṇagulmalatācchannakṣetre ciṃtākulo hi saḥ .. 24 ..
4.3.d:
भागीरथ्यास्तटे रम्ये वेणिकाग्रामसन्निधौ ॥
तृणगुल्मलताच्छन्नक्षेत्रे चिंताकुलो हि सः ॥ 24 ॥
4.3.m: on the charming bank of the Bhāgīrathī near the village of Veṇikā, / anxious indeed in a field overgrown with grass, bushes, and creepers.

4.3.s:
tābhyāṃ saṃprārthito vipro bhojyaṃ prādācca kiṃcana ..
sakāśaṃ tava saṃprāptau dūrādatithidharmiṇau .. 25 ..
4.3.d:
ताभ्यां संप्रार्थितो विप्रो भोज्यं प्रादाच्च किंचन ॥
सकाशं तव संप्राप्तौ दूरादतिथिधर्मिणौ ॥ 25 ॥
4.3.m: Requested by the two of them, the brāhmaṇa gave some food: / "You two observant of the duties of guests have arrived in your presence from afar."

4.3.s:
ityukto'sau dvijaśreṣṭho halakarma vidhāya tat ..
ājagāma gṛhaṃ tūrṇaṃ tābhyāṃ saha sasaṃbhramam .. 26 ..
4.3.d:
इत्युक्तोऽसौ द्विजश्रेष्ठो हलकर्म विधाय तत् ॥
आजगाम गृहं तूर्णं ताभ्यां सह ससंभ्रमम् ॥ 26 ॥
4.3.m: Having been spoken to thus, that best of the twice-born left off that work of the plough / and went home quickly with the two of them in great haste.

4.3.s:
cakre caivādaraṃ bhaktyā svayamāsanasatkriyām ..
pādaśaucaṃ tathābhyaṃgaṃ kṛtvātra ca susaṃskṛtam .. 27 ..
4.3.d:
चक्रे चैवादरं भक्त्या स्वयमासनसत्क्रियाम् ॥
पादशौचं तथाभ्यंगं कृत्वात्र च सुसंस्कृतम् ॥ 27 ॥
4.3.m: And with devotion he himself showed honor and hospitality with a seat; / having performed the washing of their feet and anointment with oil, well-refined here,

4.3.s:
saha patnyā satanayo bhojyaṃ bhuktiṃ cakāra saḥ ..
bhuktabhojyau ca śarvaryāṃ sukhaṃ suptau niśātyaye..28..
4.3.d:
सह पत्न्या सतनयो भोज्यं भुक्तिं चकार सः ॥
भुक्तभोज्यौ च शर्वर्यां सुखं सुप्तौ निशात्यये॥28॥
4.3.m: together with his wife and son, he served food and ate. / And having partaken of food, they slept comfortably during the night; at the end of the night,

4.3.s:
prayātau dadatuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ varaṃ tasmai dvijātaye ..
mā te bhavatu gosvāminkadācidapi karṣaṇam .. 29 ..
4.3.d:
प्रयातौ ददतुः श्रेष्ठं वरं तस्मै द्विजातये ॥
मा ते भवतु गोस्वामिन्कदाचिदपि कर्षणम् ॥ 29 ॥
4.3.m: as they set out, they granted an excellent boon to that twice-born man: / "O Gosvāmin, may ploughing never be yours at any time;

4.3.s:
mā dhānyaṃ makhasaṃtāna matprasādādvijottama ..
ityuktvā jagmatustūrṇaṃ punaḥ papraccha nāradaḥ..4.3.30..
4.3.d:
मा धान्यं मखसंतान मत्प्रसादाद्विजोत्तम ॥
इत्युक्त्वा जग्मतुस्तूर्णं पुनः पप्रच्छ नारदः॥4.3.30॥
4.3.m: nor may grain or offspring for sacrifice [be yours], O best of the twice-born, through my grace." / Having spoken thus, they departed swiftly. Again Nārada asked:

4.3.s:
kimidaṃ vada deveśa śāparūpo varastvayā ..
bhadra gosvāmine dattaḥ kiṃ ca vaiśye tathāvidhaḥ..31..
4.3.d:
किमिदं वद देवेश शापरूपो वरस्त्वया ॥
भद्र गोस्वामिने दत्तः किं च वैश्ये तथाविधः॥31॥
4.3.m: "Tell me, O Lord of the gods, what is this boon in the form of a curse / that has been granted by you to the worthy Gosvāmin, and of such a kind to the vaiśya?"

4.3.s:
ityuktaḥ prāha deveśaḥ śṛṇu nārada madvacaḥ ..
paramārthaṃ pravakṣye'haṃ tava saṃśayakartanam .. 32 ..
4.3.d:
इत्युक्तः प्राह देवेशः शृणु नारद मद्वचः ॥
परमार्थं प्रवक्ष्येऽहं तव संशयकर्तनम् ॥ 32 ॥
4.3.m: Thus addressed, the Lord of the gods said: "Listen, O Nārada, to my words; / I shall declare the ultimate truth, cutting away your doubt.

4.3.s:
saṃvatsareṇa yatpāpaṃ matsyaghātī samācaret ..
tadahne kena kurute lāṃgalī nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 33 ..
4.3.d:
संवत्सरेण यत्पापं मत्स्यघाती समाचरेत् ॥
तदह्ने केन कुरुते लांगली नात्र संशयः ॥ 33 ॥
4.3.m: Whatever sin a killer of fish might commit in a year, / a ploughman commits in a single day; of this there is no doubt.

4.3.s:
ato'rthaṃ kṛṣipālyena narakaṃ yāti lāṃgalī ..
tadabhāvānna kalpaḥ syāttena mokṣo mayi dhruvam .. 34 ..
4.3.d:
अतोऽर्थं कृषिपाल्येन नरकं याति लांगली ॥
तदभावान्न कल्पः स्यात्तेन मोक्षो मयि ध्रुवम् ॥ 34 ॥
4.3.m: Therefore, through the maintenance of farming, the ploughman goes to hell; / in the absence of that, there would be no such course; therefore, liberation in me is certain.

4.3.s:
mayi bhukte prasanne vā ko viśeṣo'sya nārada ..
yadi svargo'tha vā mokṣo na saṃpadyeta tadvṛthā .. 35..
4.3.d:
मयि भुक्ते प्रसन्ने वा को विशेषोऽस्य नारद ॥
यदि स्वर्गोऽथ वा मोक्षो न संपद्येत तद्वृथा ॥ 35॥
4.3.m: When I have eaten or am pleased, what is the distinction for him, O Nārada, / if heaven or liberation is not attained? Then it is in vain.

4.3.s:
idānīṃ halakāluṣyaiḥ sīrabhadro viceṣṭitaiḥ ..
bahupāpaprasaṃgena ghoraṃ narakameṣyati .. 36 ..
4.3.d:
इदानीं हलकालुष्यैः सीरभद्रो विचेष्टितैः ॥
बहुपापप्रसंगेन घोरं नरकमेष्यति ॥ 36 ॥
4.3.m: Now, because of the taints of the plough through his deeds, / through connection with many sins, Sīrabhadra will go to a terrible hell.

4.3.s:
saputrapautrasaṃtāno hṛtorthastadgṛhe mayā ..
na bhuktaṃ na ca viśrāntaṃ viśrāṃtaṃ dvijaveśmani .. 37 ..
4.3.d:
सपुत्रपौत्रसंतानो हृतोर्थस्तद्गृहे मया ॥
न भुक्तं न च विश्रान्तं विश्रांतं द्विजवेश्मनि ॥ 37 ॥
4.3.m: Along with the lineage of his sons and grandsons, his wealth was taken away by me; / in his house nothing was eaten, nor was rest taken; rest was taken in the house of the [other] twice-born man.

4.3.s:
so'pi dvijo muniśreṣṭha saṃsārāduttariṣyati ..
ityevaṃ saṃvadaṃtau ca jagmaturmārgamuttamam .. 38 ..
4.3.d:
सोऽपि द्विजो मुनिश्रेष्ठ संसारादुत्तरिष्यति ॥
इत्येवं संवदंतौ च जग्मतुर्मार्गमुत्तमम् ॥ 38 ॥
4.3.m: That twice-born man too, O best of sages, will cross beyond worldly existence." / Thus conversing, the two proceeded on the excellent road.

4.3.s:
kānyakubjasya sāmīpye saraḥ śreṣṭhamapaśyatām ..
haṃsakāraṇḍa vākīrṇaṃ cakravākopaśobhitam .. 39 ..
4.3.d:
कान्यकुब्जस्य सामीप्ये सरः श्रेष्ठमपश्यताम् ॥
हंसकारण्ड वाकीर्णं चक्रवाकोपशोभितम् ॥ 39 ॥
4.3.m: Near Kānyakubja, they saw a splendid lake, / crowded with swans and kāraṇḍava ducks, adorned with cakravāka birds,

4.3.s:
padminījalakahlāraraktotpalasitotpalaiḥ ..
chāditaṃ padminīpatrairmatsyaiḥ kūrmairjjalodbhavaiḥ .. 4.3.40 ..
4.3.d:
पद्मिनीजलकह्लाररक्तोत्पलसितोत्पलैः ॥
छादितं पद्मिनीपत्रैर्मत्स्यैः कूर्मैर्ज्जलोद्भवैः ॥ 4.3.40 ॥
4.3.m: covered with lotus clusters, water kahlāras, red lotuses, and white lotuses, / with lotus leaves, with fish and water-born turtles,

4.3.s:
taṭai ramyairghanairvṛkṣaiḥ ketakīkhaṇḍamaṃḍitam..
ketakīkusumāmodairllakucaistaṭamaṃḍitaiḥ .. 41 ..
4.3.d:
तटै रम्यैर्घनैर्वृक्षैः केतकीखण्डमंडितम्॥
केतकीकुसुमामोदैर्ल्लकुचैस्तटमंडितैः ॥ 41 ॥
4.3.m: adorned with groves of ketakī on its lovely banks thick with trees, / with the fragrances of ketakī blossoms, with lakuca trees adorning the banks,

4.3.s:
dātyūhaśikhibhāruṇḍacakorādyaiśca saṃkulam ..
kuravaiścātakai ramyaṃ kekākulanināditam .. 42 ..
4.3.d:
दात्यूहशिखिभारुण्डचकोराद्यैश्च संकुलम् ॥
कुरवैश्चातकै रम्यं केकाकुलनिनादितम् ॥ 42 ॥
4.3.m: crowded with water cocks, peacocks, bhāruṇḍas, cakoras, and other birds, / delightful with kuravas and cātakas, resounding with noisy peacock cries,

4.3.s:
jalakukkuṭasaṃgītaṃ haṃsasārasaśobhitam ..
jīvaṃjīvakahārītacakorairupaśobhitam .. 43 ..
4.3.d:
जलकुक्कुटसंगीतं हंससारसशोभितम् ॥
जीवंजीवकहारीतचकोरैरुपशोभितम् ॥ 43 ॥
4.3.m: musical with water hens, adorned with swans and cranes, / beautified with jīvañjīvakas, green pigeons, and cakoras,

4.3.s:
vaśiṣṭhasya munernāmnā vikhyātaṃ śrīmahodayam ..
asminnadya praveṣṭavyaṃ mahājanavivekinām .. 44..
4.3.d:
वशिष्ठस्य मुनेर्नाम्ना विख्यातं श्रीमहोदयम् ॥
अस्मिन्नद्य प्रवेष्टव्यं महाजनविवेकिनाम् ॥ 44॥
4.3.m: famed by the name of the sage Vasiṣṭha as Śrīmahodaya. / "Into this lake, discerning men of the assembly must enter today;

4.3.s:
sthātavyaṃ puratasteṣāṃ tasmātsnānaṃ samācaret ..
ityuktvā keśavaḥ pāpaṃ sasnau prāgeva tajjalaiḥ .. 45 ..
4.3.d:
स्थातव्यं पुरतस्तेषां तस्मात्स्नानं समाचरेत् ॥
इत्युक्त्वा केशवः पापं सस्नौ प्रागेव तज्जलैः ॥ 45 ॥
4.3.m: one must stand before them; therefore one should take a bath." / Having spoken thus, Keśava bathed first in its waters, [destroying] sin.

4.3.s:
yattīrthalokaṃ vikhyātaṃ snātvā tīraṃ samāśritaḥ ..
prahare vāsudevasya nārado'pi mudā yutaḥ .. 46 ..
4.3.d:
यत्तीर्थलोकं विख्यातं स्नात्वा तीरं समाश्रितः ॥
प्रहरे वासुदेवस्य नारदोऽपि मुदा युतः ॥ 46 ॥
4.3.m: Having bathed in that famed sacred ford, he resorted to the bank. / In that watch of Vāsudeva, Nārada too, filled with joy,

4.3.s:
ācamya sasnau tīrthena kṣaṇāttīrthamavāpya ca ..
yāvaduttiṣṭhate toyātsnātvā ṛṣirudāradhīḥ .. 47 ..
4.3.d:
आचम्य सस्नौ तीर्थेन क्षणात्तीर्थमवाप्य च ॥
यावदुत्तिष्ठते तोयात्स्नात्वा ऋषिरुदारधीः ॥ 47 ॥
4.3.m: sipped water and bathed in the ford, having entered the ford in an instant. / As soon as the noble-minded sage arose from the water after bathing,

4.3.s:
tāvatstrītvaṃ samāpanno nāradaḥ kena varṇyate ..
yasyāstu vistṛte netre vaktraṃ candropamaṃ śubham .. 48 ..
4.3.d:
तावत्स्त्रीत्वं समापन्नो नारदः केन वर्ण्यते ॥
यस्यास्तु विस्तृते नेत्रे वक्त्रं चन्द्रोपमं शुभम् ॥ 48 ॥
4.3.m: so soon had Nārada attained womanhood—by whom can she be described? / Her eyes were wide, her lovely face resembled the moon;

4.3.s:
smarapāśopamau karṇau kapolau kanakojjvalau ..
nāsikā tilasūnena kāmacāpopame bhruvau .. 49 ..
4.3.d:
स्मरपाशोपमौ कर्णौ कपोलौ कनकोज्ज्वलौ ॥
नासिका तिलसूनेन कामचापोपमे भ्रुवौ ॥ 49 ॥
4.3.m: her ears were like the nooses of Smara, her cheeks radiant as gold; / her nose was like a sesame blossom, her eyebrows like the bow of Kāma;

4.3.s:
daśanā hīrakaistulyā vidrumābhaḥ śubhādharaḥ ..
mayūrasya kalāpena tulya kacanibaṃdhanam .. 4.3.50 ..
4.3.d:
दशना हीरकैस्तुल्या विद्रुमाभः शुभाधरः ॥
मयूरस्य कलापेन तुल्य कचनिबंधनम् ॥ 4.3.50 ॥
4.3.m: her teeth were like diamonds, her auspicious lower lip shone like coral; / the braid of her hair was equal to the plumage of a peacock;

4.3.s:
śaṃkharekhātrayeṇaiva kaṃṭhadeśo virājate ..
mādhavīlatayā tulyau maṃjū tasyā bhujau śubhau .. 51 ..
4.3.d:
शंखरेखात्रयेणैव कंठदेशो विराजते ॥
माधवीलतया तुल्यौ मंजू तस्या भुजौ शुभौ ॥ 51 ॥
4.3.m: her throat region shone with three conch-shell lines; / her lovely, auspicious arms were charming, like mādhavī creepers,

4.3.s:
yutau raktotpalābhāsau pāṇī raktanakhāṃgulī ..
pīnāvatuṃgatanudhṛtkaṭhinau kalaśopamau .. 52 ..
4.3.d:
युतौ रक्तोत्पलाभासौ पाणी रक्तनखांगुली ॥
पीनावतुंगतनुधृत्कठिनौ कलशोपमौ ॥ 52 ॥
4.3.m: fitted with hands having the luster of red lotuses, their fingers having red nails; / plump, held upon a slender frame, firm, like water jars,

4.3.s:
stanāvaviralau snigdhau cakravākayugopamau ..
svalpakaṃ madhyadeśaṃ tu muṣṭigrāhyamasaṃśayam .. 53 ..
4.3.d:
स्तनावविरलौ स्निग्धौ चक्रवाकयुगोपमौ ॥
स्वल्पकं मध्यदेशं तु मुष्टिग्राह्यमसंशयम् ॥ 53 ॥
4.3.m: her breasts were close together, smooth, resembling a pair of cakravāka birds; / her waist was slender, graspable by the fist without doubt;

4.3.s:
nābhimaṃḍalagāṃbhīryaṃ lāvaṇyaṃ kena varṇyate ..
valitrayeṇa vikṛtā romarājirvirājitā .. 54 ..
4.3.d:
नाभिमंडलगांभीर्यं लावण्यं केन वर्ण्यते ॥
वलित्रयेण विकृता रोमराजिर्विराजिता ॥ 54 ॥
4.3.m: by whom can the depth of the circle of her navel and her beauty be described? / Adorned with three folds, the line of hair shone splendidly;

4.3.s:
nayane ca punastasyā mṛgyā iva suśobhane ..
nitaṃbo biṃbaphalakā manmathāyatanaṃ śubham .. 55 ..
4.3.d:
नयने च पुनस्तस्या मृग्या इव सुशोभने ॥
नितंबो बिंबफलका मन्मथायतनं शुभम् ॥ 55 ॥
4.3.m: and her eyes again were very lovely, like those of a doe; / her buttocks were broad as a bimba fruit, an auspicious abode of Manmatha;

4.3.s:
raṃbhāyugmopamāvūrū smarabāṇanibaṃdhanau ..
viparītaratāyāsakhedabhārasahau dṛḍhau .. 56 ..
4.3.d:
रंभायुग्मोपमावूरू स्मरबाणनिबंधनौ ॥
विपरीतरतायासखेदभारसहौ दृढौ ॥ 56 ॥
4.3.m: her thighs resembled a pair of plantain trunks, binding the arrows of Smara, / firm, capable of bearing the heavy toil and exertion of inverted sexual union;

4.3.s:
navakundalatāsārasaralaṃ sanibaṃdhanam ..
jaṃghāyugaṃ mahārāja gūḍhagulpha yugaṃ tathā .. 57 ..
4.3.d:
नवकुन्दलतासारसरलं सनिबंधनम् ॥
जंघायुगं महाराज गूढगुल्फ युगं तथा ॥ 57 ॥
4.3.m: straight, compact, like the essence of a fresh kunda creeper, / was the pair of her shanks, O great king, and likewise her pair of hidden ankles;

4.3.s:
raktāṃgulīlatātalpanakhacandrakayācitam ..
caraṇāraviṃdayugalaṃ saraktaṃ supratiṣṭhitam .. 58 ..
4.3.d:
रक्तांगुलीलतातल्पनखचन्द्रकयाचितम् ॥
चरणारविंदयुगलं सरक्तं सुप्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ 58 ॥
4.3.m: adorned with crescent moon-like nails upon the couches of red creeper-like toes, / her pair of lotus feet was reddish and firmly planted.

4.3.s:
saivaṃvidhā tadā nārī sarvalakṣaṇapū jitā ..
babhūva kṣaṇamātreṇa jagadvyāmohakāriṇī .. 59 ..
4.3.d:
सैवंविधा तदा नारी सर्वलक्षणपू जिता ॥
बभूव क्षणमात्रेण जगद्व्यामोहकारिणी ॥ 59 ॥
4.3.m: Such a woman, endowed with all auspicious marks, / she became in a mere moment, bewildering the entire world.

4.3.s:
kṣīrodamathanottīrṇā lakṣmīmanyābhivocchritām ..
dṛṣṭvāpyadarśanaṃ prāpto māyayā madhusūdanaḥ .. 4.3.60 ..
4.3.d:
क्षीरोदमथनोत्तीर्णा लक्ष्मीमन्याभिवोच्छ्रिताम् ॥
दृष्ट्वाप्यदर्शनं प्राप्तो मायया मधुसूदनः ॥ 4.3.60 ॥
4.3.m: Having seen her, like another exalted Lakṣmī arisen from the churning of the Ocean of Milk, / Madhusūdana vanished through his māyā.

4.3.s:
saṃprāpyate ca sā kālasaṃgarāhāriṇī yathā ..
āsta ekākinī mugdhā kuryāddigavalokanam .. 61 ..
4.3.d:
संप्राप्यते च सा कालसंगराहारिणी यथा ॥
आस्त एकाकिनी मुग्धा कुर्याद्दिगवलोकनम् ॥ 61 ॥
4.3.m: And when she found herself like one robbed in the battle of time, / the bewildered woman sat alone and looked in every direction.

4.3.s:
athājagāma taṃ deśaṃ nāmnā tāladhvajo nṛpaḥ ..
saha sainyaiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraṃdara ivāmaraiḥ .. 62 ..
4.3.d:
अथाजगाम तं देशं नाम्ना तालध्वजो नृपः ॥
सह सैन्यैः परिवृतः पुरंदर इवामरैः ॥ 62 ॥
4.3.m: Then there arrived at that place a king named Tāladhvaja, / surrounded by his armies like Purandara by the immortals.

4.3.s:
gajārūḍhairhayārūḍhai rathārūḍhairnarottamaiḥ ..
vimānayānayugmasthaistathāṃtaḥpurikājanaiḥ ..63..
4.3.d:
गजारूढैर्हयारूढै रथारूढैर्नरोत्तमैः ॥
विमानयानयुग्मस्थैस्तथांतःपुरिकाजनैः ॥63॥
4.3.m: with foremost men mounted on elephants, on horses, and on chariots, / and with the women of the inner apartments riding together in aerial conveyances and vehicles,

4.3.s:
dhvajātapatrakalilairanīkaiḥ parivāritaḥ ..
tena sā sahasā dṛṣṭā nārī kamalalocanā .. 64 ..
4.3.d:
ध्वजातपत्रकलिलैरनीकैः परिवारितः ॥
तेन सा सहसा दृष्टा नारी कमललोचना ॥ 64 ॥
4.3.m: surrounded by armies crowded with banners and royal parasols. / Suddenly he caught sight of that lotus-eyed woman.

4.3.s:
babhūva kṣaṇamātreṇa kaṃdarpaśarapīḍitaḥ ..
keyaṃ kasya kutaḥ prāptā kiṃ devī vātha mānuṣī .. 65 ..
4.3.d:
बभूव क्षणमात्रेण कंदर्पशरपीडितः ॥
केयं कस्य कुतः प्राप्ता किं देवी वाथ मानुषी ॥ 65 ॥
4.3.m: In a mere moment he became tormented by the arrows of the god of love. / “Who is she? Whose is she? Whence did she arrive? Is she a goddess or a mortal woman?

4.3.s:
adṛṣṭarūpāpsarasā kāciddevī samāgatā ..
ahorūpaṃ surūpāyā gocare paritaḥ pumān .. 66 ..
4.3.d:
अदृष्टरूपाप्सरसा काचिद्देवी समागता ॥
अहोरूपं सुरूपाया गोचरे परितः पुमान् ॥ 66 ॥
4.3.m: Some goddess has arrived whose beauty has never been seen even among the apsarases. / Ah, the beauty of this fair woman! If a man comes within the range of her sight,

4.3.s:
mumūrṣurjāyate mohādanudigdhahato yathā ..
iti saṃcintya hṛdaye rājā tāladhvajo'ntike .. 67 ..
4.3.d:
मुमूर्षुर्जायते मोहादनुदिग्धहतो यथा ॥
इति संचिन्त्य हृदये राजा तालध्वजोऽन्तिके ॥ 67 ॥
4.3.m: he is stricken with a desire to die out of infatuation, as though struck by an unanointed weapon.” / Reflecting thus in his heart, King Tāladhvaja drew near

4.3.s:
uvāca nārīṃ mugdhāṃ tāṃ śṛṇu madvacanaṃ śubhe ..
kā tvaṃ kasya kutaḥ prāptā deśametaṃ śucismite .. 68 ..
4.3.d:
उवाच नारीं मुग्धां तां शृणु मद्वचनं शुभे ॥
का त्वं कस्य कुतः प्राप्ता देशमेतं शुचिस्मिते ॥ 68 ॥
4.3.m: and spoke to that innocent woman: “Listen to my word, auspicious lady! / Who are you? Whose are you? Whence did you come to this region, O fair-smiling one?”

4.3.s:
ityukte sāśru cārvaṃgī prāha māṃ viddhyayonijām ..
pitrā mātrā vihīnāṃ ca tathādyāpi kumārikām .. 69 ..
4.3.d:
इत्युक्ते साश्रु चार्वंगी प्राह मां विद्ध्ययोनिजाम् ॥
पित्रा मात्रा विहीनां च तथाद्यापि कुमारिकाम् ॥ 69 ॥
4.3.m: When this was spoken, she of lovely limbs, full of tears, said: “Know me to be not born of a womb, / bereft of father and mother, and even now a maiden.”

4.3.s:
nirāśrayāṃ viditvaināṃ tato jātaḥ smarārditaḥ ..
āropya hayapṛṣṭhe tāṃ tato rājāgato gṛham .. 4.3.70 ..
4.3.d:
निराश्रयां विदित्वैनां ततो जातः स्मरार्दितः ॥
आरोप्य हयपृष्ठे तां ततो राजागतो गृहम् ॥ 4.3.70 ॥
4.3.m: Knowing that she was shelterless, he became afflicted with love. / Placing her on the back of his horse, the king then went home.

4.3.s:
nītvā vivāhayāmāsa śāstroktavidhinā tataḥ ..
reme prāsādaśṛṃgāgre paryaṃke sitayā tayā .. 71 ..
4.3.d:
नीत्वा विवाहयामास शास्त्रोक्तविधिना ततः ॥
रेमे प्रासादशृंगाग्रे पर्यंके सितया तया ॥ 71 ॥
4.3.m: Having taken her, he then married her according to the rule prescribed in the scriptures. / He took his pleasure with that fair lady on a couch at the top of the palace terrace,

4.3.s:
udyānabhavyabhūmīṣu nadīnāṃ pulineṣu ca ..
parvatānāṃ nitaṃbeṣu nirjhareṣu guhāsu ca .. 72 ..
4.3.d:
उद्यानभव्यभूमीषु नदीनां पुलिनेषु च ॥
पर्वतानां नितंबेषु निर्झरेषु गुहासु च ॥ 72 ॥
4.3.m: in the splendid grounds of pleasure-gardens, on the sandy banks of rivers, / on mountain slopes, by waterfalls, and in caves,

4.3.s:
padmakhaṃḍeṣu phulleṣu śobhiteṣu sarassu ca ..
prayāgādiṣu tīrtheṣu nadīnāmāśrameṣu ca .. 73 ..
4.3.d:
पद्मखंडेषु फुल्लेषु शोभितेषु सरस्सु च ॥
प्रयागादिषु तीर्थेषु नदीनामाश्रमेषु च ॥ 73 ॥
4.3.m: among blossoming beds of lotuses and beside adorned lakes, / at holy bathing places such as Prayāga, and at the hermitages of rivers,

4.3.s:
divyāvasatharamyeṣu velākūleṣu pārthivaḥ ..
yāvaddvādaśa varṣāṇi ekāhamapi bhārata ..74..
4.3.d:
दिव्यावसथरम्येषु वेलाकूलेषु पार्थिवः ॥
यावद्द्वादश वर्षाणि एकाहमपि भारत ॥74॥
4.3.m: and on seashore shores delightful with divine abodes, / for twelve years, O Bhārata, as though for a single day.

4.3.s:
tatastrayodaśe varṣe tasyā garbho'bhavanmahān ..
etasmingarbhasaṃpūrṇe jātaṃ dīrghamalābukam .. .. 75 ..
4.3.d:
ततस्त्रयोदशे वर्षे तस्या गर्भोऽभवन्महान् ॥
एतस्मिन्गर्भसंपूर्णे जातं दीर्घमलाबुकम् ॥ ॥ 75 ॥
4.3.m: Then, in the thirteenth year, her womb bore a great fetus. / When this womb had reached its term, a long bottle-gourd was born.

4.3.s:
tadbhedāhatakuṃbheṣu bījaprārohaṇānnarāḥ ..
babhūvurddhātuśūnyā vai divyadehabalotkaṭāḥ .. 76 ..
4.3.d:
तद्भेदाहतकुंभेषु बीजप्रारोहणान्नराः ॥
बभूवुर्द्धातुशून्या वै दिव्यदेहबलोत्कटाः ॥ 76 ॥
4.3.m: From the splitting of that into jars that were struck, through the sprouting of the seeds, men were born / devoid indeed of bodily humours, eminent with divine bodies and strength.

4.3.s:
paṃcāśatsaṃkhyayā jātā upasargādivarjitāḥ ..
ārūḍhayauvanāḥ sarve sutāḥ saṃgrāmakovidāḥ .. 77 ..
4.3.d:
पंचाशत्संख्यया जाता उपसर्गादिवर्जिताः ॥
आरूढयौवनाः सर्वे सुताः संग्रामकोविदाः ॥ 77 ॥
4.3.m: Fifty in number they were born, free from portents and ailments, / all attained to youth, sons skilled in warfare.

4.3.s:
teṣāṃ putrāśca pautrāśca babhūvuḥ surasattamāḥ ..
yuyudhuḥ śarasaṃghātaiścakraśūlāsipaṭṭiśaiḥ .. 78 ..
4.3.d:
तेषां पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च बभूवुः सुरसत्तमाः ॥
युयुधुः शरसंघातैश्चक्रशूलासिपट्टिशैः ॥ 78 ॥
4.3.m: Sons and grandsons were born to them, foremost of gods; / they fought with showers of arrows, with discs, tridents, swords, and sharp spears.

4.3.s:
hayairanyairgajairanyaiḥ krodhāṃdhāḥ kauravā iva ..
pāṃḍavaiḥ saha saṃgrāme yuyudhuḥ kṣayamaṃjasā ..79 ..
4.3.d:
हयैरन्यैर्गजैरन्यैः क्रोधांधाः कौरवा इव ॥
पांडवैः सह संग्रामे युयुधुः क्षयमंजसा ॥79 ॥
4.3.m: Some on horses and others on elephants, blind with rage like the Kauravas, / they quickly fought to destruction in battle, as with the Pāṇḍavas.

4.3.s:
sapadātigajārohāḥ sāṃtaḥpurayugecchayā ..
vineśurabdhimāsādya siṃdhūnāṃ pravahā iva..4.3.80..
4.3.d:
सपदातिगजारोहाः सांतःपुरयुगेच्छया ॥
विनेशुरब्धिमासाद्य सिंधूनां प्रवहा इव॥4.3.80॥
4.3.m: Together with foot-soldiers and elephant-riders, out of a desire for union with the inner apartments, / they perished upon reaching the ocean, like streams of rivers.

4.3.s:
sāsisabalavistārāḥ sadarpāḥ samahocchrayāḥ ..
indralokopamaṃ sarvaṃ kulaṃ naṣṭaṃ kṣaṇaṃ tadā ..81..
4.3.d:
सासिसबलविस्ताराः सदर्पाः समहोच्छ्रयाः ॥
इन्द्रलोकोपमं सर्वं कुलं नष्टं क्षणं तदा ॥81॥
4.3.m: Bearing swords, having extensive forces, proud, and of great height, / that entire family, like the world of Indra, was destroyed in an instant then.

4.3.s:
saṃdṛśya nāradīyaiṣā vinaṣṭaṃ svakulaṃ raṇe ..
ruroda snehasaṃyuktai rasaiḥ kaluṣayā girā .. 82..
4.3.d:
संदृश्य नारदीयैषा विनष्टं स्वकुलं रणे ॥
रुरोद स्नेहसंयुक्तै रसैः कलुषया गिरा ॥ 82॥
4.3.m: Seeing her own family destroyed in battle, this female form of Nārada / wept with a voice choked with emotions connected to affection:

4.3.s:
hā daiva hā vidhe pāpa hā kṛtānta namaskṛta ..
darśayitvā vidhānaṃ me punarnetre hṛte tvayā .. 83 ..
4.3.d:
हा दैव हा विधे पाप हा कृतान्त नमस्कृत ॥
दर्शयित्वा विधानं मे पुनर्नेत्रे हृते त्वया ॥ 83 ॥
4.3.m: “Alas, Fate! Alas, wicked Destiny! Alas, Death, homaged by all! / After showing me your dispensation, you have stolen away my two eyes once again!”

4.3.s:
ityuktvā svamurohastairjaghāna bhṛśaduḥkhitā ..
bhūmau mūrcchāturā bhūtvā punaḥ prāptā vicetanam ..84..
4.3.d:
इत्युक्त्वा स्वमुरोहस्तैर्जघान भृशदुःखिता ॥
भूमौ मूर्च्छातुरा भूत्वा पुनः प्राप्ता विचेतनम् ॥84॥
4.3.m: Having spoken thus, she beat her breast with her hands, utterly sorrowful. / Falling into a swoon upon the ground, she became unconscious once again.

4.3.s:
so'pi rājā viṣaṇṇo'sau nirviṇṇaḥ śokasāgare..
bhūmau nipatito duḥkhādruroda bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ ..85..
4.3.d:
सोऽपि राजा विषण्णोऽसौ निर्विण्णः शोकसागरे॥
भूमौ निपतितो दुःखाद्रुरोद भृशदुःखितः ॥85॥
4.3.m: That king too became despondent, despairing in the ocean of sorrow. / Having fallen to the ground out of grief, he wept, utterly sorrowful,

4.3.s:
viṣaṇṇo maṃtribhiḥ sārdhaṃ vṛddhaśokena saṃyutaḥ ..
etasminnaṃtare viṣṇurājagāma dvijaiḥ saha ..86..
4.3.d:
विषण्णो मंत्रिभिः सार्धं वृद्धशोकेन संयुतः ॥
एतस्मिन्नंतरे विष्णुराजगाम द्विजैः सह ॥86॥
4.3.m: despondent along with his ministers, filled with profound grief. / At that interval, Viṣṇu arrived along with brāhmaṇas.

4.3.s:
dvijaveṣaparicchanna upaviṣṭaḥ sukhāsane ..
tataḥ purassaro bhūtvā cakre dharmārthadarśanam ..87..
4.3.d:
द्विजवेषपरिच्छन्न उपविष्टः सुखासने ॥
ततः पुरस्सरो भूत्वा चक्रे धर्मार्थदर्शनम् ॥87॥
4.3.m: Disguised in the dress of a brāhmaṇa, he sat upon a comfortable seat. / Then, stepping forward, he expounded the purpose of dharma:

4.3.s:
kiṃ rodanena bahunā yuvayoḥ kleśakāriṇā ..
śrūyatāṃ viṣṇumāyaiṣā svapnadṛṣṭadhanopamā ..88..
4.3.d:
किं रोदनेन बहुना युवयोः क्लेशकारिणा ॥
श्रूयतां विष्णुमायैषा स्वप्नदृष्टधनोपमा ॥88॥
4.3.m: “What is the use of so much weeping, which causes affliction to you both? / Hear of this Māyā of Viṣṇu, which resembles wealth seen in a dream.

4.3.s:
śobhane yādṛśaḥ śokaḥ kṛtaḥ saṃsārasāgare ..
sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ pariṇāmoyamīdṛśaḥ .. .. 89 ..
4.3.d:
शोभने यादृशः शोकः कृतः संसारसागरे ॥
सर्वेषामेव भूतानां परिणामोयमीदृशः ॥ ॥ 89 ॥
4.3.m: O fair lady, such is the sorrow produced in the ocean of worldly existence; / this is the very transformation destined for all beings whatsoever.

4.3.s:
puraṃdarasahasrāṇi cakravartiśatāni ca ..
nirvāpitāni kālena pradīpa iva vāyunā .. 4.3.90 ..
ye'pi śoṣayituṃ śaktāḥ samudraṃ grāhasaṃkulam.99.
4.3.d:
पुरंदरसहस्राणि चक्रवर्तिशतानि च ॥
निर्वापितानि कालेन प्रदीप इव वायुना ॥ 4.3.90 ॥
येऽपि शोषयितुं शक्ताः समुद्रं ग्राहसंकुलम्.99.
4.3.m:
Thousands of Indras and hundreds of universal monarchs / have been extinguished by Time, like a lamp by the wind.
Even those who were able to dry up the ocean teeming with sea-monsters,

4.3.s: kuryuśca karayugmena cūrṇaṃ meruṃ mahītale .. 91 ..
4.3.d: कुर्युश्च करयुग्मेन चूर्णं मेरुं महीतले ॥ 91 ॥
4.3.m: and who could reduce Mount Meru to powder upon the earth with both hands,

4.3.s:
ūddhartuṃ dharaṇīsaṃjñāṃ grahītuṃ candrabhāskarau ..
praviṣṭāste tu kālena kṛtāṃtavadanaṃ tadā .. 92 ..
4.3.d:
ऊद्धर्तुं धरणीसंज्ञां ग्रहीतुं चन्द्रभास्करौ ॥
प्रविष्टास्ते तु कालेन कृतांतवदनं तदा ॥ 92 ॥
4.3.m: and lift up that which is called the earth, and seize the moon and sun— / they entered the jaws of Death at that time, carried off by Time.

4.3.s:
durgastrikūṭaḥ parikhāḥ samudrā rakṣāṃsi yodhā dhanadācca vittam ..
maṃtraśca yasyauśanasā praṇītaḥ sa rāvaṇo daivavaśādviṣaṇṇaḥ .. 93 ..
4.3.d:
दुर्गस्त्रिकूटः परिखाः समुद्रा रक्षांसि योधा धनदाच्च वित्तम् ॥
मंत्रश्च यस्यौशनसा प्रणीतः स रावणो दैववशाद्विषण्णः ॥ 93 ॥
4.3.m: He whose fortress was Trikūṭa, whose moats were the oceans, whose warriors were rākṣasas, whose wealth was from Kubera, / and whose counsel was delivered by the son of Uśanas—even that Rāvaṇa fell into despair by the power of Fate.

4.3.s:
saṃgrāme gajaturagasamākule'pi vādādagnau vā gatavivare mahodadhau vā ..
sarvairvā saha vasatāmudīrṇakopairnābhāvyo bhavati kadācideva nāśaḥ .. 94 ..
4.3.d:
संग्रामे गजतुरगसमाकुलेऽपि वादादग्नौ वा गतविवरे महोदधौ वा ॥
सर्वैर्वा सह वसतामुदीर्णकोपैर्नाभाव्यो भवति कदाचिदेव नाशः ॥ 94 ॥
4.3.m: Whether in battle crowded with elephants and horses, or in fire through dispute, or in an entered chasm, or in the great ocean, / or even when living with all those whose anger has flared up, a destruction that is destined never fails to occur.

4.3.s:
pātālamāviśatu yātu surendralokamārohatu kṣitidharādhipatiṃ sumerum ..
maṃtrauṣadhipraharaṇaiśca karotu rakṣāṃ yadbhāvi tadbhavati nātha vibhāvito'smi .. 95 ..
4.3.d:
पातालमाविशतु यातु सुरेन्द्रलोकमारोहतु क्षितिधराधिपतिं सुमेरुम् ॥
मंत्रौषधिप्रहरणैश्च करोतु रक्षां यद्भावि तद्भवति नाथ विभावितोऽस्मि ॥ 95 ॥
4.3.m: Let him enter the netherworld, let him go to the world of the lord of the gods, let him climb Sumeru, the lord of mountains, / and let him effect protection through mantras, herbs, and weapons: whatever is to happen will happen; O Lord, I am fully convinced.

4.3.s:
roditi kaścidathāśrudhautānanagurutaraśokavihvalaḥ ..
pravikaṭacaraṇavānapi nṛtyati kaściddharmādivigrahaḥ .. 96 ..
4.3.d:
रोदिति कश्चिदथाश्रुधौताननगुरुतरशोकविह्वलः ॥
प्रविकटचरणवानपि नृत्यति कश्चिद्धर्मादिविग्रहः ॥ 96 ॥
4.3.m: One person weeps, his face washed with tears, distraught with weighty grief; / another, endowed with huge feet, dances as the embodiment of righteousness and other goals.

4.3.s:
gāyati hṛdayahāri sukhanirbharamāyatavistṛtā'dharo'dhikam ..
sāra eṣa raṃgodaragatanaṭapaṭahākāma evāyam .. 97..
4.3.d:
गायति हृदयहारि सुखनिर्भरमायतविस्तृताऽधरोऽधिकम् ॥
सार एष रंगोदरगतनटपटहाकाम एवायम् ॥ 97॥
4.3.m: Another sings, captivating to the heart, filled with delight, his lips drawn wide apart; / this is the essence, merely like a drum desired by actors within an arena.”

4.3.s:
ityevaṃ dharmamuddiśya viṣṇuḥ saṃsāraceṣṭitam ..
tūṣṇīṃ babhūvānupadaṃ tataste dvijapuṅgavāḥ .. 98 ..
4.3.d:
इत्येवं धर्ममुद्दिश्य विष्णुः संसारचेष्टितम् ॥
तूष्णीं बभूवानुपदं ततस्ते द्विजपुङ्गवाः ॥ 98 ॥
4.3.m: Having thus pointed out righteousness and the behavior of worldly existence, / Viṣṇu fell silent, and immediately thereafter those eminent brāhmaṇas spoke:

4.3.s:
uttiṣṭha snāhi putrāṇāṃ prakuruṣvaurdhvadehikam ..
mā śokaṃ viṣṇumāyaiṣā viṣṇunā nirmitā svayam .. 99 ..
4.3.d:
उत्तिष्ठ स्नाहि पुत्राणां प्रकुरुष्वौर्ध्वदेहिकम् ॥
मा शोकं विष्णुमायैषा विष्णुना निर्मिता स्वयम् ॥ 99 ॥
4.3.m: “Arise, bathe, and perform the funeral rites for your sons! / Do not grieve; this is the Māyā of Viṣṇu, created by Viṣṇu himself.”

4.3.s:
ityuktā cārusarvāṃgī sa babhūvācalaḥ pumān ..
sa eṣa sadṛśākāro nāradastatkṣaṇe'bhavat .. 4.3.100 ..
4.3.d:
इत्युक्ता चारुसर्वांगी स बभूवाचलः पुमान् ॥
स एष सदृशाकारो नारदस्तत्क्षणेऽभवत् ॥ 4.3.100 ॥
4.3.m: When she of lovely limbs was thus addressed, she became an unmoving man. / In that instant he became Nārada, having his own form.

4.3.s:
so'pi rājā dadarśātha taṃ samaṃtripurohitaḥ ..
sāṃtaḥpuramidaṃ sarvamiṃdrajālopamaṃ kṣaṇāt .. 101 ..
4.3.d:
सोऽपि राजा ददर्शाथ तं समंत्रिपुरोहितः ॥
सांतःपुरमिदं सर्वमिंद्रजालोपमं क्षणात् ॥ 101 ॥
4.3.m: Then the king too, along with his ministers and domestic priest, / beheld this entire court resembling an illusion of Indra in an instant,

4.3.s:
nāradaṃ muniśārdūlaṃ jaṭābhārabhayānakam ..
gauravarṇaṃ jvalaṃtaṃ ca brāhamyā lakṣmyā virājitam .. 102 ..
4.3.d:
नारदं मुनिशार्दूलं जटाभारभयानकम् ॥
गौरवर्णं ज्वलंतं च ब्राहम्या लक्ष्म्या विराजितम् ॥ 102 ॥
4.3.m: and [saw] Nārada, foremost among sages, dreadful with a mass of matted hair, / fair in complexion, radiant, and shining with brāhmanical splendour,

4.3.s:
śikhā kamaṇḍaludharaṃ vīṇādaṇḍakaraṃ tathā ..
brahmasūtreṇa śubhreṇa kaupīnācchādanena ca ..
pādukābhyāṃ sthitaṃ tīre saraso brāhmaṇāsane .. 103 ..
4.3.d:
शिखा कमण्डलुधरं वीणादण्डकरं तथा ॥
ब्रह्मसूत्रेण शुभ्रेण कौपीनाच्छादनेन च ॥
पादुकाभ्यां स्थितं तीरे सरसो ब्राह्मणासने ॥ 103 ॥
4.3.m: wearing a crest-lock, bearing a water-pot, holding the stem of a vīṇā in his hand, / with a white sacred thread, wearing a loincloth, / and standing upon sandals on the bank of the lake upon a brāhmaṇa's seat.

4.3.s:
saṃpragṛhya karāgreṇa jagāmādarśanaṃ hariḥ ..
ambareṇa suraiḥ sārddhaṃ tasmāddeśādyudhiṣṭhira .. 104 ..
4.3.d:
संप्रगृह्य कराग्रेण जगामादर्शनं हरिः ॥
अम्बरेण सुरैः सार्द्धं तस्माद्देशाद्युधिष्ठिर ॥ 104 ॥
4.3.m: Having taken him by the tip of the hand, Hari vanished / through the sky along with the gods from that place, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

4.3.s:
śvetadvīpamathāsādya prāha devo muniṃ nṛpa ..
devarṣe yattvayā pṛṣṭaṃ pūrvaṃ māyākathāṃ prati .. 105 ..
4.3.d:
श्वेतद्वीपमथासाद्य प्राह देवो मुनिं नृप ॥
देवर्षे यत्त्वया पृष्टं पूर्वं मायाकथां प्रति ॥ 105 ॥
4.3.m: Then, having reached Śvetadvīpa, the god spoke to the sage, O king: / ‘O divine sage, as to that which was asked by you previously concerning the story of Māyā:

4.3.s:
māyā yayedṛśī māyā yatsvarūpā yadātmikā ..
sā te māyā mayā brahmanvaiṣṇavī saṃpradarśitā .. 106 ..
4.3.d:
माया ययेदृशी माया यत्स्वरूपा यदात्मिका ॥
सा ते माया मया ब्रह्मन्वैष्णवी संप्रदर्शिता ॥ 106 ॥
4.3.m: "Māyā is of such a kind, having such a form and such an essence; that Vaiṣṇava Māyā has now been shown to you by me, O Brahmin."

4.3.s:
evamuktvā munivaraṃ devadevo janārdanaḥ ..
babhūvāntarhitassadyo devarṣestasya paśyataḥ .. 107 ..
saṃsāradoṣavarṇanam
4.3.d:
एवमुक्त्वा मुनिवरं देवदेवो जनार्दनः ॥
बभूवान्तर्हितस्सद्यो देवर्षेस्तस्य पश्यतः ॥ 107 ॥
संसारदोषवर्णनम्
4.3.m:
Having spoken thus to the excellent sage, the god of gods, Janārdana, / vanished immediately before the eyes of that divine sage.
Description of the Evils of Saṃsāra

4.4.s:
.. yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
devatvaṃ mānuṣatvaṃ ca tiryaktvaṃ kena karmaṇā ..
prāpnoti puruṣaḥ kena garbhavāsaṃ sudāruṇam .. 1 ..
4.4.d:
॥ युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
देवत्वं मानुषत्वं च तिर्यक्त्वं केन कर्मणा ॥
प्राप्नोति पुरुषः केन गर्भवासं सुदारुणम् ॥ 1 ॥
4.4.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / By what action does a person attain godhood, human state, / or animal birth? By what [action does one undergo] the most terrible dwelling in a womb?

4.4.s:
garbhasthaśca kimaśnāti kathamutpadyate punaḥ ..
dattotthānādikāndoṣānkathaṃ tarati dustarān .. 2 ..
4.4.d:
गर्भस्थश्च किमश्नाति कथमुत्पद्यते पुनः ॥
दत्तोत्थानादिकान्दोषान्कथं तरति दुस्तरान् ॥ 2 ॥
4.4.m: And what does one eat while dwelling in the womb? How is one born again? / How does one cross over the insurmountable evils such as the conditions brought on by gifts and other acts?

4.4.s:
bālabhāve kathaṃ puṣṭiḥ syādyuvā kena karmaṇā ..
kulīnaḥ kena bhavati surūpaḥ sudhanaḥ katham .. 3 ..
4.4.d:
बालभावे कथं पुष्टिः स्याद्युवा केन कर्मणा ॥
कुलीनः केन भवति सुरूपः सुधनः कथम् ॥ 3 ॥
4.4.m: How does growth occur in childhood? By what action does one become a youth? / By what does one become noble-born? How does one become handsome and very wealthy?

4.4.s:
kathaṃ dārānavāpnoti gṛhaṃ sarvaguṇairyutam ..
paṃḍitaḥ putravāṃstyāgī syādā mayavivarjitaḥ .. 4 ..
4.4.d:
कथं दारानवाप्नोति गृहं सर्वगुणैर्युतम् ॥
पंडितः पुत्रवांस्त्यागी स्यादा मयविवर्जितः ॥ 4 ॥
4.4.m: How does one obtain a wife and a house endowed with all virtues? / [How does one become] learned, endowed with sons, generous, and free from disease?

4.4.s:
kathaṃ sukhena mriyate kathaṃ bhuṃkte śubhāśubham ..
sarvamevāmalamate gahanaṃ pratibhāti me .. 5 ..
4.4.d:
कथं सुखेन म्रियते कथं भुंक्ते शुभाशुभम् ॥
सर्वमेवामलमते गहनं प्रतिभाति मे ॥ 5 ॥
4.4.m: How does one die in comfort? How does one experience good and evil? / All of this seems deeply perplexing to me, O you of pure intellect!

4.4.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
śubhairdevatvamāpnoti miśrairmānuṣatāṃ vrajet ..
aśubhaiḥ karmabhirjjaṃtustiryagyoniṣu jāyate .. 6 ..
4.4.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
शुभैर्देवत्वमाप्नोति मिश्रैर्मानुषतां व्रजेत् ॥
अशुभैः कर्मभिर्ज्जंतुस्तिर्यग्योनिषु जायते ॥ 6 ॥
4.4.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / By good deeds one attains godhood; by mixed deeds one goes to the human state; / by evil deeds a living being is born in animal wombs.

4.4.s:
pramāṇaṃ śrutirevātra dharmādharmaviniścaye ..
pāpaṃ pāpena bhavati puṇyaṃ puṇyena karmaṇā .. 7 ..
4.4.d:
प्रमाणं श्रुतिरेवात्र धर्माधर्मविनिश्चये ॥
पापं पापेन भवति पुण्यं पुण्येन कर्मणा ॥ 7 ॥
4.4.m: Sacred tradition alone is the authority here in determining righteousness and unrighteousness: / evil comes from evil, and merit comes from meritorious action.

4.4.s:
ṛtukāle tadā bhuktaṃ nirdoṣaṃ yena saṃsthitam ..
tadā tadvāyunā spṛṣṭaṃ strīraktenaikatāṃ vrajet ..8..
4.4.d:
ऋतुकाले तदा भुक्तं निर्दोषं येन संस्थितम् ॥
तदा तद्वायुना स्पृष्टं स्त्रीरक्तेनैकतां व्रजेत् ॥8॥
4.4.m: What is then consumed during the fertile season, remaining free of defects, / touched then by wind, unites with the woman's blood.

4.4.s:
visargakāle śukrasya jīvaḥ karaṇasaṃyutaḥ ..
bhṛtyaḥ praviśate yoniṃ karmabhiḥ svairnniyojitaḥ .. 9 ..
4.4.d:
विसर्गकाले शुक्रस्य जीवः करणसंयुतः ॥
भृत्यः प्रविशते योनिं कर्मभिः स्वैर्न्नियोजितः ॥ 9 ॥
4.4.m: At the time of the emission of semen, the soul, accompanied by the sense faculties, / enters the womb like a servant, impelled by its own actions.

4.4.s:
tacchukraraktamekasthamekāhātkalalaṃ bhavet ..
pañcarātreṇa kalalaṃ budbudākāratāṃ vrajet .. 4.4.10 ..
4.4.d:
तच्छुक्ररक्तमेकस्थमेकाहात्कललं भवेत् ॥
पञ्चरात्रेण कललं बुद्बुदाकारतां व्रजेत् ॥ 4.4.10 ॥
4.4.m: That semen and blood joined in one becomes a kalala in one day; / in five nights the kalala assumes the shape of a bubble.

4.4.s:
budbudaṃ saptarātreṇa māṃsapeśī bhavettataḥ ..
dvisaptāhādbhavetpeśī raktamāṃsadṛḍhāṃcitaḥ .. 11 ..
4.4.d:
बुद्बुदं सप्तरात्रेण मांसपेशी भवेत्ततः ॥
द्विसप्ताहाद्भवेत्पेशी रक्तमांसदृढांचितः ॥ 11 ॥
4.4.m: In seven nights the bubble becomes a lump of flesh; / in a fortnight the lump becomes firmly layered with blood and flesh.

4.4.s:
bījasyevāṃkurāḥ peśyāḥ pañcaviṃśa tirātrataḥ ..
bhavaṃti māsamātreṇa pañcadhā jāyate punaḥ .. 12 ..
4.4.d:
बीजस्येवांकुराः पेश्याः पञ्चविंश तिरात्रतः ॥
भवंति मासमात्रेण पञ्चधा जायते पुनः ॥ 12 ॥
4.4.m: Like sprouts from a seed, [limbs emerge] from the lump after twenty-five nights; / in just a month it is formed in five parts.

4.4.s:
grīvā śiraśca skandhaśca pṛṣṭhavaṃśastathodaram ..
māsadvayena sarvāṇi kramaśaḥ saṃbhavaṃti ca .. 13 ..
4.4.d:
ग्रीवा शिरश्च स्कन्धश्च पृष्ठवंशस्तथोदरम् ॥
मासद्वयेन सर्वाणि क्रमशः संभवंति च ॥ 13 ॥
4.4.m: The neck, the head, the shoulders, the backbone, and likewise the belly— / all these arise gradually in two months.

4.4.s:
tribhirmāsaiḥ prajāyaṃte sadravyāṃkurasaṃdhayaḥ ..
māsaiścaturbhiraṃgulyaḥ prajāyaṃte yathākramam .. 14 ..
4.4.d:
त्रिभिर्मासैः प्रजायंते सद्रव्यांकुरसंधयः ॥
मासैश्चतुर्भिरंगुल्यः प्रजायंते यथाक्रमम् ॥ 14 ॥
4.4.m: In three months the joints, having the material sprouts, are produced; / in four months the fingers and toes are produced in due order.

4.4.s:
mukhaṃ nāsā ca karṇau ca jāyante pañca māsakaiḥ ..
daṃtapaṃktistathā guhyaṃ jāyaṃte ca nakhāḥ punaḥ .. 15 ..
4.4.d:
मुखं नासा च कर्णौ च जायन्ते पञ्च मासकैः ॥
दंतपंक्तिस्तथा गुह्यं जायंते च नखाः पुनः ॥ 15 ॥
4.4.m: The mouth, the nose, and the ears are formed in five months; / likewise the rows of teeth, the private parts, and nails are produced.

4.4.s:
karṇau ca raṃdhrasahitau ṣaṇmāsābhyaṃtareṇa tu ..
pāyurmeḍhramupasthaśca nābhiścāpyupa jāyate .. 16 ..
4.4.d:
कर्णौ च रंध्रसहितौ षण्मासाभ्यंतरेण तु ॥
पायुर्मेढ्रमुपस्थश्च नाभिश्चाप्युप जायते ॥ 16 ॥
4.4.m: And the ears with their cavities [arise] within six months; / the anus, the penis, the genitals, and the navel also arise.

4.4.s:
saṃdhayo ye ca gātreṣu māsairjāyaṃti saptabhiḥ ..
aṅgapratyaṃgasaṃpūrṇaḥ śiraḥ keśasamanvitaḥ .. 17 ..
4.4.d:
संधयो ये च गात्रेषु मासैर्जायंति सप्तभिः ॥
अङ्गप्रत्यंगसंपूर्णः शिरः केशसमन्वितः ॥ 17 ॥
4.4.m: And the joints that are in the limbs arise in seven months; / [the fetus becomes] complete with major and minor limbs, endowed with head-hair.

4.4.s:
vibhaktāvayavaḥ puṣṭaḥ punarmāsāṣṭakena ca ..
paṃcātmakasamāyuktaḥ paripakvaḥ sa tiṣṭhati .. 18 ..
4.4.d:
विभक्तावयवः पुष्टः पुनर्मासाष्टकेन च ॥
पंचात्मकसमायुक्तः परिपक्वः स तिष्ठति ॥ 18 ॥
4.4.m: With divided limbs, nourished, again in eight months / it rests fully matured, endowed with the five elements.

4.4.s:
māturāhāravīryeṇa ṣaḍvidhena sa tiṣṭhati ..
rasena pratyahaṃ bālo vardhate bharatarṣabha .. 19 ..
4.4.d:
मातुराहारवीर्येण षड्विधेन स तिष्ठति ॥
रसेन प्रत्यहं बालो वर्धते भरतर्षभ ॥ 19 ॥
4.4.m: By the strength of the mother's sixfold food, / the child grows day by day through the nutritive fluid, O bull of the Bharatas!

4.4.s:
tatte'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi yathāśrutamariṃdama ..
nābhisūtranibandhena varddhate sa dinedine .. 4.4.20 ..
4.4.d:
तत्तेऽहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि यथाश्रुतमरिंदम ॥
नाभिसूत्रनिबन्धेन वर्द्धते स दिनेदिने ॥ 4.4.20 ॥
4.4.m: I shall tell you that as it has been heard, O subduer of enemies: / bound by the umbilical cord, it grows day by day.

4.4.s:
tataḥ smṛtiṃ labhejjīvaḥ saṃpūrṇe'smiñcharīrake ..
sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ vijānāti nidrāsvapnaṃ purā kṛtam .. 21 ..
4.4.d:
ततः स्मृतिं लभेज्जीवः संपूर्णेऽस्मिञ्छरीरके ॥
सुखं दुःखं विजानाति निद्रास्वप्नं पुरा कृतम् ॥ 21 ॥
4.4.m: Then the soul gains memory when this body is complete; / it knows pleasure and pain, sleep and dreams, and what was done in the past:

4.4.s:
mṛtaścāhaṃ punarjāto jātaścāhaṃ punarmṛtaḥ ..
nānāyoni sahasrāṇi mayā dṛṣṭāni tāni vai .. 22 ..
4.4.d:
मृतश्चाहं पुनर्जातो जातश्चाहं पुनर्मृतः ॥
नानायोनि सहस्राणि मया दृष्टानि तानि वै ॥ 22 ॥
4.4.m: "I have died and been born again, and born I have died again; / indeed, many thousands of wombs have been seen by me.

4.4.s:
adhunā jātamātro'haṃ prāptasaṃskāra eva ca..
etacchreyaḥ kariṣyāmi yena garbhe na saṃśrayaḥ ..23..
4.4.d:
अधुना जातमात्रोऽहं प्राप्तसंस्कार एव च॥
एतच्छ्रेयः करिष्यामि येन गर्भे न संश्रयः ॥23॥
4.4.m: Now, as soon as I am born and have received the purificatory rites, / I shall perform this good [action] by which there will be no resting in a womb [again]."

4.4.s:
garbhasthaściṃtaye devamahaṃ garbhādviniḥsṛtaḥ ..
adhyeṣye caturo vedānsaṃsāravinivartakān .. 24 ..
4.4.d:
गर्भस्थश्चिंतये देवमहं गर्भाद्विनिःसृतः ॥
अध्येष्ये चतुरो वेदान्संसारविनिवर्तकान् ॥ 24 ॥
4.4.m: Dwelling in the womb, it thinks of God: "Having emerged from the womb, / I shall study the four Vedas that turn one away from saṃsāra."

4.4.s:
evaṃ sa garbhaduḥkhena mahatā paripīḍitaḥ ..
jīvaḥ karmavaśādāste mokṣopāyaṃ viciṃtayan .. 25 ..
4.4.d:
एवं स गर्भदुःखेन महता परिपीडितः ॥
जीवः कर्मवशादास्ते मोक्षोपायं विचिंतयन् ॥ 25 ॥
4.4.m: Thus afflicted by great suffering in the womb, / the soul sits under the sway of karma, contemplating the means of liberation.

4.4.s:
yathā girivarākrāṃtaḥ kaścidduḥkhena tiṣṭhati ..
tathā jarāyuṇā dehī duḥkhe tiṣṭhati ceṣṭitaḥ .. 26 ..
4.4.d:
यथा गिरिवराक्रांतः कश्चिद्दुःखेन तिष्ठति ॥
तथा जरायुणा देही दुःखे तिष्ठति चेष्टितः ॥ 26 ॥
4.4.m: Just as someone oppressed by a great mountain stands in misery, / so the embodied soul, wrapped in the amnion, stays struggling in sorrow.

4.4.s:
patitaḥ sāgare yadvadduḥkhairāste samākula. ..
garbhodakena siktāṃgastathāste vyākulaḥ pumān .. 27 ..
4.4.d:
पतितः सागरे यद्वद्दुःखैरास्ते समाकुल॥।
गर्भोदकेन सिक्तांगस्तथास्ते व्याकुलः पुमान् ॥ 27 ॥
4.4.m: Just as one fallen into the ocean remains overwhelmed with sorrows, / so the person stays agitated, its limbs drenched with amniotic fluid.

4.4.s:
lohakuṃbhe yathā nyastaḥ pacyate kaścidagninā ..
tathā sa pacyate jaṃturgarbhasthaḥ pīḍitodaraḥ .. 28 ..
4.4.d:
लोहकुंभे यथा न्यस्तः पच्यते कश्चिदग्निना ॥
तथा स पच्यते जंतुर्गर्भस्थः पीडितोदरः ॥ 28 ॥
4.4.m: Just as someone placed in an iron cauldron is cooked by fire, / so that creature dwelling in the womb is cooked, its belly squeezed.

4.4.s:
sūcībhiragnivarṇābhirvibhinnasya niraṃtaram ..
yadduḥkhamupajāyeta tadgarbhe'ṣṭaguṇaṃ bhavet .. 29 ..
4.4.d:
सूचीभिरग्निवर्णाभिर्विभिन्नस्य निरंतरम् ॥
यद्दुःखमुपजायेत तद्गर्भेऽष्टगुणं भवेत् ॥ 29 ॥
4.4.m: Whatever pain would arise for one continually pierced by fire-coloured needles, / that [pain] in the womb is eightfold.

4.4.s:
garbhavāsātparo vāsaḥ kaṣṭo naivāsti kutracit ..
dehināṃ duḥkhavadrājansughoro hyatisaṅkaṭaḥ .. 4.4.30 ..
4.4.d:
गर्भवासात्परो वासः कष्टो नैवास्ति कुत्रचित् ॥
देहिनां दुःखवद्राजन्सुघोरो ह्यतिसङ्कटः ॥ 4.4.30 ॥
4.4.m: Nowhere is there a dwelling more miserable than dwelling in a womb; / for embodied beings, O king, it is full of pain, very terrible, and extremely cramped.

4.4.s:
ityetadgarbhaduḥkha hi prāṇināṃ parikīrtitam ..
carasthirāṇāṃ sarveṣātmāmagarbhānurūpataḥ .. 34 ..
4.4.d:
इत्येतद्गर्भदुःख हि प्राणिनां परिकीर्तितम् ॥
चरस्थिराणां सर्वेषात्मामगर्भानुरूपतः ॥ 34 ॥
4.4.m: Thus this suffering in the womb is proclaimed for living beings, / for all moving and unmoving things according to their respective wombs.

4.4.s:
garbhātkoṭiguṇaṃ duḥkhaṃ yoniyaṃtraprapīḍanāt ..
saṃmūrcchitasya jāyeta jāyamānasya dehinaḥ ..32..
4.4.d:
गर्भात्कोटिगुणं दुःखं योनियंत्रप्रपीडनात् ॥
संमूर्च्छितस्य जायेत जायमानस्य देहिनः ॥32॥
4.4.m: Ten million times greater than [the pain of] the womb is the suffering from being crushed in the machine of the vaginal passage, / which occurs for the swooning, embodied being as it is being born,

4.4.s:
śaravatpīḍyamānasya yaṃtreṇeva samaṃtataḥ ..
śirasi tāḍyamānasya pāpamudgarakeṇa ca .. 33 ..
4.4.d:
शरवत्पीड्यमानस्य यंत्रेणेव समंततः ॥
शिरसि ताड्यमानस्य पापमुद्गरकेण च ॥ 33 ॥
4.4.m: squeezed all around like an arrow as if by a press, / and struck on the head with the mallet of evil deeds.

4.4.s:
garbhānniṣkampamāṇasya prabalaiḥ sūtimārutaiḥ ..
jāyate sumahadduḥkhaṃ paritrāṇamaviṃdataḥ .. 34 ..
4.4.d:
गर्भान्निष्कम्पमाणस्य प्रबलैः सूतिमारुतैः ॥
जायते सुमहद्दुःखं परित्राणमविंदतः ॥ 34 ॥
4.4.m: For it, driven out from the womb by the violent winds of birth, / finding no protection, very great suffering arises.

4.4.s:
yaṃtreṇa pīḍitā yadvanniḥsārāḥ syustilekṣavaḥ ..
tathā śarīraṃ niḥsāraṃ yoniyaṃtraprapīḍitam ..35..
4.4.d:
यंत्रेण पीडिता यद्वन्निःसाराः स्युस्तिलेक्षवः ॥
तथा शरीरं निःसारं योनियंत्रप्रपीडितम् ॥35॥
4.4.m: Just as sesame seeds and sugarcanes crushed by a press become devoid of essence, / so the body, crushed by the machine of the vaginal passage, becomes sapless.

4.4.s:
asthimajjātvacāmāṃsasnāyubaṃdhena yaṃtritam ..
raktamāṃsamṛdā yuktaṃ viṇmūtradravalepanam .. 36 ..
4.4.d:
अस्थिमज्जात्वचामांसस्नायुबंधेन यंत्रितम् ॥
रक्तमांसमृदा युक्तं विण्मूत्रद्रवलेपनम् ॥ 36 ॥
4.4.m: It is bound together by the binding of bones, marrow, skin, flesh, and sinews, / mixed with the clay of blood and flesh, smeared with the fluid of feces and urine,

4.4.s:
keśalomatṛṇācchannaṃ rogāyatanamāturam ..
vadanaikamahaddvāraṃ daṃtoṣṭhakavibhūṣitam.. 37 ..
4.4.d:
केशलोमतृणाच्छन्नं रोगायतनमातुरम् ॥
वदनैकमहद्द्वारं दंतोष्ठकविभूषितम्॥ 37 ॥
4.4.m: covered with the grass of hair and body hair, an afflicted abode of diseases, / having the mouth as its one great doorway, adorned with teeth and lips,

4.4.s:
oṣṭhadvayakapāṭaṃ ca dantajihvārgalānvitam ..
nāḍīsvedapravāhaṃ ca kaphapittapariplutam .. 38 ..
4.4.d:
ओष्ठद्वयकपाटं च दन्तजिह्वार्गलान्वितम् ॥
नाडीस्वेदप्रवाहं च कफपित्तपरिप्लुतम् ॥ 38 ॥
4.4.m: with the two lips as doors, fitted with the bolts of teeth and tongue, / with streams of channels and sweat, overflowed with phlegm and bile,

4.4.s:
jarāśokasamāviṣṭaṃ kālacakrānale sthitam ..
kāmakrodhasamākrāṃtaṃ vyasanaiścopamarditam .. 39 ..
4.4.d:
जराशोकसमाविष्टं कालचक्रानले स्थितम् ॥
कामक्रोधसमाक्रांतं व्यसनैश्चोपमर्दितम् ॥ 39 ॥
4.4.m: possessed by old age and grief, situated in the fire of the wheel of time, / overcome by lust and anger, and crushed by misfortunes,

4.4.s:
bhogatṛṣṇāturaṃ mūḍhaṃ rāgadveṣavaśānugam ..
saṃvartitāṃgapratyaṃgaṃ jarāyupariveṣṭitam .. 4.4.40 ..
4.4.d:
भोगतृष्णातुरं मूढं रागद्वेषवशानुगम् ॥
संवर्तितांगप्रत्यंगं जरायुपरिवेष्टितम् ॥ 4.4.40 ॥
4.4.m: afflicted by thirst for enjoyment, deluded, subject to passion and hatred, / its major and minor limbs folded up, wrapped around by the amnion,

4.4.s:
saṃkaṭenāviviktena yonidvāreṇa nirgatam ..
viṇmūtraraktasiktāṃgaṃ patkeśācca samudbhavam .. 41 ..
4.4.d:
संकटेनाविविक्तेन योनिद्वारेण निर्गतम् ॥
विण्मूत्ररक्तसिक्तांगं पत्केशाच्च समुद्भवम् ॥ 41 ॥
4.4.m: emerged through the narrow, unclean vaginal aperture, / its limbs drenched with feces, urine, and blood, and born from hair and cloth.

4.4.s:
iti dehagṛhaṃ proktaṃ nityasyānityamā tmanaḥ ..
aviśuddhaṃ viśuddhasya karmabaṃdhavinirmitam .. 42 ..
4.4.d:
इति देहगृहं प्रोक्तं नित्यस्यानित्यमा त्मनः ॥
अविशुद्धं विशुद्धस्य कर्मबंधविनिर्मितम् ॥ 42 ॥
4.4.m: Thus the dwelling of the body is described: impermanent for the eternal self, / impure for the pure, fashioned by the bond of karma.

4.4.s:
śukraśoṇitasaṃyogāddehaḥ saṃjāyate yataḥ ..
nityaṃ viṇmūtrapūrṇaśca tenāyamaśuciḥ smṛtaḥ .. 43 ..
4.4.d:
शुक्रशोणितसंयोगाद्देहः संजायते यतः ॥
नित्यं विण्मूत्रपूर्णश्च तेनायमशुचिः स्मृतः ॥ 43 ॥
4.4.m: Because the body is produced from the union of semen and blood, / and is ever filled with feces and urine, therefore it is called impure.

4.4.s:
yathāṃtarviṣṭhayā pūrṇaḥ śuciḥ syānna bahirghaṭaḥ ..
yatnataḥ śodhyamāno'pi deho'yamaśucistathā .. 44 ..
4.4.d:
यथांतर्विष्ठया पूर्णः शुचिः स्यान्न बहिर्घटः ॥
यत्नतः शोध्यमानोऽपि देहोऽयमशुचिस्तथा ॥ 44 ॥
4.4.m: Just as a pot filled with excrement inside cannot be clean on the outside / even if diligently washed, so too is this body impure.

4.4.s:
saṃprāpyātra pavitrāṇi paṃcaga vyahavīṃṣi ca ..
aśucitvaṃ kṣaṇāccāpi kimanyadvastubiṃdavaḥ .. 45 ..
4.4.d:
संप्राप्यात्र पवित्राणि पंचग व्यहवींषि च ॥
अशुचित्वं क्षणाच्चापि किमन्यद्वस्तुबिंदवः ॥ 45 ॥
4.4.m: Even when pure things and oblations of the five products of the cow reach it, / they turn instantly into impurity; what else needs to be said of drops of other substances?

4.4.s:
dehaḥ saṃśodhyamāno'pi pañcagavyakuśāṃbubhiḥ ..
ghṛṣyamāṇa ivāṃgāro nirmalatvaṃ na gacchati .. 46 ..
4.4.d:
देहः संशोध्यमानोऽपि पञ्चगव्यकुशांबुभिः ॥
घृष्यमाण इवांगारो निर्मलत्वं न गच्छति ॥ 46 ॥
4.4.m: Even when cleansed with the five products of the cow and water with kuśa grass, / the body, like charcoal being rubbed, does not attain purity.

4.4.s:
srotāṃsi yasya satataṃ pravahaṃti gireriva ..
kaphamūtrapurīṣādyaiḥ sa dehaḥ śuddhyate katham .. 47 ..
4.4.d:
स्रोतांसि यस्य सततं प्रवहंति गिरेरिव ॥
कफमूत्रपुरीषाद्यैः स देहः शुद्ध्यते कथम् ॥ 47 ॥
4.4.m: How can that body be purified whose channels constantly flow / with phlegm, urine, feces, and the like, as if from a mountain?

4.4.s:
sarvāśucinidhānasya śarīrasya na vidyate ..
śucirekaḥ pradeśo'pi viṭpūrṇaḥ syaṃdate kila .. 48 ..
4.4.d:
सर्वाशुचिनिधानस्य शरीरस्य न विद्यते ॥
शुचिरेकः प्रदेशोऽपि विट्पूर्णः स्यंदते किल ॥ 48 ॥
4.4.m: In the body, which is a receptacle of all impurities, not even a single place / is pure; filled with excrement, it indeed oozes.

4.4.s:
kāyaḥ sugaṃdhadhūpādyairyatnenāpi tu saṃskṛtaḥ ..
na jahāti svakaṃ bhāvaṃ śvapu cchamiva nāmitam .. 49 ..
4.4.d:
कायः सुगंधधूपाद्यैर्यत्नेनापि तु संस्कृतः ॥
न जहाति स्वकं भावं श्वपु च्छमिव नामितम् ॥ 49 ॥
4.4.m: Though carefully treated with fragrant incense and other perfumes, / the body does not abandon its innate nature, like a dog's tail that has been bent.

4.4.s:
yathā jātyaiva kṛṣṇo hi na śuklaḥ syādupāyataḥ ..
saṃśodhyamānā'pi tathā bhavenmūrtirna nirmalā .. 4.4.50 ..
4.4.d:
यथा जात्यैव कृष्णो हि न शुक्लः स्यादुपायतः ॥
संशोध्यमानाऽपि तथा भवेन्मूर्तिर्न निर्मला ॥ 4.4.50 ॥
4.4.m: Just as what is black by nature cannot be made white by any means, / so too this form, even when cleansed, does not become spotless.

4.4.s:
jighrannapi svadurgaṃdhaṃ paśyannapi malaṃ svakam ..
na virajjati loko'yaṃ pīḍayannapi nāsikām .. 51 ..
4.4.d:
जिघ्रन्नपि स्वदुर्गंधं पश्यन्नपि मलं स्वकम् ॥
न विरज्जति लोकोऽयं पीडयन्नपि नासिकाम् ॥ 51 ॥
4.4.m: Even while smelling its own foul stench and seeing its own filth, / this world does not become detached, even while holding its nose.

4.4.s:
aho mohasya māhātmyaṃ yena vyāmohitaṃ jagat ..
jighranpaśyansvakaṃ doṣaṃ kāyasya na virajyate .. 52 ..
4.4.d:
अहो मोहस्य माहात्म्यं येन व्यामोहितं जगत् ॥
जिघ्रन्पश्यन्स्वकं दोषं कायस्य न विरज्यते ॥ 52 ॥
4.4.m: Ah, the power of delusion by which the world is utterly confounded! / Smelling and seeing its own bodily fault, it does not become dispassionate.

4.4.s:
evametaccharīraṃ hi nisargādaśuci dhruvam ..
tvaṅmātrasāraṃ niḥsāraṃ kadalīsārasaṃnibham ..53..
4.4.d:
एवमेतच्छरीरं हि निसर्गादशुचि ध्रुवम् ॥
त्वङ्मात्रसारं निःसारं कदलीसारसंनिभम् ॥53॥
4.4.m: Thus this body is surely impure by its very nature, / having its essence in the skin alone, devoid of substance, resembling the pith of a plantain tree.

4.4.s:
garbhasthasya smṛtiryāsītsā jātasya praṇaśyati ..
saṃmūrcchitasya duḥkhena yoniyaṃtraprapīḍanāt .. 54 ..
4.4.d:
गर्भस्थस्य स्मृतिर्यासीत्सा जातस्य प्रणश्यति ॥
संमूर्च्छितस्य दुःखेन योनियंत्रप्रपीडनात् ॥ 54 ॥
4.4.m: The memory that one had while in the womb perishes when one is born, / stupefied by pain from the crushing in the press of the womb.

4.4.s:
bāhyena vāyunā cāsya mohasaṃjñena dehinaḥ..
spṛṣṭamātreṇa ghoreṇa jvaraḥ samupajāyate .. 55 ..
4.4.d:
बाह्येन वायुना चास्य मोहसंज्ञेन देहिनः॥
स्पृष्टमात्रेण घोरेण ज्वरः समुपजायते ॥ 55 ॥
4.4.m: And as soon as this embodied being is touched by the terrible external wind / called delusion, a fever arises.

4.4.s:
tena jvareṇa mahatā mahāmohaḥ prajāyate ..
saṃmūḍhasya smṛtibhraṃśaḥ śīghraṃ saṃjāyate punaḥ .. 56 ..
4.4.d:
तेन ज्वरेण महता महामोहः प्रजायते ॥
संमूढस्य स्मृतिभ्रंशः शीघ्रं संजायते पुनः ॥ 56 ॥
4.4.m: From that great fever, great delusion arises; / and for one who is confounded, loss of memory swiftly occurs again.

4.4.s:
smṛtibhraṃśāttu tasyeha pūrvakarmavaśena ca ..
ratiḥ saṃjāyate tūrṇaṃ jaṃtostatraiva janmani .. 57 ..
4.4.d:
स्मृतिभ्रंशात्तु तस्येह पूर्वकर्मवशेन च ॥
रतिः संजायते तूर्णं जंतोस्तत्रैव जन्मनि ॥ 57 ॥
4.4.m: From the loss of memory and under the influence of past deeds, / attachment swiftly arises for the creature right in that birth.

4.4.s:
rakto mūḍhasya loko'yamakārye saṃpravartate ..
na cātmānaṃ vijānāti na paraṃ vindate ca saḥ .. 58 ..
4.4.d:
रक्तो मूढस्य लोकोऽयमकार्ये संप्रवर्तते ॥
न चात्मानं विजानाति न परं विन्दते च सः ॥ 58 ॥
4.4.m: Attached and bewildered, this world engages in what ought not to be done; / it knows neither itself nor attains the supreme.

4.4.s:
na śrūyate paraṃ śreyaḥ sati cakṣuṣi nekṣate ..
same pathi śanairgacchanskhalatīva padepade .. 59 ..
4.4.d:
न श्रूयते परं श्रेयः सति चक्षुषि नेक्षते ॥
समे पथि शनैर्गच्छन्स्खलतीव पदेपदे ॥ 59 ॥
4.4.m: It does not hear the highest good; though having eyes, it does not see; / walking slowly even on an even path, it seems to stumble at every step.

4.4.s:
satyāṃ buddhau na jānāti bodhyamāno budhairapi ..
saṃsāre kliśyate tena rāgalobhavaśānugaḥ .. 4.4.60 ..
4.4.d:
सत्यां बुद्धौ न जानाति बोध्यमानो बुधैरपि ॥
संसारे क्लिश्यते तेन रागलोभवशानुगः ॥ 4.4.60 ॥
4.4.m: Though having intellect, it does not understand even when instructed by the wise; / therefore, subject to passion and greed, it suffers in saṃsāra.

4.4.s:
garbhasmṛterabhāvena śāstramuktaṃ maharṣibhiḥ ..
tadduḥkhamathanārthāya svargamokṣaprasādhakam .. 61 ..
4.4.d:
गर्भस्मृतेरभावेन शास्त्रमुक्तं महर्षिभिः ॥
तद्दुःखमथनार्थाय स्वर्गमोक्षप्रसाधकम् ॥ 61 ॥
4.4.m: Because of the absence of the memory of the womb, scripture was spoken by the great sages / to crush that suffering and to accomplish heaven and liberation.

4.4.s:
ye saṃtyasminpare jñāne sarvakāmārthasādhake ..
na kurvaṃtyātmanaḥ śreyastadatra mahadbhutam .. 62 ..
4.4.d:
ये संत्यस्मिन्परे ज्ञाने सर्वकामार्थसाधके ॥
न कुर्वंत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्तदत्र महद्भुतम् ॥ 62 ॥
4.4.m: When this supreme knowledge that accomplishes all desires and ends exists, / that people do not bring about their own welfare is a great wonder here.

4.4.s:
avyakteṃdriyavṛttitvādbālye duḥkhaṃ mahatpunaḥ ..
icchannapi na śaknoti kartuṃ vaktuṃ ca satkriyām .. 63 ..
4.4.d:
अव्यक्तेंद्रियवृत्तित्वाद्बाल्ये दुःखं महत्पुनः ॥
इच्छन्नपि न शक्नोति कर्तुं वक्तुं च सत्क्रियाम् ॥ 63 ॥
4.4.m: Moreover, because the functions of the sense-organs are unmanifest, there is great suffering in childhood; / even wishing to do or speak a proper act, one is not able.

4.4.s:
daṃtotthāne mahadduḥkhaṃ maulena vyādhinā tathā ..
bālarogaiśca vividhaiḥ pīḍā bālagrahairapi .. 64 ..
4.4.d:
दंतोत्थाने महद्दुःखं मौलेन व्याधिना तथा ॥
बालरोगैश्च विविधैः पीडा बालग्रहैरपि ॥ 64 ॥
4.4.m: There is great pain when teeth erupt, as well as from innate diseases, / from various childhood illnesses, and affliction by childhood seizures.

4.4.s:
tṛḍbubhukṣāparītāṃgaḥ kaścittiṣṭhati rāraṭan ..
viṇmūtrabhakṣaṇamapi mohādbālaḥ samācaret .. 65 ..
4.4.d:
तृड्बुभुक्षापरीतांगः कश्चित्तिष्ठति रारटन् ॥
विण्मूत्रभक्षणमपि मोहाद्बालः समाचरेत् ॥ 65 ॥
4.4.m: With limbs overcome by thirst and hunger, someone sits wailing; / out of delusion, a child may even eat feces and urine.

4.4.s:
kaumāre karṇavedhena mātāpitrośca tāḍanāt ..
akṣarādhyayanātpuṃsāṃ duḥkhaṃ syādguruśāsanāt .. 66 ..
4.4.d:
कौमारे कर्णवेधेन मातापित्रोश्च ताडनात् ॥
अक्षराध्ययनात्पुंसां दुःखं स्याद्गुरुशासनात् ॥ 66 ॥
4.4.m: In boyhood there is suffering from the piercing of the ears, from beatings by mother and father, / from studying letters, and from the teacher's discipline.

4.4.s:
prasanneṃdriyavṛttiśca kāmarāgaprapīḍanāt ..
rogoddhatasya satataṃ kutaḥ saukhyaṃ ca yauvane .. 67 ..
4.4.d:
प्रसन्नेंद्रियवृत्तिश्च कामरागप्रपीडनात् ॥
रोगोद्धतस्य सततं कुतः सौख्यं च यौवने ॥ 67 ॥
4.4.m: And in youth, when the functions of the sense-organs are active, where is happiness / for one constantly afflicted by lust and passion and ravaged by illness?

4.4.s:
īrṣyayā ca mahadduḥkhaṃ mohādraktasya jāyate ..
netrasya kupitasyaiva rāgo duḥkhāya kevalam ..68..
4.4.d:
ईर्ष्यया च महद्दुःखं मोहाद्रक्तस्य जायते ॥
नेत्रस्य कुपितस्यैव रागो दुःखाय केवलम् ॥68॥
4.4.m: Great suffering arises out of envy for one attached through delusion; / just as for an inflamed eye, passion produces only pain.

4.4.s:
na rātrau viṃdate nidrāṃ kopāgniparipīḍitaḥ ..
divā vāpi kutaḥ saukhyamarthopārjanaciṃtayā .. 69 ..
4.4.d:
न रात्रौ विंदते निद्रां कोपाग्निपरिपीडितः ॥
दिवा वापि कुतः सौख्यमर्थोपार्जनचिंतया ॥ 69 ॥
4.4.m: Afflicted by the fire of anger, he finds no sleep at night; / or during the day, where is happiness amidst anxiety over acquiring wealth?

4.4.s:
strīṣvāyāsitadehasya ye puṃsaḥ śukrabiṃdavaḥ ..
na te sukhāya maṃtavyāḥ svedajā iva biṃdavaḥ .. 4.4.70 ..
4.4.d:
स्त्रीष्वायासितदेहस्य ये पुंसः शुक्रबिंदवः ॥
न ते सुखाय मंतव्याः स्वेदजा इव बिंदवः ॥ 4.4.70 ॥
4.4.m: The drops of semen of a man whose body is exhausted over women / should not be considered conducive to pleasure, just like drops born of sweat.

4.4.s:
krimibhistudyamānasya kuṣṭhinaḥ kāminastathā ..
kaṇḍūyanāgnitāpena yadbhavetstrīṣu taddhi tat .. .. 71 ..
4.4.d:
क्रिमिभिस्तुद्यमानस्य कुष्ठिनः कामिनस्तथा ॥
कण्डूयनाग्नितापेन यद्भवेत्स्त्रीषु तद्धि तत् ॥ ॥ 71 ॥
4.4.m: Whatever happens with women is just like that of a lustful leper / bitten by worms, through scratching and the heat of fire.

4.4.s:
yādṛśaṃ viṃdate saukhyaṃ gaṃḍānvayavinirgame ..
tādṛśaṃ strīṣu maṃtavyaṃ nādhikaṃ tāsu vidyate ..72..
4.4.d:
यादृशं विंदते सौख्यं गंडान्वयविनिर्गमे ॥
तादृशं स्त्रीषु मंतव्यं नाधिकं तासु विद्यते ॥72॥
4.4.m: Such happiness as one finds when the core of a boil comes out, / such is to be understood in the case of women; there is nothing more in them.

4.4.s:
gaṃḍasya vedanā yadvatsphuṭitasya nivartate ..
tadvatstrīṣvapi maṃtavyaṃ na saukhyaṃ paramārthataḥ .. 73 ..
4.4.d:
गंडस्य वेदना यद्वत्स्फुटितस्य निवर्तते ॥
तद्वत्स्त्रीष्वपि मंतव्यं न सौख्यं परमार्थतः ॥ 73 ॥
4.4.m: Just as the pain of a boil ceases when it bursts, / so it should be understood in the case of women; in absolute truth there is no pleasure.

4.4.s:
viṇmūtrasya samutsargātsukhaṃ bhavati yādṛśam ..
tādṛśaṃ teṣu vijñeyaṃ mūḍhaiḥ kalpitamanyathā .. ..74..
4.4.d:
विण्मूत्रस्य समुत्सर्गात्सुखं भवति यादृशम् ॥
तादृशं तेषु विज्ञेयं मूढैः कल्पितमन्यथा ॥ ॥74॥
4.4.m: Such pleasure as comes from discharging feces and urine, / such is to be known in them; it has been imagined otherwise by fools.

4.4.s:
nārīṣvaśucibhūtāsu sarvadoṣāśrayāsu ca ..
nāṇumātrakamapyevaṃ sukhamasti vicārataḥ ..75..
4.4.d:
नारीष्वशुचिभूतासु सर्वदोषाश्रयासु च ॥
नाणुमात्रकमप्येवं सुखमस्ति विचारतः ॥75॥
4.4.m: In women who are impure and the abode of all faults, / upon reflection there is not even an atom of pleasure.

4.4.s:
sanmānamapamānena viyogena susaṃgamaḥ ..
yauvanaṃ jarayā grastaṃ kiṃ saukhyamanupadravam .. 76 ..
4.4.d:
सन्मानमपमानेन वियोगेन सुसंगमः ॥
यौवनं जरया ग्रस्तं किं सौख्यमनुपद्रवम् ॥ 76 ॥
4.4.m: Respect is seized by insult, good company by separation, / youth by old age; what happiness is free from calamity?

4.4.s:
valīpalitakhālityaiḥ śithilīkṛtavigraham ..
sarvakriyāsvaśaktaṃ ca jarayā jarjarīkṛtam .. 77 ..
4.4.d:
वलीपलितखालित्यैः शिथिलीकृतविग्रहम् ॥
सर्वक्रियास्वशक्तं च जरया जर्जरीकृतम् ॥ 77 ॥
4.4.m: Its body slackened by wrinkles, grey hair, and baldness, / incapable of all actions, shattered by old age—

4.4.s:
strīpuṃsayornnavaṃ rūpaṃ tadānyonyaṃ priyaṃ purā ..
tadeva jarayā grastamubhayorapi na priyam ..78..
4.4.d:
स्त्रीपुंसयोर्न्नवं रूपं तदान्योन्यं प्रियं पुरा ॥
तदेव जरया ग्रस्तमुभयोरपि न प्रियम् ॥78॥
4.4.m: the fresh beauty of a woman and a man, which was formerly dear to each other, / when seized by old age, is no longer dear to either of them.

4.4.s:
apūrvavatsvamātmānaṃ jarayā parivartitaḥ ..
yaḥ paśyannapi rajyeta ko'nyastasmādacetanaḥ .. 79 ..
4.4.d:
अपूर्ववत्स्वमात्मानं जरया परिवर्तितः ॥
यः पश्यन्नपि रज्येत कोऽन्यस्तस्मादचेतनः ॥ 79 ॥
4.4.m: Transformed by old age as if into someone unprecedented, / who could be more senseless than one who, seeing himself, is still attached?

4.4.s:
jarābhibhūtaḥ puruṣaḥ patnīputrādibāṃdhavaiḥ ..
aśaktatvāddurācārairbhṛtyaiśca paribhūyate .. 4.4.80 ..
4.4.d:
जराभिभूतः पुरुषः पत्नीपुत्रादिबांधवैः ॥
अशक्तत्वाद्दुराचारैर्भृत्यैश्च परिभूयते ॥ 4.4.80 ॥
4.4.m: Overcome by old age, a man is treated with contempt / by his wife, sons, and relatives, and by ill-behaved servants on account of his helplessness.

4.4.s:
dharmamarthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca mokṣaṃ ca na jarī yataḥ ..
śaktaḥ sādhayituṃ tasmāccharīramidamātmanaḥ .. 81 ..
4.4.d:
धर्ममर्थं च कामं च मोक्षं च न जरी यतः ॥
शक्तः साधयितुं तस्माच्छरीरमिदमात्मनः ॥ 81 ॥
4.4.m: Since an aged person is unable to accomplish dharma, / wealth, pleasure, or liberation, therefore this body of oneself [is useless].

4.4.s:
vātapittakaphādīnāṃ vaiṣamyaṃ vyādhirucyate ..
tasmādvyādhimayaṃ jñeyaṃ śarīramidamātmanaḥ .. 82 ..
4.4.d:
वातपित्तकफादीनां वैषम्यं व्याधिरुच्यते ॥
तस्माद्व्याधिमयं ज्ञेयं शरीरमिदमात्मनः ॥ 82 ॥
4.4.m: The imbalance of wind, bile, phlegm, and the rest is called disease; / therefore this body of oneself should be known as consisting of disease.

4.4.s:
vātādyavyatiriktatvādvyādhīnāṃ pañjarasya ca ..
rogairnānāvidhairyāni dehaduḥkhānyanekadhā ..
tāni ca svātmavedyāni kimanyatkathayāmyaham .. 83 ..
4.4.d:
वाताद्यव्यतिरिक्तत्वाद्व्याधीनां पञ्जरस्य च ॥
रोगैर्नानाविधैर्यानि देहदुःखान्यनेकधा ॥
तानि च स्वात्मवेद्यानि किमन्यत्कथयाम्यहम् ॥ 83 ॥
4.4.m: Since it is not distinct from wind and the rest, and is a cage of diseases, / the various bodily pains caused by diverse illnesses / can only be known by oneself; what else can I say?

4.4.s:
ekottaraṃ mṛtyuśatamasmindehe pratiṣṭhitam ..
tatraikaḥ kālasaṃyuktaḥ śeṣāścāgantavaḥ smṛtāḥ .. 84 ..
4.4.d:
एकोत्तरं मृत्युशतमस्मिन्देहे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
तत्रैकः कालसंयुक्तः शेषाश्चागन्तवः स्मृताः ॥ 84 ॥
4.4.m: One hundred and one forms of death are established in this body; / among them, one is linked to time, and the rest are considered accidental.

4.4.s:
ye tvihāgaṃtavaḥ proktāste praśāmyaṃti bheṣajaiḥ ..
japahomapradānaiśca kālamṛtyurna śāmyati .. 85 ..
4.4.d:
ये त्विहागंतवः प्रोक्तास्ते प्रशाम्यंति भेषजैः ॥
जपहोमप्रदानैश्च कालमृत्युर्न शाम्यति ॥ 85 ॥
4.4.m: Those that are called accidental here are pacified by medicines, / by silent recitation, burnt oblations, and gifts; but timely death is not pacified.

4.4.s:
yadi cāpi na mṛtyuḥ syādviṣamadyādaśaṃkitaḥ ..
na saṃti puruṣe tasmādapamṛtyuvibhītayaḥ .. 86 ..
4.4.d:
यदि चापि न मृत्युः स्याद्विषमद्यादशंकितः ॥
न संति पुरुषे तस्मादपमृत्युविभीतयः ॥ 86 ॥
4.4.m: And if there were no death, one would drink poison without hesitation; / therefore, there are no fears of premature death in a man [if it were not so].

4.4.s:
vividhā vyādhayaḥ śastraṃ sarpādyāḥ prāṇinastathā ..
viṣāṇi jaṃgamādyāni mṛtyordvārāṇi dehinām .. .. 87 ..
4.4.d:
विविधा व्याधयः शस्त्रं सर्पाद्याः प्राणिनस्तथा ॥
विषाणि जंगमाद्यानि मृत्योर्द्वाराणि देहिनाम् ॥ ॥ 87 ॥
4.4.m: Various diseases, weapons, creatures such as snakes, / and mobile [and immobile] poisons are the gateways of death for embodied beings.

4.4.s:
pīḍitaṃ sarvarogādyairapi dhanvantariḥ svayam ..
svasthīkartuṃ na śaknoti prāptamṛtyuṃ ca dehinam .. 88 ..
4.4.d:
पीडितं सर्वरोगाद्यैरपि धन्वन्तरिः स्वयम् ॥
स्वस्थीकर्तुं न शक्नोति प्राप्तमृत्युं च देहिनम् ॥ 88 ॥
4.4.m: Even Dhanvantari himself cannot restore to health / an embodied being who is afflicted by all manner of diseases and has reached [his appointed] death.

4.4.s:
nauṣadhaṃ na tapo dānaṃ na maṃtrā na ca bāṃdhavāḥ ..
śaknuvaṃti paritrātuṃ naraṃ kālena pīḍitam .. 89 ..
4.4.d:
नौषधं न तपो दानं न मंत्रा न च बांधवाः ॥
शक्नुवंति परित्रातुं नरं कालेन पीडितम् ॥ 89 ॥
4.4.m: Neither medicine, nor asceticism, nor gifts, nor mantras, nor kinsmen / can save a man afflicted by time.

4.4.s:
rasāyanatapojapyairyogasiddhairmahātmabhiḥ ..
kālamṛtyurapi prājñaistīryate nālasairnnaraiḥ .. 4.4.90 ..
4.4.d:
रसायनतपोजप्यैर्योगसिद्धैर्महात्मभिः ॥
कालमृत्युरपि प्राज्ञैस्तीर्यते नालसैर्न्नरैः ॥ 4.4.90 ॥
4.4.m: Through elixirs, asceticism, and recitation, great-souled men perfected in yoga / and wise men cross over even death by time, but not lazy men.

4.4.s:
nāsti mṛtyusamaṃ duḥkhaṃ nāsti mṛtyusamaṃ bhayam ..
nāsti mṛtyusamastrāsaḥ sarveṣāmeva dehinām .. 91 ..
4.4.d:
नास्ति मृत्युसमं दुःखं नास्ति मृत्युसमं भयम् ॥
नास्ति मृत्युसमस्त्रासः सर्वेषामेव देहिनाम् ॥ 91 ॥
4.4.m: There is no pain equal to death, there is no fear equal to death, / there is no terror equal to death for all embodied beings.

4.4.s:
sadbhāryāputramitrāṇi rājyaiśvaryadha nāni ca ..
abaddhāni ca vairāṇi mṛtyuḥ sarvāṇi kṛntati .. 92 ..
4.4.d:
सद्भार्यापुत्रमित्राणि राज्यैश्वर्यध नानि च ॥
अबद्धानि च वैराणि मृत्युः सर्वाणि कृन्तति ॥ 92 ॥
4.4.m: A good wife, sons, friends, kingdom, lordship, and wealth, / and unavenged enmities—death cuts off all of these.

4.4.s:
he janāḥ kiṃ na paśyadhvaṃ sahasrasyāpi madhyataḥ ..
janāḥ śatāyuṣaḥ pañca bhavaṃti na bhavaṃti ca .. 93 ..
4.4.d:
हे जनाः किं न पश्यध्वं सहस्रस्यापि मध्यतः ॥
जनाः शतायुषः पञ्च भवंति न भवंति च ॥ 93 ॥
4.4.m: O people, do you not see that even among a thousand, / people who live a hundred years are five, or are not [even five]?

4.4.s:
aśītikā vipadyante kecitsaptatikā narāḥ ..
paramāyuṣaṃ sthitaṃ ṣaṣṭistaccaivāniścitaṃ punaḥ .. 94 ..
4.4.d:
अशीतिका विपद्यन्ते केचित्सप्ततिका नराः ॥
परमायुषं स्थितं षष्टिस्तच्चैवानिश्चितं पुनः ॥ 94 ॥
4.4.m: Some men perish at eighty, some at seventy; / the maximum life span stands at sixty, and even that is uncertain.

4.4.s:
yasya yāvadbhavedāyurdehināṃ pūrvakarmabhiḥ ..
tasyārddhamāyuṣo rātrirharate mṛtyurūpiṇī .. 95 ..
4.4.d:
यस्य यावद्भवेदायुर्देहिनां पूर्वकर्मभिः ॥
तस्यार्द्धमायुषो रात्रिर्हरते मृत्युरूपिणी ॥ 95 ॥
4.4.m: Whatever life span an embodied being has through his past actions, / half of that life span night takes away, in the form of death.

4.4.s:
bālabhāvena mohena vārddhakye jarayā tathā ..
varṣāṇāṃ viṃśatiryāṃti dharmakāmārthavarjitā .. 96 ..
4.4.d:
बालभावेन मोहेन वार्द्धक्ये जरया तथा ॥
वर्षाणां विंशतिर्यांति धर्मकामार्थवर्जिता ॥ 96 ॥
4.4.m: Through childhood and ignorance, and likewise through old age and infirmity, / twenty years pass away, devoid of righteousness, desire, and wealth.

4.4.s:
āgaṃtukerbhayaiḥ puṃsāṃ vyādhiśokairanekadhā ..
bhakṣyate'rddhaṃ ca tatrāpi yaccheṣaṃ tacca jīvati .. 97 ..
4.4.d:
आगंतुकेर्भयैः पुंसां व्याधिशोकैरनेकधा ॥
भक्ष्यतेऽर्द्धं च तत्रापि यच्छेषं तच्च जीवति ॥ 97 ॥
4.4.m: By accidental fears of men, and by many kinds of disease and grief, / half of what remains is consumed; and that which is left, one lives.

4.4.s:
jīvitāṃte ca maraṇaṃ mahāghoramavāpnuyāt ..
jāyate janmakoṭīṣu mṛtaḥ karmavaśātpunaḥ .. 98 ..
4.4.d:
जीवितांते च मरणं महाघोरमवाप्नुयात् ॥
जायते जन्मकोटीषु मृतः कर्मवशात्पुनः ॥ 98 ॥
4.4.m: And at the end of life, one meets a most dreadful death; / having died, one is born again through the power of karma in ten million births.

4.4.s:
dehabhedena yaḥ puṃsāṃ viyogaḥ karmasaṃkṣayāt ..
maraṇaṃ tadvinirdiṣṭaṃ nānyathā paramārthataḥ .. 99 ..
4.4.d:
देहभेदेन यः पुंसां वियोगः कर्मसंक्षयात् ॥
मरणं तद्विनिर्दिष्टं नान्यथा परमार्थतः ॥ 99 ॥
4.4.m: The separation of men through the breaking of the body when karma is exhausted— / that is declared to be death; in absolute reality, it is not otherwise.

4.4.s:
mahātapapraviṣṭasya cchidyamāneṣu marmasu ..
yadduḥkhaṃ maraṇe jaṃtorna tasyehopamā kvacit .. 4.4.100 ..
4.4.d:
महातपप्रविष्टस्य च्छिद्यमानेषु मर्मसु ॥
यद्दुःखं मरणे जंतोर्न तस्येहोपमा क्वचित् ॥ 4.4.100 ॥
4.4.m: For one who has entered upon great fever, when the vital organs are severed, / whatever pain there is at the death of a creature has no comparison in this world.

4.4.s:
hā tāta mātaḥ kāṃteti rudannevaṃ hi duḥkhitaḥ ..
maṃḍūka iva sarpeṇa grasyate mṛtyunā janaḥ .. 101 ..
4.4.d:
हा तात मातः कांतेति रुदन्नेवं हि दुःखितः ॥
मंडूक इव सर्पेण ग्रस्यते मृत्युना जनः ॥ 101 ॥
4.4.m: Crying thus in distress, 'Alas, father! mother! beloved!', / a person is swallowed by death like a frog by a snake.

4.4.s:
bāṃdhavaiḥ saṃpariṣvaktaḥ priyaiḥ sa parivāritaḥ ..
niḥśvasandīrghamuṣṇaṃ ca mukhena pariśuṣyati .. 102 ..
4.4.d:
बांधवैः संपरिष्वक्तः प्रियैः स परिवारितः ॥
निःश्वसन्दीर्घमुष्णं च मुखेन परिशुष्यति ॥ 102 ॥
4.4.m: Embraced by kinsmen, surrounded by loved ones, / sighing long and hot breaths, he dries up through his mouth.

4.4.s:
krandate caiva khaṭvāyāṃ parivartanmuhurmuhuḥ ..
saṃmūḍhaḥ kṣipate'tyarthaṃ hastapādāvitastataḥ ..103..
4.4.d:
क्रन्दते चैव खट्वायां परिवर्तन्मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
संमूढः क्षिपतेऽत्यर्थं हस्तपादावितस्ततः ॥103॥
4.4.m: And he cries out on the bed, tossing and turning again and again; / bewildered, he flings his hands and feet violently this way and that.

4.4.s:
khaṭvāto kāṃkṣate bhūmiṃ bhūmeḥ khaṭvāṃ punarmahīm ..
vivaśastyaktalajjaśca mūtraviṣṭhānulepitaḥ .. 104 ..
4.4.d:
खट्वातो कांक्षते भूमिं भूमेः खट्वां पुनर्महीम् ॥
विवशस्त्यक्तलज्जश्च मूत्रविष्ठानुलेपितः ॥ 104 ॥
4.4.m: From the bed he desires the ground, from the ground the bed, and again the earth; / helpless, shorn of shame, and smeared with urine and feces.

4.4.s:
yācamānaśca salilaṃ śuṣkakaṇṭhoṣṭhatālukaḥ ..
ciṃtayānaśca vittāni kasyaitāni mṛte mayi .. 105 ..
4.4.d:
याचमानश्च सलिलं शुष्ककण्ठोष्ठतालुकः ॥
चिंतयानश्च वित्तानि कस्यैतानि मृते मयि ॥ 105 ॥
4.4.m: And begging for water, his throat, lips, and palate parched, / and thinking about his riches: 'Whose will these be when I am dead?'

4.4.s:
pañcāvaṭānkhanyamānaḥ kālapāśena karṣitaḥ ..
mriyate paśyatāmeva janānāṃ ghurghurasvanaḥ .. .. 106 ..
4.4.d:
पञ्चावटान्खन्यमानः कालपाशेन कर्षितः ॥
म्रियते पश्यतामेव जनानां घुर्घुरस्वनः ॥ ॥ 106 ॥
4.4.m: Punctured in his five cavities, dragged by the noose of time, / he dies while people are actually watching, rattling in his throat.

4.4.s:
jīvastṛṇajalaukeva dehāddehaṃ viśetkramāt ..
saṃprāpyottarakālaṃ hi dehaṃ tyajati paurvakam .. 107 ..
4.4.d:
जीवस्तृणजलौकेव देहाद्देहं विशेत्क्रमात् ॥
संप्राप्योत्तरकालं हि देहं त्यजति पौर्वकम् ॥ 107 ॥
4.4.m: Just as a caterpillar [moves from leaf to leaf], the soul enters body after body in succession; / having obtained the next state, it abandons the former body.

4.4.s:
maraṇātprārthanāduḥkhamadhikaṃ hi vive kinaḥ ..
kṣaṇikaṃ maraṇāduḥkhamanaṃtaṃ prārthanākṛtam .. 108 ..
4.4.d:
मरणात्प्रार्थनादुःखमधिकं हि विवे किनः ॥
क्षणिकं मरणादुःखमनंतं प्रार्थनाकृतम् ॥ 108 ॥
4.4.m: Indeed, for a discerning person, the pain of begging is greater than death; / the pain caused by death is momentary, but that caused by begging is endless.

4.4.s:
jagatāṃ patirarthitvādviṣṇurvāmanatāṃ gataḥ ..
adhikaḥ ko'parastasmādyo na yā syati lāghavam .. 109 ..
4.4.d:
जगतां पतिरर्थित्वाद्विष्णुर्वामनतां गतः ॥
अधिकः कोऽपरस्तस्माद्यो न या स्यति लाघवम् ॥ 109 ॥
4.4.m: Through begging, Viṣṇu, the lord of the worlds, became a dwarf; / what other person, greater than him, will not incur humiliation?

4.4.s:
jñātaṃ mayedamadhunā mataṃ bhavati yadguru ..
na paraṃ prārthayedbhūyastṛṣṇā lāghavakāraṇam .. 4.4.110 ..
4.4.d:
ज्ञातं मयेदमधुना मतं भवति यद्गुरु ॥
न परं प्रार्थयेद्भूयस्तृष्णा लाघवकारणम् ॥ 4.4.110 ॥
4.4.m: I have now understood this opinion, which is weighty: / one should never beg another again; craving is the cause of humiliation.

4.4.s:
ādau duḥkhaṃ tathā madhye duḥkhamaṃte ca dāruṇam ..
nisargātsarvabhūtānāmiti duḥkhaparaṃparā .. 111 ..
4.4.d:
आदौ दुःखं तथा मध्ये दुःखमंते च दारुणम् ॥
निसर्गात्सर्वभूतानामिति दुःखपरंपरा ॥ 111 ॥
4.4.m: Pain in the beginning, pain likewise in the middle, and terrible pain in the end— / by nature, there is such a succession of pain for all beings.

4.4.s:
vartamānānyatītāni duḥkhānyetāni yāni tu ..
narā na bhāvayaṃtyajñā na virajyati tena te .. 112 ..
4.4.d:
वर्तमानान्यतीतानि दुःखान्येतानि यानि तु ॥
नरा न भावयंत्यज्ञा न विरज्यति तेन ते ॥ 112 ॥
4.4.m: These pains that are present and past, however, / ignorant men do not contemplate; therefore, they do not turn away [from worldly life].

4.4.s:
atyāhārānmahadduḥkhamanāhārānmahattamam ..
tulitaṃ jīvitaṃ kaṣṭaṃ manye'pyevaṃ kutaḥ sukham .. 113 ..
4.4.d:
अत्याहारान्महद्दुःखमनाहारान्महत्तमम् ॥
तुलितं जीवितं कष्टं मन्येऽप्येवं कुतः सुखम् ॥ 113 ॥
4.4.m: From overeating comes great pain; from fasting comes the greatest pain; / weighed [together], life is miserable; how can there be happiness even thus?

4.4.s:
bubhukṣā sarvarogāṇāṃ vyādhiḥ śreṣṭhatamaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
sa cānnauṣadhilepena kṣaṇamātraṃ praśāmyati .. 114 ..
4.4.d:
बुभुक्षा सर्वरोगाणां व्याधिः श्रेष्ठतमः स्मृतः ॥
स चान्नौषधिलेपेन क्षणमात्रं प्रशाम्यति ॥ 114 ॥
4.4.m: Hunger is considered the foremost disease among all diseases; / and it is calmed only for a moment by the balm of food as medicine.

4.4.s:
kṣudvyādhivedanātulyā niḥśeṣabalakartanī ..
tayābhibhūto mriyate yathānyairvyādhibhirna hi ..1 15..
4.4.d:
क्षुद्व्याधिवेदनातुल्या निःशेषबलकर्तनी ॥
तयाभिभूतो म्रियते यथान्यैर्व्याधिभिर्न हि ॥1 15॥
4.4.m: The agony of hunger is comparable to a disease that cuts down all strength; / overcome by it, one dies in a way one does not from other diseases.

4.4.s:
tadrasopi hi kāmādvā jihvāgre parivartate ..
tatkṣaṇādvārddhakālena kaṃṭhaṃ prāpya nivartate ..116..
4.4.d:
तद्रसोपि हि कामाद्वा जिह्वाग्रे परिवर्तते ॥
तत्क्षणाद्वार्द्धकालेन कंठं प्राप्य निवर्तते ॥116॥
4.4.m: Even its taste rolls on the tip of the tongue out of desire; / in that instant, having reached the throat, it ceases through the passage of time.

4.4.s:
iti kṣudvyādhitaptānāmannamauṣadhavatsmṛtam ..
na tatsukhāya mantavyaṃ paramārthena paṃḍitaiḥ .. 117 ..
4.4.d:
इति क्षुद्व्याधितप्तानामन्नमौषधवत्स्मृतम् ॥
न तत्सुखाय मन्तव्यं परमार्थेन पंडितैः ॥ 117 ॥
4.4.m: Thus, food is considered medicine for those tormented by the disease of hunger; / it should not be thought to exist for pleasure by the wise in absolute reality.

4.4.s:
mṛtopamo yaścekṣeta sarvakāryavivarjitaḥ ..
tatrāpi ca kutaḥ saukhyaṃ tamasācchāditātmanaḥ .. 118 ..
4.4.d:
मृतोपमो यश्चेक्षेत सर्वकार्यविवर्जितः ॥
तत्रापि च कुतः सौख्यं तमसाच्छादितात्मनः ॥ 118 ॥
4.4.m: And if one should look on like a dead person, free from all activity, / even there, how can there be happiness for one whose self is covered by darkness?

4.4.s:
prabodhe'pi kutaḥ saukhyaṃ kāryairupahatātmanaḥ ..
kṛṣigorakṣavāṇijyasevādhvādipariśramaiḥ ..119..
4.4.d:
प्रबोधेऽपि कुतः सौख्यं कार्यैरुपहतात्मनः ॥
कृषिगोरक्षवाणिज्यसेवाध्वादिपरिश्रमैः ॥119॥
4.4.m: Even in waking, how can there be happiness for one whose mind is afflicted by duties, / by the fatigues of agriculture, cattle rearing, trade, service, traveling on the road, and the like?

4.4.s:
prātarmūtrapurīṣābhyāṃ madhyāhne tu bubhukṣayā ..
tṛptāḥ kāmena bādhyante jaṃtavo'pi vinidrayā .. 4.4.120 ..
4.4.d:
प्रातर्मूत्रपुरीषाभ्यां मध्याह्ने तु बुभुक्षया ॥
तृप्ताः कामेन बाध्यन्ते जंतवोऽपि विनिद्रया ॥ 4.4.120 ॥
4.4.m: In the morning by urine and feces, at midday by hunger, / satisfied, creatures are tormented by desire, and even by sleeplessness.

4.4.s:
arthasyopārjane duḥkhamarjitasyāpi rakṣaṇe ..
āye duḥkhaṃ vyaye duḥkhamarthebhyaśca kutaḥ sukham .. 121 ..
4.4.d:
अर्थस्योपार्जने दुःखमर्जितस्यापि रक्षणे ॥
आये दुःखं व्यये दुःखमर्थेभ्यश्च कुतः सुखम् ॥ 121 ॥
4.4.m: There is pain in acquiring wealth, and pain in protecting what has been acquired; / there is pain in its income and pain in its expenditure; how can there be happiness from riches?

4.4.s:
caurebhyaḥ salilādagneḥ svajanātpārthivādapi ..
bhayamarthavatāṃ nityaṃ mṛtyoḥ prāṇabhṛtā miva .. 122 ..
4.4.d:
चौरेभ्यः सलिलादग्नेः स्वजनात्पार्थिवादपि ॥
भयमर्थवतां नित्यं मृत्योः प्राणभृता मिव ॥ 122 ॥
4.4.m: From thieves, from water, from fire, from relatives, and even from the king, / there is constant fear for the wealthy, as from death for living beings.

4.4.s:
khe yātaṃ pakṣibhirmāṃsaṃ bhakṣyate śvāpadairbhuvi ..
jale ca bhakṣyate matsyaistathā sarvatra vittavān .. 123 ..
4.4.d:
खे यातं पक्षिभिर्मांसं भक्ष्यते श्वापदैर्भुवि ॥
जले च भक्ष्यते मत्स्यैस्तथा सर्वत्र वित्तवान् ॥ 123 ॥
4.4.m: Flesh flying in the air is eaten by birds, on earth by beasts of prey, / and in water it is eaten by fish; likewise is the wealthy man everywhere.

4.4.s:
vimohayati saṃpatsu tāpayaṃti vipattiṣu ..
khedayaṃtyarjanākāle kadā hyarthāḥ sukhāvahāḥ .. 124 ..
4.4.d:
विमोहयति संपत्सु तापयंति विपत्तिषु ॥
खेदयंत्यर्जनाकाले कदा ह्यर्थाः सुखावहाः ॥ 124 ॥
4.4.m: [Riches] delude in prosperity, torment in adversity, / and cause exhaustion at the time of acquisition; when are riches ever conducive to happiness?

4.4.s:
yathārthapatirudvigno yaśca sarvārthaniḥspṛhaḥ ..
yataścārthapatirduḥkhī sukhī sarvārthaniḥspṛhaḥ .. 125 ..
4.4.d:
यथार्थपतिरुद्विग्नो यश्च सर्वार्थनिःस्पृहः ॥
यतश्चार्थपतिर्दुःखी सुखी सर्वार्थनिःस्पृहः ॥ 125 ॥
4.4.m: Just as the owner of wealth is anxious, so he who is free from desire for all riches [is not]; / because the owner of wealth is miserable, while he who is free from desire for all riches is happy.

4.4.s:
śītena duḥkhaṃ hemaṃte grīṣme tāpena dāruṇam ..
varṣāsu vātavarṣābhyāṃ kāle'pyevaṃ kutaḥ sukham .. 126 ..
4.4.d:
शीतेन दुःखं हेमंते ग्रीष्मे तापेन दारुणम् ॥
वर्षासु वातवर्षाभ्यां कालेऽप्येवं कुतः सुखम् ॥ 126 ॥
4.4.m: There is pain through cold in winter, and terrible [pain] through heat in summer; / in the rains through wind and rain; even in season, how can there be happiness?

4.4.s:
vivāhavistare duḥkhaṃ tadgarbhodvahane punaḥ ..
prasave'patyadoṣaiśca duḥkhaṃ duḥkhādikarmabhiḥ .. 127 ..
4.4.d:
विवाहविस्तरे दुःखं तद्गर्भोद्वहने पुनः ॥
प्रसवेऽपत्यदोषैश्च दुःखं दुःखादिकर्मभिः ॥ 127 ॥
4.4.m: There is pain in the elaborate affair of marriage, and again in carrying the fetus; / in childbirth and through faults of children, there is pain from painful deeds and the like.

4.4.s:
dantākṣiraugaiḥ putrasya hā kaṣṭaṃ kiṃ karomyaham ..
gāvo naṣṭāḥ kṛṣirbhagnā vṛṣāḥ kvāpi palāyitāḥ .. 128 ..
4.4.d:
दन्ताक्षिरौगैः पुत्रस्य हा कष्टं किं करोम्यहम् ॥
गावो नष्टाः कृषिर्भग्ना वृषाः क्वापि पलायिताः ॥ 128 ॥
